recording driver 1078e02, zero.h2h's per-side view 052ea00, the flagged extra rows e5873bb, docs
2c04cd9: zero-core docs/search.md 3.6, az.md 16); this repo: the non-deciding viewer's leak
checks, two `#[doc(hidden)]` engine helpers for them, `tools/root_view.py` (the CPU evidence), this
section. With the settings off a run is the run of before, byte for byte (67.9).

### 67.1 Why

The search determinizes hidden cards from the root player's view (section 10) and, before this,
valued every leaf with the network on `encode(decider)` of the leaf: at a leaf where the opponent
decides, that view **cannot see the root player's hand** and **reads the opponent's sampled hand as
known**. 64.4 measured it at the mulligan: after a kept landless hand the next decider's view gives
the keeper 0.51, the keeper's own view 0.36. Every other leaf of the mirror's searches is the
opponent's. A replay the user flagged (Delver AI 1193650d66c0, delver2 iteration 38, frame 20: seat
1's own upkeep, Brainstorm x2 and Ponder in hand, priority with an empty stack): Pass got 1 visit at Q
0.464 against Brainstorm's 0.655 (root v 0.683) - Pass's one leaf is seat 0's priority, valued from
seat 0's view, blind to seat 1's hand.

### 67.2 The design (zero-core docs/search.md 3.6)

* **Views.** Seat key / run setting `leaf_value_view` (`selfplay_leaf_value_view`,
  `eval_leaf_value_view`): 'mover' (default) or 'root'. With 'root', a leaf of the opponent sends two
  rows in the same batch: its own, `encode(opponent)`, for the **priors** (the opponent's model of the
  game: it cannot see our hand either), and a value-only row `encode(root player)` of the same sampled
  state for the **value and margin** (relative to the root player; backed up as any). The value-only
  row has no options and is flagged `ROW_VALUE` in the batch's `extra` (zero-core's generic flagged
  extra rows: the belief head's stage 2, 66.8, adds its own kind). The evaluator interface is
  unchanged. A leaf of the root player is one row as before.
* **The encoding for a non-decider** already writes the pending decision's options, the list block
  (since 65.10 the graveyard list too) and the decision's option count only for the decider
  (`mine_to_decide`, `encode_context`): a non-deciding viewer sees the decision's kind, its decider and
  its public context (the asking task, the card, the cost being paid), nothing derived from the
  decider's hand. 67.3 checks it.
* **Value-only samples** (`selfplay_view_samples`, `view_sample_target`): a share of the recorded
  decisions also records the real state from the other player's view - `encode(other)`, its
  perspective, no options (no policy loss), z its result. **Target**: q = the other player's **own
  next search's** root value (`next_q`, the default; z when it never searches again), blended with z
  by the run's `value_q` as every sample. Why: between the sample and its next search the other
  player only learns more, so that search's value is an unbiased estimate (up to the search's error)
  of the outcome given what it knows at the sample - the tower property - with less variance than z.
  Its *previous* search's q is stale (it predates the decider's move); the decider's q negated
  (zero-sum) is computed from the decider's information set, the other player's hand sampled and the
  decider's known, so it would teach the other view to ignore its own hand and to know the decider's:
  the bias reversed. `z` alone is offered (`view_sample_target z`).

### 67.3 Leaks: the non-deciding viewer's encoding

`determinize(viewer)` keeps the cards a payment in progress pins (section 10: the payer's mana
sources in hand, the cards a cost may exile from it - Force of Will's blue card), so the existing
check (`determinize_keeps_features_and_legal_actions_for_both_viewers`) cannot see a leak through
them. Two engine helpers for tests (`#[doc(hidden)]`): `Game::resample_unpinned(viewer, rng)`
(determinize's deal of **every** card hidden from the viewer, pins included, nothing else: no reseed,
no observer, the pending decision as it is) and `Game::pinned_for(viewer)`; `determinize`'s deal is
factored out (`deal_hidden`) unchanged (the digests, 67.9).

* `tests/hidden.rs`: `a_non_deciding_viewers_features_ignore_the_deciders_hidden_cards` (60 random cube
  games, 232 worlds, the decider's hand dealt again in 215: the other viewer's features identical);
  `a_non_deciding_viewers_features_ignore_pinned_cards_of_a_payment` (P1 pays for a spell with Simian
  Spirit Guide in hand, then casts Force of Will by its alternative cost: at every decision of both,
  P0's features identical in 24 worlds each with the pinned cards dealt again; 6 decisions with pins).
* `tests/az.rs`: `a_non_deciding_viewers_encoding_ignores_the_deciders_hidden_cards` (the public-state
  gate's positions - cube, Delver mirror, best-of-three, a drafted match, 40 each: 480 worlds, all
  with cards dealt again; with `AZ_SCALE=5` 2,400) and `root_view_leaves_encode_alike_whatever_the_
  deciders_options` - the search's own case: two worlds sampled for the root player at its decision
  (cube positions and the Delver mirror), played on with the same actions while the keys agree; at
  every decision of the other player the root player's encoding is the same in both worlds, **also
  where the other player's options differ** (they follow its sampled hand: different tree nodes, one
  information state of the root player). 314 positions compared, 63 with different options (`AZ_SCALE=5`:
  1,785 and 378). `equal_keys_mean_equal_features` stops where the options differ.
* **The public-state gate** (58.6) already requires every public perturbation to reach the encoding of
  **both** viewers, the non-deciding one included: 131 encoded, 3 deliberate limits, 1 gap for the
  next layout (main's). Found on the way, not caused here: at `AZ_SCALE=5` the gate reports 3 findings
  (can't block 4 of 1,047, can't be blocked 6 of 1,047, can't be countered 2 of 249 perturbations
  without an encoding change, both viewers alike) - main 0f98448 reports the same 3 at that scale.

### 67.4 Distribution shift: calibration on CPU self-play

`python tools/root_view.py selfplay --model <copy of delver2 iteration 41> --games 192 --conc 96
--config <delver2's config>`: the line's self-play seat (64 / 16 simulations, p_full 0.25, minor 4,
cq 0.3, mover-view leaves as the line plays), every decision's value-only sample recorded (26,884
samples: 13,442 decisions and 13,442 other views; 1,006 s, 1,476 leaves/s on 4 + 4 threads). `calib`:
the network's P(win) for each row's player against the outcome.

| rows | n | log loss (constant 0.681) | Brier | ECE (5 bins) | mean prediction / won |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decisions (the decider's view: trained) | 13,442 | 0.358 | 0.117 | 0.025 | 0.568 / 0.578 |
| value-only (the other view: never trained) | 13,442 | 0.367 | 0.120 | 0.014 | 0.431 / 0.422 |

* **The shift is small**: the value head, never shown a non-decider's encoding, is about as calibrated
  on it as on the decider's.
* **The views disagree, without a bias**: the decider's own P(win) minus 1 - the other view's at the
  same state: -0.002 on average (13,442 pairs), 0.077 mean absolute, 0.21 at the 90th percentile.
  Neither view is systematically optimistic in real positions.

`finetune` (the 192 games split by game, 48 held out; 300 steps of 256, lr 1e-4, value_q 0.6; 90 s on
CPU), the held-out games' log loss / Brier / ECE:

| | decision rows | value-only rows |
|---|---|---|
| iteration 41 | 0.335 / 0.107 / 0.065 | 0.349 / 0.112 / 0.041 |
| fine-tuned with value-only samples | 0.320 / 0.101 / 0.055 | **0.330** / 0.105 / 0.036 |
| control: decision rows only | 0.319 / 0.101 / 0.059 | 0.334 / 0.107 / 0.033 |

Training on the other view helps it a little beyond fresh data (0.330 vs 0.334 nats) and costs the
decision rows nothing: value-only samples are cheap insurance, not a necessity.

### 67.5 Search: leaf values and the mulligan

`python tools/root_view.py mull --model M --reps 2` (64.3's hands: 50 with no land, 100 with one, 50
with 2-4; 64 simulations, two seeds each, no noise; both views; CPU 4 threads). At the opponent's
leaves of these searches the root player's value from its own view minus from the opponent's:
**+0.054** on average (iteration 31; +0.044 iteration 41), 0.11 mean absolute, 0.23 at p90, more than
0.05 at 73% of 16,216 leaves - far more than at real positions (67.4): in a sampled world the
opponent's hand is a uniform deal of the unseen cards, which its own view then reads as known.

Per declaration (mover view / root view; Q Mulligan where visited; keep = the line's rule cq4 s0.3):

| network | hands | searches | prior Mulligan | Q Keep | Q Mulligan | Mulligan's visits | keep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | 0 lands, first | 42 | 0.954 | 0.387 / 0.355 | 0.401 / 0.401 | 60.4 / 61.2 | 0% / 0% |
| 31 | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.028 | 0.460 / 0.417 | 0.417 / 0.404 | 1.0 / 1.6 | 100% / 100% |
| 31 | 1 land, first | 102 | 0.159 | 0.517 / 0.526 | 0.393 / 0.393 | 10.2 / 10.3 | 82% / 82% |
| 31 | 1 land, second | 98 | 0.001 | 0.470 / 0.557 | - | 0 / 0 | 100% / 100% |
| 41 | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.035 | 0.471 / 0.421 | 0.414 / 0.415 | 1.2 / 2.0 | 100% / 98% |
| 41 | 1 land, second | 98 | 0.001 | 0.482 / 0.565 | 0.349 / - | 0 / 0 | 100% / 100% |
| 41 fine-tuned (67.4) | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.049 | 0.485 / **0.378** | 0.368 / 0.371 | 1.4 / 2.7 | 100% / 97% |
| 41 fine-tuned, floor k 4 (64) | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.049 | 0.485 / 0.378 | 0.370 / 0.369 | 4.9 / 5.9 | 100% / 97% |
| 41 fine-tuned | 1 land, second | 98 | 0.003 | 0.499 / 0.524 | 0.405 / 0.415 | 0.1 / 0.2 | 100% / 100% |

* **Root-view values move the keep's Q as predicted** where the hand is bad and the opponent acts
  next: a landless keep on the draw drops by 0.04-0.05 (0.11 after the fine-tune) to the mulligan's Q.
* **They do not move the keep rates**: overall 0 lands 58% (mover) / 58-56% (root), 1 land 91% / 91%.
  The prior (0.95-0.97 on Keep on the draw) gives Mulligan 1-6 visits, and the cq rule at scale 0.3
  needs a Q gap of ~0.09 to beat that prior; with the floor (64) Mulligan is measured and still level.
* **One-land and normal hands on the draw look better from the keeper's own view** (Q Keep 0.47 ->
  0.56): 64.4's own-view optimism of the value head for a keep on the draw, now the search's leaf
  value. The mulligan's remaining lever is that value head (the outcomes' weight), as 64.4 said.

### 67.6 The replay's upkeep Brainstorm, instants by step, and the cost

`python tools/root_view.py position --model <copy of iteration 38> --replay rep_1193650d66c0_full.json
--frame 20 --reps 16 --sims 64,256` (the game rebuilt from the replay's seed and actions - the legal
actions match at every network frame; 16 seeds per run):

| | Pass: visits, Q | Brainstorm: visits, Q | the rule's move |
|---|---|---|---|
| replay (mover view, 64) | 1, 0.464 | 62, 0.655 | Brainstorm |
| mover view, 64 | 2.0, 0.512 | 61.0, 0.643 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |
| **root view, 64** | 3.5, **0.638** | 59.5, 0.652 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |
| mover view, 256 | 11.7, 0.619 | 243.3, 0.653 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |
| root view, 256 | 11.6, 0.634 | 243.4, 0.664 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |

After Pass the next decider is seat 0, whose view gives seat 1 **0.503**; seat 1's own view of the
same state **0.610** (after the cast: 0.535 / 0.610). So the suspicion holds - Pass's 22-point deficit
is the opponent's-view leaf - and root-view values close most of it (Q Pass 0.51 -> 0.64, the gap to
Brainstorm 0.13 -> 0.014), but **the decision does not change**: the prior (0.934) keeps the visits
and the network still rates Brainstorm now slightly higher.

**Instants by step** (`play --model <iteration 38> --games 24`: the network against itself, the line's
rule cq4 s0.3, 64 simulations, minor 4; instants = Brainstorm, Lightning Bolt, Daze, Force of Will,
Unholy Heat, Prismari Charm), cast by the player whose turn it is, by step, mover view / root view:

| step | mover view | root view | of which Brainstorm |
|---|---|---|---|
| own upkeep | 27 | 40 | 6 / 12 |
| own draw step | 47 | 49 | 19 / 18 |
| own main phase 1 | 81 | 80 | 22 / 19 |
| own main 2, combat | 14 | 14 | 3 / 4 |
| in the opponent's turn (any step; upkeep) | 72 (6) | 74 (17) | 2 / 3 |

Root-view leaves do not make the network wait for its main phase: own-upkeep instants are as common
or more (24 games each: noisy; seat 0 scored 0.33 / 0.46). The upkeep habit is the policy's, not a
leaf-view artefact; a network trained with root-view targets would be the test (67.8).

**Cost** (`speed`, iteration 41, 64 self-play games of the line's seat, 4 torch + 4 search threads, 90
s each): mover view **1,313 leaves/s**, root view **887 leaves/s** with 0.51 value-only rows per leaf -
1,313 / 1,342 network rows/s: the CPU is inference-bound, so the extra rows cost their full share
(-32% leaves/s). On the GPU (batches of ~96 rows at the line's conc 192) the extra rows ride in the
same batch and should cost less; not measured (A/B round 2 holds the GPU). Value-only samples at
share s add s samples per recorded decision: the window holds (1 + s) x the rows and training runs (1 +
s) x the steps per iteration (zero-core az.md 16.4).

### 67.7 What it means

Root-view leaf values are correct and leak-free here, cost a third of CPU leaves/s, and the value head
can serve them today (67.4). On today's networks they change Q where 64.4 said they would but rarely
the moves: the priors were trained on mover-view searches and dominate the visits at 64 simulations.
Whether a network trained on root-view searches plays better is the A/B's question.

### 67.8 The A/B (flags; not run)

As 64.6 / 63.6 (`runs/ab-r2/ab_driver.py`): fork the main line at K with root-view self-play and
value-only samples at 0.5, run fork and control K -> K + 10 on the same build, h2h of the two K + 10
checkpoints (600 games, both sides the line's rule cq4 s0.3 **and the same leaf view**: `mtgz.az.h2h`
follows each run's `eval_leaf_value_view`, mover on both arms); the fork wins at >= 0.5 + 2 se. The
experiment entry for an `ab_config.json`:

```json
{"name": "rootview", "requires": "--selfplay-leaf-value-view",
 "flags": ["--selfplay-leaf-value-view", "root", "--selfplay-view-samples", "0.5"],
 "set": ["selfplay_leaf_value_view=root", "selfplay_view_samples=0.5"]}
```

A variant isolating the data: `{"name": "viewsamples", "requires": "--selfplay-view-samples", "flags":
["--selfplay-view-samples", "0.5"], "set": ["selfplay_view_samples=0.5"]}` (the search unchanged). A
cheaper first look, no training: the same checkpoint with both views head to head, `python -m
mtgz.az.h2h M M --games 600 --a-leaf-value-view root --b-leaf-value-view mover` (the line's rule from
its run's config). By hand (`$BASE` = round 2's `base_flags`):

```
python tools/fork_run.py --source runs/delver2 --dest runs/r3-rootview --iter K --set selfplay_leaf_value_view=root --set selfplay_view_samples=0.5
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/r3-rootview/supervisor_console.txt   python tools/supervise.py runs/r3-rootview $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000 --selfplay-leaf-value-view root --selfplay-view-samples 0.5
```

* **The build and the Mac**: a pinned run worktree of the merged main, and `bash tools/mac.sh
  --eval-checkout` for the Mac's checkout: remote self-play ships the fork's seat with the keys
  `leaf_value_view`, `view_samples`, `view_sample_target`, which an older checkout **refuses** (an
  error, never a silent off); remote evaluation only if `eval_leaf_value_view` is set (not in this
  A/B). With the settings off the build plays as main, byte for byte (67.9), so the control continues
  delver2 unchanged.
* **Budget**: the fork's self-play is ~1.5x the network rows per leaf (GPU and Mac), its training 1.5x
  the steps (share 0.5); equal *iterations* is the comparison, as round 2.
* **What to read**: the verdict; the mulligan rates (`tools/root_view.py mull` on both K + 10:
  0-land keeps on the draw); `train.value_view` against `value_decision` (the other view's value loss
  should fall to the decider's); `train.entropy` and the policy loss; both arms against the
  heuristic; `selfplay.view.rows_per_leaf` (~0.5).

### 67.10 Risks, limits, conflict points

* **The opponent's search in the tree plays against our hand.** With root-view values the opponent's
  nodes back up the root player's assessment (as before they backed up the mover's): the opponent is
  modelled by its priors (its own view) and by values that know our hand. That is the root player's
  best estimate of each line, and the standard choice for determinized search; an opponent whose real
  play depends on what it believes we hold is modelled only through its priors.
* **Priors trained on mover-view searches.** Today's policies were distilled from searches with
  mover-view leaves; a root-view run's targets drift from them for a while (the A/B reads entropy and
  policy loss).
* **Training cost** of value-only samples (1 + s rows and steps) and the window's RAM: lower the share
  (0.25) if the window must keep its iterations.
* **The encoding contract** now matters for non-deciders: a new decision kind or encoded field must
  keep the decider's options, list and anything derived from its hidden cards out of a non-decider's
  view (67.3's tests catch it on random and Delver positions; rare decisions only if they occur).
* **Distill** (`zero.distill`) averages its policy losses over every row: a window with value-only rows
  dilutes them (its agreement metrics already skip empty segments); not on the run path.
* **Conflict points**: zero-core `Batch` / `LeafBuf` / `Dest` (`extra`), `Pending::Leaf` (`vrow`),
  `worker::decide` (the value-only records: aux targets per record, after the belief head), `NnSeat`'s
  three fields and the seat keys, `run.train_model`'s loss block (merged with the belief head's),
  `play.PyDriver._leaf_batches` (also the recording driver's). The belief head's stage 2 (66.8) adds a
  row kind to `extra` rather than a second mechanism. This repo: `engine/src/hidden.rs`
  (`deal_hidden`), tests appended at the ends of `tests/az.rs` and `tests/hidden.rs`.

## 68. The Gumbel root search (zero-core `root_search`)

Branch `gumbel-root` (from main b818054, rebased after 69's belief search): zero-core pinned at **2f0a2e8**
(feat/gumbel-root on zero-core main 353335c: the feature 7357762, its docs 2f0a2e8: zero-core docs/search.md
3.7, az.md 1.2 and 19);
this repo: the pin, `mtgz.az.replays` (recorded games search with the Gumbel root whenever the run trains
with it - `replays.root_search`, the rule of 67's `leaf_view` - and a Gumbel seat's payments get the
minor budget's schedule), `tools/gumbel_eval.py` (the CPU evidence), this section. With the settings off a run is
the run of before, byte for byte (68.8). Approved by the user 2026-10-29.

### 68.1 Why

At 64 simulations PUCT is locked in by the prior. 64.3: Keep's prior >= 0.98 in 89 of 100 one-land
hands of delver2's iteration 21, Mulligan unvisited in most; 67.6: the replay's upkeep Brainstorm
(prior 0.934) got 62 of 63 visits, Pass 1, also after root-view leaf values raised Q(Pass) to 0.638
against Brainstorm's ~0.65 - the moves barely change because the prior holds the visits. Gumbel
AlphaZero's root (Danihelka et al. 2022) samples m candidates by Gumbel-top-k, spreads the budget by
sequential halving and plays argmax(g + logits + sigma(completedQ)): a policy improvement whatever the
budget, and with <= m legal actions every option is considered. The line already had its other two
pieces: the completed-Q target (`policy_target cq`, `cq_c_scale` 0.3) and the 'cq' move rule.

### 68.2 The design (zero-core docs/search.md 3.7, az.md 19)

* **The root** (`Tree::set_gumbel`; mctx's arithmetic, its schedule checked against mctx's source):
  noise g per root option; the score g + ln P0 + sigma(completedQ), sigma(q) = (c_visit + max N)
  c_scale q - the 'cq' target's logits; sequential halving (root walk j takes an option whose walks of
  this search equal the schedule's entry, the best score among them); the move the best score among the
  most walked options; PUCT below the root. The schedule is that of the search's simulations (a fresh
  root's own evaluation takes the first).
* **Settings and seat keys**: `selfplay_root_search` / `eval_root_search` ('puct' default | 'gumbel'),
  `gumbel_m` 16, `selfplay_gumbel_scale` 1, `eval_gumbel_scale` 0; seat keys `root_search`, `gumbel_m`,
  `gumbel_scale`, `gumbel_c_visit`, `gumbel_c_scale`.
* **Interactions** (each decided and tested in zero-core):

| with | decision |
|---|---|
| sigma | one sigma for the search and its target: self-play's is the 'cq' target's (50, 0.3); an evaluation's the rule's transform (`eval_select_c_scale` 0.3) |
| Dirichlet noise, temperature | replaced by the Gumbel noise: self-play's first `temp_moves` (60) searched decisions are searched with noise 1 (the move a sample of the improved policy), later ones without; evaluation: noise `eval_gumbel_scale` (0: deterministic) |
| the move rule (`*_select`, guard 4) | not used: the Gumbel move replaces it; `eval_select_c_scale` still gives the evaluation's sigma |
| fast and minor searches (`sims_fast` 16, `sims_minor` 4, `p_full` 0.25) | Gumbel searches too (every search of the seat): at 16 simulations a root of up to 15 options gets one walk each and the best score plays; a minor payment at 4 the top 3 by g + ln P0 once each |
| the recorded target | 'cq' (required: a recording Gumbel seat with 'visits' is refused), from every root visit as the paper's |
| the root value target q | the improved policy's value (`gumbel_q`), not the root's mean backup: the halving walks every considered option, so the mean is biased low (68.3: kept hands 0.435 against Keep's 0.518) |
| tree reuse | kept: a reused root's visits count in Q and sigma, the schedule only counts this search's walks |
| root minimum visits (64) | exclusive (an error): sequential halving gives a 2-4 option root 8-31 walks per option at 64 |
| root-view leaf values (67) | orthogonal (tested together) |
| chance, determinization | unchanged; the noise is per search |
| the league seat (63) | the self-play seat: Gumbel with self-play's noise |
| the root's belief (69) | orthogonal: the belief deals the Gumbel search's worlds; a reused root's belief row (its search waits for it) costs no simulation, so the schedule is the same (zero-core's `gumbel_with_a_root_belief` tests, both drivers) |
| evaluation's Elo pool | `gumbel-m16-v50-s0.3` (a new pool: a Gumbel-evaluated run's ratings start there; with a belief `-b1` after it) |
| `mtgz.az.h2h` (zero.h2h) | each side its run's `eval_root_search` whatever `--select` says; `--a-root-search` / `--b-root-search`, `--gumbel-m`, `--a-gumbel-scale` / `--b-gumbel-scale` |

* **Not done**: the paper's deterministic interior selection (PUCT stays below the root: the starvation
  measured is at the root; it would be a separate flag with its own A/B).

### 68.3 The mulligan: keep rates (CPU)

`python tools/gumbel_eval.py mull --model <copy of iteration 51> --reps 2 --noise-reps 8` (64.3's
hands: 50 without a land, 100 with one, 50 with 2-4; 64 simulations; no noise but `gumbel-noise`; each

the same rows, the root value q against the outcome z (CPU, shared with three matches):

| | PUCT | Gumbel |
|---|---|---|
| records per game (turns) | 73.4 (18.5) | 63.1 (16.8) |

Every record is valid (a 'cq' target summing to 1, q a win vector); the Gumbel games are shorter
(16.8 against 18.5 turns; 48 games each, so a hint at most) and their targets a little less sharp (entropy

**1,794**: no cost (+3%). The search's own time per leaf 48 against 52 us (63 against 68 on the final
build): the root's completed-Q logits per walk cost nothing visible, and fewer Gumbel walks end in a

### 68.6 Head to head: Gumbel vs PUCT on the same checkpoint (CPU)

`python tools/gumbel_eval.py h2h --model <copy of iteration 51> --a gumbel --b puct --games 300 --sims S
[--view root] --seed 7` (zero.h2h's match: seats alternating, the Delver spec, chance_k 2 as the A/B
driver's h2h; side A the Gumbel root - m 16, no noise, sigma 0.3 -, side B PUCT with the line's rule
cq4 s0.3; both sides' leaves in the view given; 4 torch + 4 search threads each, three matches at once):

| simulations, leaves | seed | games | Gumbel's score +- se | margin | Elo | minutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32, mover | 7 | 300 | **0.460 +- 0.029** | -1.21 | -28 | 37 |
| 32, mover | 8 | 300 | **0.477 +- 0.029** | -1.01 | -16 | 39 |
| 64, mover | 7 | 300 | **0.540 +- 0.029** | +1.63 | +28 | 72 |
| 64, mover | 8 | 300 | **0.463 +- 0.029** | -1.93 | -26 | 53 |
| 32, root view | 7 | 300 | **0.520 +- 0.029** | +0.32 | +14 | 58 |
| 32, mover: both seeds | | 600 | **0.468 +- 0.020** | | | |
| 64, mover: both seeds | | 600 | **0.502 +- 0.020** | | | |

* **No search-only gain on today's network, either way.** At 32 simulations the Gumbel root scores
  **0.468 +- 0.020** over 600 games (two seeds: 0.460 and 0.477; 1.6 se below even); at 64, **0.502 +- 0.020** over
  600 games (0.540, 0.463); with root-view leaves on both sides at 32, **0.520 +- 0.029** (300 games). None is
  2 se from 0.5, and the pattern (a little below at 32, a little above at 64) is within the noise of
  two seeds each.
* **Why not more**: iteration 51 was trained on PUCT's searches - its priors are sharp (the recorded
  roots' top prior averages 0.87, 68.5) and its value head agrees with them where Gumbel measures the
  alternatives (the mulligan 68.3, the Brainstorm 68.4). Sequential halving then spends part of a small
  budget confirming low-prior options are worse (at 32 simulations over 16 options: eight get one walk),
  which PUCT spent deepening its favourite; at 64 there is budget for both. The search's guarantee is a
  policy improvement over the *prior*: with a prior this good and sigma at 0.3, the improvement on
  today's network is small.
* **What the A/B is for**: the question is the training signal, not the search alone - targets and
  self-play moves from a search that measures every considered option (68.5: the targets move off the
  prior's favourite where the measured Q says so). That needs a network trained on them (68.7).

### 68.7 The A/B (flags; not run)

As 64.6 / 67.8 (`runs/ab-r3/ab_driver.py`): fork the main line at K with the Gumbel root in self-play
**and** in evaluation, run fork and control K -> K + 20 on the same build, h2h of the two K + 20
checkpoints. The experiment entry for an `ab_config.json`:

```json
{"name": "gumbel", "iters": 20, "requires": "--selfplay-root-search",
 "flags": ["--selfplay-root-search", "gumbel", "--eval-root-search", "gumbel", "--selfplay-root-min-visits", "0"],
 "set": ["selfplay_root_search=gumbel", "eval_root_search=gumbel", "selfplay_root_min_visits=0"]}
```

* **Why `eval_root_search` too**: so that each side of the readout searches the way it trained with no
  driver change. The round-3 driver passes `--select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3
  --b-cq-c-scale 0.3` to `mtgz.az.h2h`; zero.h2h gives each side its run's `eval_root_search` whatever
  `--select` says, so the fork's side plays the Gumbel root (no noise, sigma 0.3 from its cq flags) and
  the control's PUCT with cq4 s0.3. The fork's own evaluations are off during the arms (`--eval-every
  1000`); if it wins and becomes the main line, its Elo pool is `gumbel-m16-v50-s0.3` (a new pool).
  (A fork that leaves `eval_root_search` at 'puct' would need `--a-root-search gumbel` in the driver's
  h2h - a driver change.)
* **`selfplay_root_min_visits=0`**: the root minimum visits are exclusive with it; round 3's `rootmin4`
  may become the main line before this experiment (an error at the fork's start otherwise).
* **The rest of the line stays**: `policy_target` cq (required) at `cq_c_scale` 0.3 (the search's sigma
  too), `temp_moves` 60 (now: the decisions searched with noise), `sims` 64 / 16 / minor 4, a root-view
  main line's leaf view (orthogonal; the driver passes each side's view).
* **The build and the Mac**: a pinned run worktree of the merged main and `bash tools/mac.sh
  --eval-checkout` for the Mac's checkout - remote self-play ships the fork's seat with the keys
  `root_search`, `gumbel_m`, `gumbel_scale`, `gumbel_c_visit`, `gumbel_c_scale`, which an older checkout
  **refuses** (an error, never a silent off), and the Mac's remote evaluation (Elo of a Gumbel main line)
  needs them too. The `requires` check only reads the desktop worktree's `--help`.
* **Budget**: the same as the control (no extra rows, the same simulations; throughput 68.5).
* **What to read**: the verdict; `train.entropy` and the policy loss (the targets move off the prior
  where the search measured a gap: 68.5); the value loss (q is the improved policy's value);
  `selfplay.unfinished` and game length; the mulligan rates (`tools/gumbel_eval.py mull` on both K + 20);
  both arms against the heuristic; the replay position.
* A cheaper first look, no training: 68.6's matches on the main line's newest checkpoint.

### 68.9 Risks, limits, conflict points

* **Sigma's scale against the prior.** Gumbel measures every considered option, but the move (and the
  target) still weigh Q against the log-prior: at 64 simulations sigma is (50 + 32) x 0.3 = 24.6 logits
  per unit of Q, so a 0.98 prior needs a Q gap of ~0.16 to be overruled (the paper's scale 1.0: ~0.05).
  The line's 0.3 won round 1 as a target scale; the Gumbel search inherits it. `gumbel-s1` (68.3) shows
  what 1.0 would do to the mulligan (a few more keeps).
* **Shallower search of the favourite.** Sequential halving spends its first round on every considered
  option (16 options at 64: eight get one walk), so the best line is searched less deeply than PUCT
  would; at small budgets with many options a single-walk Q decides the first cut. The matches (68.6)
  are the measure on today's network; a network trained on Gumbel targets may differ (the A/B).
* **Fast searches** (16 simulations) now walk up to 15 options once each and play the best noisy
  one-walk score; PUCT spent them on 1-3 options. Not measured separately (they record nothing; the
  self-play games of 68.5 contain them).
* **Exploration.** The noise is on for the first `temp_moves` (60) searched decisions - minor payments
  count -, then self-play is deterministic, with no Dirichlet noise either (PUCT: Dirichlet noise on
  every full search). If the A/B shows the policy collapsing (`train.entropy`), raise `temp_moves`.
* **The root value target.** q is the improved policy's value over the walked options (68.3), a change
  of definition for the Gumbel arm only; with the noise off (after `temp_moves`) the move is the argmax,
  whose value is slightly above it.
* **Reuse.** A reused root's first round ranks the options this search has not walked by their score,
  Q included (the paper's search has no reuse): an option measured before competes with its Q.
* **The pin is local.** zero-core `feat/gumbel-root` is not pushed (this task did not push); the pin
  2f0a2e8 must reach GitHub (and the Mac) before a worktree elsewhere can check it out.
* **The Elo pool.** A Gumbel-evaluated main line rates in `gumbel-m16-v50-s0.3`, a new pool: its ratings
  are not comparable with `cq-n4-v50-s0.3`'s history.
* **The dashboard's pool name** (zerodash `runfiles.elo_pool`) knows the Gumbel pools but not the
  belief's `-b` suffix (69's gap, not this branch's): a run evaluated with a belief shows the pool without it.
* **Conflict points** (69's belief search landed first; this branch is rebased on it - 15 files merged by
  hand in zero-core, both features kept and tested together): zero-core `tree.rs` (`Tree`'s
  fields, `Default`, `reset`, `compact`, `simulate_with`'s root selection, `backup`), `driver.rs`
  (`NnSeat`'s field and `NnSeat::eval`, `Driver::new`'s seat checks, `Slot`'s `gnoise`),
  `driver/worker.rs` (`start`, `apply_eval`'s noise condition, `decide`'s move and q, `restart_search`),
  `dynapi.rs` (`DynTree`), the bindings (`SEAT_KEYS`, `parse_seat`, `SearchTree`'s methods), Python
  `mcts.Tree` (slots, `simulate`, `backup`), `play.NNSeat` / `PyDriver._start` / `_decide` / `submit`,
  `games.nn_seat`, `run.py` (DEFAULTS, `Run.nn_seat`, `check_eval_settings`), `h2h.py`, `replay.py`,
  `parity.py`; docs search.md 3.7 (belief: its own subsection), az.md 1.2 rows and 19 (belief: 18).
  This repo: `tools/gumbel_eval.py` (new), `mtgz/az/replays.py` (`root_search`, the recorder's minor
  schedule), a test at the end of `tests/test_mtg_az.py`, this section.

## 69. Belief-weighted determinization (stage 2 of the belief head; zero-core `belief_tilt`)

Branch `belief-search` (on main 0d4328f): zero-core pinned at **353335c** (feat/belief-search on zero-core main
3b5134d: the feature 28be0f9 + 42c455e, docs 353335c - zero-core docs/search.md 3.8, az.md 18); this repo:
`Game::determinize_weighted` (`hidden.rs`), `az/belief.rs` (`deal_weights`, `MtgAz::determinize_with`), the tests
(69.4), the fuzz's `FUZZ_BELIEF`, `tools/belief_search.py` (the CPU evidence), this section. With every tilt at 0
(the default) a run is the run of before, byte for byte (69.8). The user's go-ahead (2026-10-29): "build the head
and use it in search"; the design is 66.8's.

### 69.1 What was built, and where it departs from 66.8

66.8's design is built as written: the weights w_k = clip(((e_k - known_k)^+ / max(u_k - known_k, eps))^alpha,
1/R, R); a deal that keeps everything `determinize` keeps and fills the hand's unknown slots by sequential
weighted sampling without replacement (Wallenius' urn), the rest uniform; best-of-three's hidden pool sampled
first; one forward pass of the root decider's own features per decision; the hooks `SearchGame::
determinize_with(viewer, rng, belief)` (default `determinize`) and `Tree::set_belief`; seat keys `belief_tilt`,
`belief_clip`, `belief_mix`, `belief_fast`, full searches only by default. Where it departs, and why:

* **The protocol: one dedicated `ROW_BELIEF` row per search** (kind 2 of the flagged extra rows that root-view
  values introduced, 67.2), not an `aux_rows` mask on leaf rows. A fresh root sends it after the root's own
  leaf row (a copy of the same features: the first simulation's leaf is the root, whatever world it dealt), a
  reused root alone (its simulations wait one batch round trip - the "one extra row in the next batch" of
  66.8). So a `ROW_LEAF` row is always a leaf, the cost is always one row per search, and an evaluator that
  ignores the flags (the CUDA graphs, `UniformEvaluator`) answers every leaf as before. The answer's `aux` is
  a fourth item, required when the batch has belief rows (`Driver::submit_aux`): an evaluator without it is
  an error. `NetEvaluator` computes the head on those rows only (`forward(aux_rows=)`), as 66.8 asked.
* **A checkpoint without the head is refused, never a uniform fallback** (zero-core az.md 18.3, against the
  no-silent-no-ops rule: an arm asked for belief-weighted searches that dealt uniformly would report "no
  effect" for an experiment that never ran). `net.HeadMissing`: a run refuses at start (exit 78, not
  restarted), a league opponent's checkpoint is checked, `zero.h2h` checks both sides, the evaluator raises
  for any batch with belief rows.
* **The weights' "known" cards are the ones the decider knows exactly**; a payment's pinned cards (10) count
  among the hand's unknown slots m - their identities are not read - and stay where they are (they are not
  in the deal's slots). 66.8 left it open; reading them would make the weights depend on hidden cards.
* **A cloud over the hand**: its listed cards placed in its domain first (as `determinize`), its free places
  filled from the pool uniformly, then its hand slots drawn from the cloud's cards by the weights, the rest
  of its places uniform - 66.8's "with the same weights for the cloud's hand-or-library choice". 0.7% of the
  stage-1 positions have a cloud (66.6).
* **`belief_mix`** is a per-simulation draw (one `rng.unit()` when 0 < mix), not a fixed stride; mix 1 is
  refused (it would make the tilt a no-op).
* **No fixed-point refinement, no Metropolis chain**: the measurement (69.5) shows tilt 1's dealt counts
  near the head's own; refine only if a run asks for it.
* **Additions**: remote self-play's hello carries the worker's belief keys and an older checkout is refused
  (zero-core az.md 18.5: a worker builds its seat from config.json, so an older checkout would deal uniformly
  in silence); `zero.h2h` sides follow their run's `eval_belief_tilt` even with `--select` (the A/B driver's
  h2h passes one), so an arm whose config sets it is dealt the way it trained.

### 69.2 The weights and the deal (engine)

`az::belief::deal_weights(g, viewer, p, tilt, clip)` -> one weight per identity (`identity::D`): n = the
opponent's hand size, known_k = its cards of identity k the viewer knows exactly, m = n - their number,
h_k / H = identity k's share of the opponent's cards hidden from the viewer (hand, library, face down:
`unknown_to`); for every k with h_k > 0, w_k = `zero_search::belief_weight`(n p_k - known_k, m h_k / H, tilt,
clip) (others 1). What it reads is the viewer's: the head's input (its features), the public hand size, its
exact knowledge and the hidden pool's multiset - in best-of-one the decklist less what is public or known to
it, the same in every world it deals; in best-of-three the deck `sample_hidden_pool` sampled from what it
knows (first, as `determinize` does).

`Game::determinize_weighted(viewer, rng, w)`: `determinize` with the opponent's deal replaced by
`resample_weighted`: its unknown slots and their identities as `determinize` takes them (the pinned cards
out), each cloud's listed cards removed from the pool as before; the hand's slots outside every cloud get
`weighted_draws` from the pool (each card with probability proportional to w(its identity), one at a time,
without replacement; the pool sorted, so the draw depends on the multiset and the generator only, never on
which slot held what); the rest of the pool shuffled, the clouds filled as before (a cloud over the hand:
its hand slots by `weighted_draws` from its cards); the viewer's own unknown cards dealt as `determinize`
deals them. Then the same reseeding, observer and refresh (`after_deal`, factored out of `determinize`
unchanged). Weights all equal: `determinize`'s distribution (another generator stream); hand sizes exact by
construction. `MtgAz::determinize_with` (= `determinize_belief`, which also returns the weights for tests):
between the games of a match (no hand) `determinize`; else one draw for the deal's generator, the hidden
pool (best-of-three), the weights, the weighted deal, the match's generator - `determinize`'s order.
Cost: the weights and <= 7 draws over <= 64 cards, 6 us a call against `determinize`'s 1 us (69.6).

### 69.3 Hidden information

The belief is computed from `encode(root decider)` of the live decision (zero-core: `push_belief_row` encodes
the live game, never a world; the same features in every world by the encoding's contract, tested since
section 10), and the weights read only the viewer's information (69.2). Tests: `tests/hidden.rs`
`deal_weights_ignore_the_opponents_hidden_cards` (40 random cube games, 160 worlds `determinize(viewer)` dealt
- most with another opponent hand -: the weights for one belief bit for bit the same) and `tests/az.rs`
`the_belief_weights_ignore_the_opponents_hidden_cards` (the public-state gate's positions - cube, best-of-
three, the Delver mirror, a drafted match: the decider's features identical across worlds, so the head's
prediction is, and the weights identical; best-of-three after the hidden pool is sampled with one seed).

`tests/hidden.rs` (3 new): `a_weighted_deal_follows_the_wallenius_urn` (a 5-card hidden pool {Bolt 1, Island

`FUZZ_BELIEF=t` (69.8).

### 69.5 CPU evidence: the deal against the true hand

All on the desktop's CPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`, below normal; A/B round 3 live on the GPU and the Mac), with
copies of stage 1's two networks with a fitted head (`E:\mtg-zero-scratch\belief2`; `runs/` only read): **jt** =
the joint fine-tune of 66.6 (delver2's iteration 41, 400 steps of zero-core's training with the belief loss at
weight 1; its head 2.375 nats per card held out; sha256 3e400d94...) and **ho** = the head-only fit on the frozen
iteration 41 (2.599; e7d888fa...). Positions: `tools/belief_search.py positions` - 60 games of jt against itself at
32 simulations, the line's rule (cq, guard 4, scale 0.3), uniform deals, 20,232 decisions; every 8th decision of a
player whose opponent holds a card the decider does not know: 2,412 positions. Per position the head's prediction
from the decider's features, then 200 worlds per tilt (tilt 0 = `determinize`), clip 20. Columns: the cross-entropy
per true card of the worlds' mean hand (1% of the uniform deal's exact expectation mixed in,
`belief.uniform_prior`); the cards misplaced by the mean hand (half the L1 distance to the true one); the distinct
hands among the 200 worlds (the search's diversity); for Force of Will and Daze the worlds' recall (the share
dealing one when the true hand holds one) and false alarm (the share dealing one when it holds none).

| deal (jt's head) | cross-entropy per card +- se | cards misplaced | distinct hands of 200 | Force of Will: dealt / true; recall, false alarm | Daze: recall, false alarm | Brainstorm: dealt / true |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform deal, exact expectation | 2.773 +- 0.009 | 2.844 | - | 0.305 / 0.600 | (0.279 / 0.412 dealt / true) | 0.252 / 0.187 |
| `determinize` (tilt 0) | 2.781 +- 0.010 | 2.840 | 151 | 0.304 / 0.600; 0.317, 0.222 | 0.328, 0.204 | 0.252 / 0.187 |
| belief, tilt 0.5 | **2.615** +- 0.012 | 2.640 | 144 | 0.433 / 0.600; 0.428, 0.313 | 0.403, 0.246 | 0.200 / 0.187 |
| belief, tilt 1 | 2.676 +- 0.017 | 2.540 | 128 | 0.539 / 0.600; 0.491, 0.376 | 0.432, 0.258 | 0.159 / 0.187 |
| belief, tilt 2 | 3.036 +- 0.026 | **2.523** | 97 | 0.662 / 0.600; 0.526, 0.422 | 0.426, 0.248 | 0.115 / 0.187 |
| the head's own expectation | 2.745 +- 0.015 | 2.646 | - | 0.541 / 0.600 | (0.391 / 0.412) | 0.155 / 0.187 |
| ho's head, tilt 1 | 2.654 +- 0.015 | 2.595 | 136 | 0.524 / 0.600; 0.480, 0.386 | 0.389, 0.238 | 0.156 / 0.187 |

By stratum (jt; cross-entropy, then Force of Will and Brainstorm dealt / true):

| stratum (positions) | tilt 0 | tilt 0.5 | tilt 1 | tilt 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| my turn, they have no untapped land (910) | 2.782; FoW 0.31 / 0.52; BS 0.28 / 0.27 | 2.694; 0.39 / 0.52; 0.26 / 0.27 | 2.780; 0.45 / 0.52; 0.22 / 0.27 | 3.349; 0.52 / 0.52; 0.18 / 0.27 |
| my turn, they have 1+ untapped (662) | 2.769; FoW 0.25 / 0.65; BS 0.19 / 0.06 | **2.480**; 0.43 / 0.65; 0.10 / 0.06 | 2.572; 0.59 / 0.65; 0.06 / 0.06 | 3.191; 0.77 / 0.65; 0.02 / 0.06 |
| their turn (840) | 2.791; FoW 0.34 / 0.66; BS 0.27 / 0.19 | 2.634; 0.48 / 0.66; 0.21 / 0.19 | 2.747; 0.59 / 0.66; 0.17 / 0.19 | 3.379; 0.73 / 0.66; 0.12 / 0.19 |

Read: the uniform deal's measured rows match its exact expectation (the measurement is sound). Every tilt deals
closer to the true hand than `determinize` in cards misplaced (2.84 -> 2.54 at tilt 1), and the head mostly
corrects base rates the uniform deal gets wrong: it holds Force of Will in 60% of these positions (65% when it
keeps a land up on our turn) and the uniform deal gives it one in 30% (25%); tilt 1 deals 54% (59%), and drops
Brainstorm where the line has already cast it (0.19 -> 0.06 against a true 0.06). Discrimination within a stratum
is modest (Force of Will recall minus false alarm 0.095 -> 0.115, Daze 0.124 -> 0.174). Cross-entropy is best at
tilt 0.5 (-0.166 nats per card against `determinize`, > 10 se unpaired) and tilt 1 is still better than uniform
(-0.105): past it the deal is overconfident (tilt 2 worse than uniform, 97 distinct hands of 200 instead of 151).
The tilt-1 deal beats the head's own expectation (2.676 vs 2.745): the hidden pool's multiset and the clip remove
the head's mass on cards that cannot be there. ho's head deals about as well as jt's (2.654). So tilt 1 (the head's
own odds) or 0.5 (better calibrated) are the settings worth an A/B; 2 is not.

### 69.6 Decisions and cost

**Decisions** (`belief_search.py decisions`, jt): the first 40 main-phase decisions of those games where the
decider may cast a threat (Murktide Regent, Dragon's Rage Channeler, Tamiyo, Cori-Steel Cutter) into an opponent
with 2+ cards and an untapped land; per tilt 8 Rust trees (seeds) at 64 simulations, the line's rule. The move the
rule picks moved by 3+ of the 8 seeds at **1** position of 40 (Dragon's Rage Channeler, 4 -> 1 of 8 seeds); the
threat was cast in 48% of the searches uniform and 46% with the belief. Its Q moves where the head expects a
counter: Murktide Regent into 0.81 expected Daze (they held one) 0.58 -> 0.47; Murktide into 1.35 expected Force of
Will and 0.73 Daze (they held neither) 0.78 -> 0.69; into a hand the head reads as blank, nothing. At 64
simulations the belief moves values more than moves at these decisions; 69.7 measures play.

**Cost** (`belief_search.py speed --rounds 4 --seconds 45`, jt, 64 concurrent games, 4 torch + 4 search threads,
the arms interleaved round by round on the shared machine - two h2h arms running beside it): evaluation seats (32
simulations, every search full) 1,402 -> 1,304 leaves/s, the paired ratio **0.929 +- 0.019** (a first single 90 s
run: 0.966), 0.032 belief rows per leaf - one row per search (~3% of a batch's rows) and, the tree reused from the
last move, the search waiting one batch round trip for it (another ~3%); the line's self-play seat (64 / 16, p_full
0.25, minor 4; only full searches take the belief) 1,360 -> 1,322, **0.974 +- 0.034** (0.94 in the first run),
0.0094 rows per leaf. So 3-7% of an evaluation's throughput, 1-3% of self-play's. The weighted deal itself:
`Game.determinize_with` 6.1 us a call against `determinize`'s 1.0 us (150 Delver positions, 200 calls each, the
clone subtracted) - a few microseconds a simulation (every simulation deals), nothing beside 1,500 leaves a second.

### 69.7 Head to head (CPU, 32 simulations)

The same checkpoint on both sides, side A belief-weighted, side B uniform; `zero.h2h` with the line's rule (cq,
guard 4, scale 0.3; the `-b...` tag marks A's), chance_k 0, the Delver spec, seats alternating, the driver's seed 7
(every arm starts from the same shuffles); 300 games an arm on the CPU (4 search + 4 torch threads each, two arms
at a time).

| network | side A (B uniform) | leaf values | games | A score +- se | Elo | (score - 0.5) / se | A margin | A tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jt | null: uniform vs uniform | mover | 300 | **0.517** +- 0.029 | +12 | +0.6 | +0.63 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3` |
| jt | tilt 1 | mover | 300 | **0.567** +- 0.029 | +47 | +2.3 | +2.00 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-b1` |
| jt | tilt 0.5 | mover | 300 | **0.517** +- 0.029 | +12 | +0.6 | +0.03 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-b0.5` |
| jt | tilt 1, mix 0.25 | mover | 300 | **0.512** +- 0.029 | +8 | +0.4 | +0.60 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-b1m0.25` |
| jt | tilt 1 | root (both) | 300 | **0.567** +- 0.029 | +47 | +2.3 | +2.23 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv-b1` |
| jt | tilt 1, mix 0.25 | root (both) | 300 | **0.557** +- 0.029 | +40 | +2.0 | +2.01 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv-b1m0.25` |
| ho | tilt 1 | mover | 300 | **0.500** +- 0.029 | +0 | +0.0 | +0.10 | `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-b1` |

Read: the null arm (both sides uniform) scores 0.517 +- 0.029 - the table's noise at 300 games. Every arm of jt
with the belief scores above 0.5: tilt 1 0.567 in both value views (independent games), 0.557 with the uniform
share under root-view values (the main line's search since round 3, 69.9), 0.512 with it under mover-view values;
jt's four tilt-1 arms pooled 0.551 +- 0.015 (+3.5 se), its five belief arms 0.544 +- 0.013 (+3.4 se), about +30
Elo. No two of jt's arms differ by more than 1.3 se of their difference: tilt 0.5 (the best-calibrated deal, 69.5)
against 1, the mix against none, are not separable at this size. ho (the head fitted on the frozen trunk, its deal
as good as jt's) gains nothing at tilt 1 (0.500): one arm, 1.6 se below jt's - whether the joint fine-tune's trunk
matters or it is noise, these numbers cannot say. So: a likely small gain at 32 simulations for a network trained
with the head, for 3-7% fewer leaves a second (69.6); the GPU's 600-game evaluation-only A/B on the main line's
checkpoint with a trained head (69.9) is the test.

   worlds the viewer can tell apart). Not diagnosed further here.

### 69.9 The A/B (66.8's order: evaluation only, then self-play)

**Precondition: the main line must have a trained head.** Every belief search needs the auxiliary head; a
checkpoint without one is refused (69.1). Round 3 adopted `rootview` (the main line is `r3-1-rootview` from
checkpoint 71: root-view leaf values in self-play, and in the round's h2h on both sides) and is running `belief025`
from it (K = 71, 20 iterations: the head trained at weight 0.25; `runs/ab-r3/state.json`). Neither delver2 nor
r3-1-rootview has a head. If `belief025` wins, the main line has the head from 91 on; if it loses, the
evaluation-only A/B below can still use `r3-2-belief025`'s iteration 91, and the self-play arm must fork from that
run instead of the main line. Check a checkpoint with
`python -c "from zero.net import load, check_belief_head; check_belief_head(load('M', 'cpu')[0], 'mtg')"` (from a
worktree of this build; silent = has it).

**1. Evaluation only (no training): does the belief help the search at all?** The same checkpoint on both sides, A
belief-weighted, B uniform, the round's h2h (its `H2H_SELECT`, 32 simulations, h2h's default chance_k 2, both sides
root-view as the main line now searches), 600 games, on the GPU when it is free:

```
SPEC=$(python -c "import mtgz.az as A; print(A.SPEC_DELVER)")
python -m mtgz.az.h2h M M --games 600 --sims 32 --spec "$SPEC" --device cuda --threads 8 --seed 7 \
  --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3 --b-cq-c-scale 0.3 \
  --a-leaf-value-view root --b-leaf-value-view root --a-belief-tilt 1 --b-belief-tilt 0
#   variants: --a-belief-tilt 0.5; --a-belief-mix 0.25
```

A positive score (>= 0.5 + 2 se) is worth a self-play arm; 69.7's CPU numbers (chance_k 0, 300 games an arm) are
its first look.

**2. Self-play: does a line that searches with the belief learn faster?** An `ab_config.json` entry (round 3's
driver: `requires` waits for a build with the flag, `set` goes to fork_run, `flags` to the fork's supervisor):

```json
{"name": "beliefsp", "iters": 10, "requires": "--selfplay-belief-tilt",
 "flags": ["--selfplay-belief-tilt", "1", "--belief-mix", "0.25", "--aux-belief-w", "0.25"],
 "set": ["selfplay_belief_tilt=1", "eval_belief_tilt=1", "belief_mix=0.25", "aux_belief_w=0.25"]}
```

* The fork inherits the main line's config (root-view self-play and its view samples: the round's h2h gives both
  sides root-view values). `eval_belief_tilt=1` in the fork's config makes the round's h2h deal the fork's side by
  its belief and the control's uniformly - each side searches the way it trained - with no change to the driver
  (`zero.h2h` takes a side's `eval_belief_tilt` from its run's config even with the driver's `--select`; 69.1). By
  hand: add `--a-belief-tilt 1 --a-belief-mix 0.25 --b-belief-tilt 0`. The arm runs with `--eval-every 1000`, so
  its own evaluations never use it; a winning fork that becomes the main line evaluates in a new Elo pool
  (`cq-n4-v50-s0.3-b1m0.25`), its Elo opponents (offsets 1, 2, 4, 8) checkpoints with the head.
* `aux_belief_w=0.25` keeps the head training (the belief's quality follows the policy: 66.8's feedback loop).
* Mix 0.25 is the safety net against an overconfident head (69.10); tilt 1 is the head's own expected counts.
  69.7's CPU arms do not separate tilt 1 with and without the mix (0.512 vs 0.567 with mover-view values, 0.557 vs
  0.567 with root-view values, +- 0.029 each): run the evaluation-only A/B with both (`--a-belief-mix 0.25` and
  without) and drop `belief_mix` from the entry if the mix loses clearly.
* **The build and the Mac**: a pinned run worktree of the merged main and `bash tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout`: the
  Mac's self-play worker reports its belief keys and an older checkout is refused (zero-core az.md 18.5); its
  remote evaluations carry the rule's `-b` tag (an older checkout's results are refused).
* **League**: with the round's `league25` merged, the league opponent takes the belief too and every pool
  checkpoint needs the head: a pool reaching back before the head's iteration is refused at load (HeadMissing) -
  narrow `selfplay_league_pool` or run the arm without the league.
* **What to read**: the verdict; both arms against the heuristic and older checkpoints (the feedback loop's tell is
  a fork that beats its control but loses ground against fixed opponents); `train.aux_belief` (a sudden rise: the
  policy moved away from what the head learned); `selfplay.belief.per_decision` (~0.25-0.3: the full searches'
  share); the policy loss and entropy.

By hand (K = the main line's newest checkpoint with a trained head, `$BASE` = round 3's `base_flags`):

```
python tools/fork_run.py --source runs/<main> --dest runs/r3-beliefsp --iter K --set selfplay_belief_tilt=1 \
  --set eval_belief_tilt=1 --set belief_mix=0.25 --set aux_belief_w=0.25
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/r3-beliefsp/supervisor_console.txt \
  python tools/supervise.py runs/r3-beliefsp $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000 --selfplay-belief-tilt 1 \
  --belief-mix 0.25 --aux-belief-w 0.25
```

### 69.10 Risks, limits, conflict points

* **Overconfidence**: a search only explores the worlds it deals. A sharp, wrong head (Daze at 0.9 when they hold
  Force of Will) blinds it to the punish. Mitigations built: the clip (no card below 1/20 of its uniform odds), the
  tilt, `belief_mix`; measured: 69.5's distinct hands per position and the false-alarm rates.
* **The feedback loop** of self-play with the belief (66.8): the arm reads it against fixed opponents.
* **The head's calibration** bounds what the deal can do: 66.6's head is about 0.4 nats per card better than
  uniform on the train games' distribution; a run's window gives it more data, a policy change takes it away.
* **The weights are marginal**: one weight per identity (the multinomial's marginal); the deal's joint (two Force
  of Will vs one) is the urn's. Fine for a prior.
* **Cost**: one row per full search (69.6); a reused root's round trip.
* **Root-view values and the belief together**: both on in one search was tested for correctness; their combined
  effect on play only by 69.7's h2h rows.
* **Conflict points**: zero-core `driver.rs` (`NnSeat`'s four fields - every `NnSeat { .. }` literal gains them;
  this repo has none -, `Pending`, `Eval::Nn`, `outstanding`, `submit_aux`), `driver/worker.rs` (`advance_slot`
  before the simulation, `run_chunk`'s answers, `start`, `restart_search`), `tree.rs` (`simulate_with`'s and
  `set_base`'s deal, `reset`, `advance`, `compact`), `game.rs` (a trait method), `crates/py` (`SEAT_KEYS`,
  `submit`), Python `play.py` (`_round` / `_leaf_batches` / `submit`), `replay.py`, `infer.py` (`evaluate`),
  `net.py` (`forward`'s `aux_rows`), `run.py` (DEFAULTS, `nn_seat`, the loop's start, `check_eval_settings`),

## 70. Tiered verification gates (`tools/gate.py`): tooling for the policy, user-approved 2026-10-29

Branch `gate-tooling` (from main 6f871ac): the user adopted a tiered gate policy (memory
`feedback_tiered_gates`, a Fable review 2026-10-28) after the search smoke as a gate caught 0 bugs
in 16 runs over ~7.4 h and an agent's re-run of its own suite on the sha it had already tested
caught 0 real bugs in ~30 merges - the bug finders are fuzz during development, the Mac fuzz
farm's fresh seeds, behaviour digests and `watch_run`, not a second full suite on an already-tested
commit. This section is the tooling the policy asked for: one command per tier instead of an
agent's ad-hoc `gate_<name>.sh`, plus the supporting pieces (`search_smoke --jobs`, a fuzz build
profile, the Mac farm's guaranteed slice).

### 70.1 `tools/gate.py <tier>`

Replaces the hand-written `gate_repin2.sh` / `gate_delve.sh` / `gate_v5.sh` / `gate_encoding.sh`
(same recipes, two of their bugs fixed):

* **No shared log file.** Each step gets its own log, written by this process alone - the old
  scripts' `cmd | tee /dev/stderr | grep ...` could truncate a log with NUL bytes when the child
  and `tee` raced on the same file.
* **Positive evidence, not absence of FAILED.** `grep -q FAILED && fail` passes silently when a
  build fails before any test runs (no "test result:" line at all, so no FAILED line either).
  Every checker requires a positive marker - a "test result: ok" line (with its failed count at
  0), a "combined digest" line, "N passed", "0 failed of N configurations" - and fails loudly when
  it is missing, not just when a bad one is found. (Not every step had one: the builds,
  `check_checkpoint_compat` and the Mac steps passed on exit 0 alone, and "N passed" was the first
  one anywhere in pytest's output - fixed in 91, which lists each step's marker.)

The seven tiers are the policy's table verbatim (`gate.py --help` prints each one's recipe and
budget): `docs`, `python`, `encoding`, `engine`, `search-core`, `optin-core`, `repin`. Run it from
WITHIN the checkout to gate - a pinned worktree the caller creates first, exactly as the old
scripts did (`git worktree add --detach ../mtg-zero-wt/run-<sha> <sha>`) - gate.py never creates or
manages a worktree itself, the same contract as `tools/build_py.sh` and `tools/search_smoke.py`.
`--sha` labels the report and fails loudly if it does not match the checkout's HEAD (never silently
gates the wrong commit).

**Report** (`gates/<sha>.json`, one per sha - the normal workflow gates a given commit with
exactly one tier, so the file name is keyed by sha alone; re-running a different tier against the
same sha for a check, as this section's own verification did, overwrites it): sha, the zero-core
pin, the tier, the digests seen, test counts per binary, each step's command, cwd, seconds, log
path and its sha256, pass/fail and the reason, and the cargo target dir. Logs: `gates/logs/`.

**Target guard.** A checkout marker (`.gate_checkout.json`) in `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` records which
checkout last built there; a second checkout pointed at the same target dir is refused instead of
silently reusing the first one's workspace-relative dep-info paths (memory
`reference_cargo_shared_target_dir`: this is exactly how a scratch worktree's build quietly became
the real worktree's build before M8d part 3).

**CPU only, always**: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` (an empty string does not hide the GPU on
Windows), `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` (default 4), below-normal process priority. A tier whose recipe has a
Mac part (`engine`'s conditional full-suite recheck, `repin`'s `mac.sh --eval-checkout`) runs it in
a thread alongside its desktop steps so neither waits on the other needlessly; `--no-mac` skips
Mac steps (marked skipped, not failed; since 91 also named in the final line). `--dry-run` prints
the plan - command, cwd, env overrides, which steps are parallel, which are skipped and why - and
runs nothing.

**What `gate.py` deliberately leaves out**: `repin`'s `watch_run` (it watches a *live* run
directory after the re-pin takes effect; a one-shot gate has no natural pass/fail endpoint for an
open-ended watch, so this stays an operator step after the gate passes, not a scripted check);
`search-core`'s "smoke_all for the other games in the background" (that is zero-core-side work
against a moving core commit - zero-core's own `tools/smoke_all.sh --build-only`, 70.3 - run by
whoever moves zero-core's main, not this repo's gate); `encoding`'s checkpoint-load and
`search-core`/`optin-core`'s `check_checkpoint_compat` need a `--checkpoint` / `--baseline-root`
the caller supplies (a specific run's checkpoint, or another checkout to diff against) - omitted,
the step is marked skipped with the reason, never silently treated as passing. (The run still
ended "GATE PASSED" with the skip unmentioned on that line. Since 91 these inputs are required unless
the caller opts out by name, `--allow-skip <step>`, and the final line then says "GATE PASSED WITH
SKIPS ... skipped: <step> (...)".)

### 70.2 `tools/search_smoke.py --jobs N`

Runs `N` (seed, spec) configurations at once (each already its own subprocess with a fixed seed,
module docs) instead of one at a time; report lines print in the same seed/spec order regardless
of which configuration finishes first, so `--jobs 4`'s output is identical to `--jobs 1`'s, only
the wall time differs - verified on one spec/seed set (70.6).

### 70.3 The fuzz build profile, and zero-core's `smoke_all.sh --build-only`

**`[profile.fuzz]`** (root `Cargo.toml`, inherits `release`): `debug-assertions = true`,
`overflow-checks = true` - an arithmetic overflow panics instead of wrapping, and
`engine/tests/fuzz.rs`'s existing sampled `check_determinize` checkpoint (`checkpoint_every`, 1-in-40
normally) runs 1-in-4 under `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, i.e. specifically under this profile: `cargo
test --profile fuzz -p engine --test fuzz`. Not wired into the farm's own build yet (`fuzz_farm.py`
still builds `--release`; switching it is a follow-up, see the todo list) - the profile exists and
the checkpoint rate change is live either way (it also fires under a plain `cargo test` built with
`-C debug-assertions=on`, e.g. a dev profile).

**zero-core `tools/smoke_all.sh --build-only`**: builds each game's `<pkg>._engine` (and, with
`--with-this-core`, against THIS core checkout) without their cargo test, pytest or smoke run -
"does an opt-in core feature's byte-identical-by-default build still compile against Glass Road,
Caverna and Kingdom Builder" without paying for their full suites. Default game discovery now
includes `../kingdombuilder-zero` alongside `../glassroad-zero` / `../caverna-zero`. zero-core
docs/az.md 17 has the details; `gate.py`'s `optin-core` tier's last step is this command. (Without
`--other-games` that step built no game - smoke_all found none from the gated worktree's submodule and
printed GREEN - until 90.)

### 70.4 The Mac fuzz farm's guaranteed slice (`tools/fuzz_farm.py`, `tools/mac_backoff.py`)

By default the farm backs every job off (SIGSTOP) while a run's remote self-play holds a busy
marker on the Mac (`mac_backoff.SELFPLAY_BUSY`, docs/ENGINE.md 50.2) - zero farm throughput for
however long that phase runs, deliberately conservative. Two new, OFF-BY-DEFAULT `config.json`
settings give it a guaranteed slice instead:

* **`guaranteed_jobs`** (int, default 0): this many of the round's jobs keep running at nice 19
  through a plain self-play busy marker (they still back off for a real evaluation lock, or
  PAUSE) - on the premise that niceness alone already tells the OS scheduler to prefer self-play's
  normal-priority process, so a guaranteed job need not fully stop to avoid competing with it.
* **`guaranteed_window`** (`"HH:MM-HH:MM"`, local time, wraps past midnight): every job is
  guaranteed during that window instead - a nightly slice when self-play is less likely running.

Either way the guaranteed job(s) still draw from each mode's normal advancing cursor - fresh seeds
every round, never a separate fixed range (`plan`'s `Job`s are built exactly as before; only
`guaranteed=` on some of them changes, which `start` passes through to
`mac_backoff.spawn`/`Governor.register`). `mac_backoff.Governor` now tracks two independent
stopped states (`stopped` / `hard_stopped`, each its own `why`/`paused_s`): normal groups back off
for `reason()` (any lock, including a self-play busy marker, as before - unchanged for
`guaranteed_jobs=0`, `guaranteed_window=None`, i.e. every existing deployment of the farm), and
GUARANTEED groups for `hard_reason()` (`hard_locks()`: every lock except the self-play busy glob,
or PAUSE) only.

**Not started on the Mac** (A/B round 3 is live there) - checked with
`python tools/fuzz_farm.py simulate-guaranteed`, which exercises `Governor.register` / `._loop` /
`.reason` / `.hard_reason` unmodified but swaps the OS-signal (`_signal_group`) and lock-discovery
(`held`) layers for controllable fakes, since real `Governor` back-off needs POSIX SIGSTOP/SIGCONT
(no equivalent on Windows, where this was written and checked): a normal job backs off for a
self-play busy marker and a guaranteed one does not; both back off for a hard lock and for PAUSE;
`in_guaranteed_window` reads a plain window and one that wraps past midnight correctly. All 13
checks passed (70.6). `fuzz_farm.py` still builds and runs its jobs at `--release`, not the new
`fuzz` profile (70.3) - wiring that in is a follow-up, not done here.

### 70.5 De-flaked: a zero-core cargo test and `test_pause_mid_phase_then_resume`

Two tests that failed under load and passed alone (found while building this tooling, not part of
the policy itself but blocking a clean verification run of it):

* **`driver::tests::queued_setups_are_shared_between_the_groups`** (zero-core
  `crates/search/src/driver/tests.rs`): asserted the exact POSITION of each group's dispatch size
  in the combined `sizes` vector (`sizes[..2]`, `sizes[2..4]`); reproduced reliably under thread
  contention (10 concurrent copies of the binary, ~1/300 runs) - the two groups' reports interleave
  by thread-scheduling order (which can give one group several reports before the other's first),
  not by the (deterministic) `queue_share` fairness logic the test means to guard. Fixed by
  asserting each GROUP's own distinct-size sequence (`own_sequence`, deduplicated) is `[1, 4]`
  regardless of interleaving - 480/480 passed under the same contention that reproduced the
  original failure.
* **zero-core `tests/test_remoteplay.py::test_pause_mid_phase_then_resume`**: polled
  `progress.json` for `remote.games > 50` in a flat 180 s window; under load the self-play phase is
  simply slower, not stuck, so a fixed deadline flakes. `wait_for_remote_progress` now extends the
  deadline as long as the count keeps climbing (a stall-based timeout, not a flat one), resets its
  "best seen" on an iteration change (a stale reading from an already-finished phase cannot
  short-circuit it), tolerates a torn read of `progress.json` (keeps the last good one instead of
  resetting to `{}`), and fails immediately with the run's own output if the process has already
  exited - instead of silently spinning out the rest of the window.

`queued_setups_fill_every_free_slot_when_the_queue_is_long` and the rest of
`crates/search/src/driver/tests.rs` (36 tests) still pass; `test_remoteplay.py`'s other tests were
not touched.

### 70.6 Checks

`gate.py docs`, `python` and `encoding` run for real on this repo's main 6f871ac, in the worktree
`mtg-zero-wt/gatetool` (target dir `E:/cargo-target/mtg-zero/gatetool`): all three **GATE PASSED**;
`encoding`'s digests matched the expected values exactly (full `65e8a5155bd2000c`, encoding-free
`c62a5ce5f290814e`), `cargo test --test az` 34 passed, `pytest` 55 passed both times. The Mac-part
tiers (`engine`, `search-core`'s baseline-dependent steps, `repin`) were `--dry-run` only - no Mac
jobs this session (A/B round 3 live on the desktop GPU and the Mac). `search_smoke --jobs 4`'s
output matched `--jobs 1`'s on `--specs random,eval --seeds 0-1` (same per-configuration result
lines, same order, only the wall time differed). The guaranteed slice's decision logic
(`fuzz_farm.py simulate-guaranteed`) was run locally - Windows cannot run the real `Governor`
(SIGSTOP/SIGCONT do not exist there), so the OS-signal and lock-discovery layers are swapped for
controllable fakes while `Governor.register` / `._loop` / `.reason` / `.hard_reason` run
unmodified; all 13 checks passed. It was not started on the Mac.

## 71. The fuzz farm's failures of 2026-10-29, and three of the belief fuzz's (fuzz triage)

The Mac's farm, on main b78c757 (2026-10-29 17:16-17:31), reported five failures it had not seen
on its previous build f10db98, and the belief-weighted deal's fuzz (section 69.8) three more, all
reproducing on main; this triage's own fuzz (71.10: the `fuzz` profile on the farm's seed range)
found three more of the same classes, failing on main too. None is the weighting's, layout v5's or
root view's; two are older than the farm's previous build (the farm names a failure by its message,
and layout v5 moved the floats the messages name); two are the view's (a test oracle), the rest are
engine bugs. Each is fixed here, with a test on real cube cards that fails on main d0b62b1
(`engine/tests/rules_farm2.rs`, 11 tests).

| Failure | Cause | Class | Live main line |
|---|---|---|---|
| farm a549df8eb756, 37acdaaec70a, 795476f18604: same keys, different encodings at 31288 | Urza's Bauble's look keyed for the looker only (71.1) | chance-key omission | yes, rarely (1 maindeck Bauble) |
| farm 32e7e5be2b2d, belief 15683: same keys, different views | marks hashed into the view by slot (71.2) | fuzz-check false positive | no |
| (found with it) a second Nadu's count | `Mark::Triggered` named its Nadu by incarnation number (71.2) | engine bug | no (not in the deck) |
| (this fuzz) 10002917 and six more: same keys, different views | the view's companion by its slot (71.2) | fuzz-check false positive | no |
| farm 7f0953e0e769 (f10db98's 7b7fc0b85e1b): determinize changed the encoding at 16 | "you may cast it" skipped when uncastable (71.3) | determinize bug (section 10's second rule) | no (non-decider deals only) |
| (this fuzz) 10038672: determinize changed the view | the miracle cast question skipped, and a revealed miracle card's knowledge moved to its twin (71.3) | determinize bugs | no (no miracle card in the deck) |
| belief 7193: PayMana: no way to pay | a face choice did not pin the hand's mana sources (71.4) | determinize bug (pins) | no (non-decider deals only) |
