### 71.1 Urza's Bauble: the hand's owner sees which card was seen

**The failures.** `match ... step N: same keys, different encodings of P1 at 31288` (three seeds:
a Manifold Key's ability, an AssignDamage, an Erode on the stack - the decisions printed are the
ones the check reached; the Bauble's look came a step or two before, in every seed's dump of both
worlds). Float 31288 is the hand block (`O_HAND` 31172) slot 1, float 56 = `CODE` + 4: **"known to
the opponent"** of a card in the viewer's hand. Not new: layout v4's hand block began at 27588, and
the same failure is in the farm's list since 433ff28 at 27644 / 27704 / 27824 (slots 0, 1, 3:
ca3f8fd6d46b x9, 910523e34733, 78564f28d3db, efa513e0097d, b0bfc5350c44, dbbd6a49c522 - which names
the Bauble -, 89490d2619bb); layout v5 (7d1f24b) moved the block, the messages changed, and the
farm hashed them as new. All three seeds reproduce at f10db98, at 27704.

**Cause.** "Look at a card at random in target player's hand" (`Ext::LookAtRandomHandCard`) picks
with the state's generator, which `determinize` reseeds per world, and makes the card known to the
looker - remembered, because its owner knows which card was seen (23.7) - but keyed it
`KEY_LOOK(looker, def)` privately: in a search of the **hand's owner** the key was masked
(`HIDDEN`), so the worlds in which different cards were seen shared a node, while the owner's
encoding (the hand block's float 4) and knowledge differed. A chance-key omission (a fact the
viewer observes and the encoding shows, missing from its keys), not a leak: the owner does know
which card.

**Fix.** The look at another player's hand is keyed public (both players know the card: the looker
saw it, the owner saw which); a look at one's own hand stays private. `force_chance` replays it in
the owner's worlds now too (the key is no longer `HIDDEN` there). `Game::view_of` (the
information-set checks' view) gains the viewer's own hand as the multiset of (definition, known to
the opponent): the games fuzz's `check_information_set` did not see this fact (only the match
check, which compares encodings, did).

**Who it affects.** Every pool with Urza's Bauble (the cube, interactions, drafted pools) and the
Delver mirror (one maindeck Bauble): a search of the player whose hand the opponent's Bauble looks
at merged the worlds past that look and evaluated the merged nodes with whichever world's encoding
reached them (mover and root-view leaves alike). A search-quality fix; no network input changes.

**Test.** `urzas_bauble_keys_the_card_seen_for_the_hands_owner_too`: 24 worlds of the owner; the
key names the card now known to the looker, equal keys give equal encodings, and the worlds saw
different cards.

### 71.2 Marks naming another object; a second Nadu

**The failures.** `seed 10588610 step 8: same keys, different views` (farm, interactions and
games) and the belief fuzz's seed 15683 (`--profile fuzz`; Grief evoked, then Animate Dead on it):
the views differed in one value, a mark's hash. `view_of` hashes the marks (since 32a06e4, section
58.6) with `h64(&mark)`, and two marks carry another object's identity: `Mark::Reanimated(ObjRef)`
(Animate Dead's creature: card #4 in one world, #34 in the other - Grief came from a hand the
viewer did not know) and `Mark::Triggered { src_inc }` (Nadu's granted trigger: the granting Nadu's
incarnation number - found by Green Sun's Zenith, it was a different library slot per world, with
another history). Neither is observable; the encoding reads neither. **A fuzz-check false
positive**: the view now names both objects by their public place (as it names links and
`ExiledToPay`'s card). Bisect: f10db98 passes 10588610, 32a06e4 (the commit that put marks in the
view) fails it; 15683 is the same root cause under the `fuzz` profile's denser checkpoints (release
builds pass that seed at every commit).

**The engine bug found with it.** "This ability triggers only twice each turn" (Nadu,
`TrigPred::TimesPerSubject`) counts per granting object (a Nadu that leaves and returns grants a new
ability: CR 400.7, ruling 96e9a886), but the mark named the granting Nadu by its incarnation number
alone, which another Nadu that came the same way shares (hand, stack, battlefield: 2): the second
Nadu's grant found the first one's two triggers and did not trigger that turn. `Mark::Triggered`
now carries the granting object (`src: ObjRef`).

**The companion.** The view also showed the revealed companion's slot's zone once it was in the
game; beside a twin in a hand the viewer does not know (a second Lutri, the Spellchaser), which slot
leaves when its owner casts "Lutri" is not observable, and the worlds differed (this triage's fuzz:
default-pool seeds 10002917, 10005671, 10005795, 10006483, 10027195, 10037943, 10038627, the `fuzz`
profile's checkpoints; main fails every one). The view now shows whether the companion is still
outside the game; where it is in public is the zones' own entries. Also a fuzz-check false positive.

**Who it affects.** The view: tests only. Nadu: the cube, interactions and drafted pools, not the
Delver deck.

**Tests.** `an_animated_creature_from_a_searched_library_looks_the_same_in_every_world` (Entomb,
then Animate Dead: the creature's slot differs between the worlds, the views do not),
`a_nadus_granted_trigger_looks_the_same_in_every_world` (Nadu cast from a hand the opponent does
not know: from a slot drawn this turn or one held since),
`a_second_nadu_grants_a_new_twice_each_turn_count_cr400_7`,
`a_companion_cast_beside_a_twin_looks_the_same_in_every_world` (the twin on a hand slot before the
companion's in one world, after it in the other).

### 71.3 "You may cast it" is asked even when it cannot be cast

**The failures.** `match 10278736: determinize changed the encoding of P1 (mover P0) at 16: 1 -> 0`
(farm, drafted; the same message at f10db98 as 7b7fc0b85e1b, interactions match 10319082, and at
433ff28 as 46e5799497d7). Global 16 is "the viewer has priority". The real games: P0 to answer
Bilbo, Thief in the Night's attack trigger ("you may cast an artifact, instant or sorcery spell from
your graveyard", `ChooseGraveyardCard`) while P1 held priority; 10319082: Chandra, Torch of
Defiance's +1 ("exile the top card of your library; you may cast that card", `YesNo`).

**Cause.** Both askers skipped their question when no card could be cast, and castability counts
the caster's hidden hand (a Simian Spirit Guide's mana, a card an alternative cost exiles). A world
`determinize` deals for the other player re-runs the asker (`refresh_pending`) with P0's hand dealt
again: without the Guide the question was gone, the ability finished and priority passed - so P1's
encoding changed, and the world was not in P1's information set. Section 10's second rule (a
decision whose options depend on hidden cards is asked even when only "pass" remains) was broken:
**a determinize bug**, in the askers. Only a deal for the non-deciding player shows it (71.8).

**Fix.** Asked whenever the card is a spell card the effect names (public: in the graveyard and
matching the filter by a spell face, `gy_spell_matches`; exiled with a spell face,
`Game::has_spell_face`) and the caster may cast spells during a resolution at all
(`may_cast_during_resolution`: no "can't cast spells", no "only any time they could cast a sorcery"
- public too, so under Teferi, Time Raveler the effect still goes on without a question), the card
(or "yes") offered only if it can be cast now. A question left
with "pass" alone is answered by the engine and keyed `KEY_AUTO` (public), as every single-option
decision is (section 10), so real play is unchanged but for that key. The same pattern was fixed in
the free-cast askers - cascade, Etali's exile-until-nonland, "an opponent exiles three, you may cast
one" (`M7d::OppExilesThreeMayCastOne`), Malcolm's loot - whose castability counts the hand through
a spree's mode costs (Three Steps Ahead) paid with a Spirit Guide - and miracle's cast question
(`Ext::MiracleCast`, "you may cast it for its miracle cost", this triage's fuzz seed 10038672);
Shelldock Isle's question and miracle's reveal question already followed the rule.

**A miracle card beside its twin.** Seed 10038672 had a second cause. P0 held two Metamorphosis
Fanatics and revealed the one drawn; `canon_hand_knowledge` treats twins as interchangeable and
moved the "known" bit onto the other copy (the lower card index), so a world for P1 dealt the
trigger's own card (`ev.obj`) another identity, and the question had no miracle card to ask about.
But the revealed card is played revealed until its ability resolves (CR 702.94b): it is told apart.
The canonicalization now leaves alone a hand card a waiting trigger, a stack item or a delayed
trigger names. This one reaches a live search: P1 deciding while P0's miracle trigger waits (P1's
priority over it) dealt worlds in which the miracle could not happen - but only with two copies of a
miracle card in one hand, never in the Delver deck.

**Who it affects.** Worlds dealt for the non-deciding player only: tests and analysis (the fuzz's
checks, `tools/root_view.py`'s leak check, `tools/belief_search.py`); no live search deals for a
non-decider (71.8). The cube, interactions and drafted pools; the Delver deck has none of these
cards.

**Tests.** `bilbos_graveyard_cast_is_asked_whether_or_not_the_hand_can_pay` (the Bolt castable only
with the Guide: 40 worlds of the opponent, some without the Guide, all asking the same question,
P1's encoding unchanged; with an Island instead, the question with "pass" alone),
`chandras_exiled_card_is_asked_whether_or_not_the_hand_can_pay` (the same; "no" deals the 2 damage),
`a_miracle_cast_is_asked_whether_or_not_the_hand_can_pay`,
`a_miracle_card_beside_its_twin_stays_the_revealed_one_cr702_94b`.

### 71.4 A face choice pins the caster's hand mana sources

**The failure.** The belief fuzz's seed 7193 under `--profile fuzz` (main's own fuzz, no weighting):
`in a world determinized for P0 (mover P1), option 4 (ChooseFace P1: 0) of ChooseFace for P1 can't
be completed: PayMana: no way to pay {1}{R}`. **Cause:** "which face?" (`Task::ChooseFace`, an
Adventure, an MDFC or a split card with both faces castable) comes before `begin_cast`, so
`payment_in_progress` saw no payment, and the faces' mask - computed at priority counting a Simian
Spirit Guide in hand, and kept in the task so that a refresh asks the same question - outlived a
world for the other player that dealt the Guide away. **A determinize bug** (the pins). **Fix:**
`payment_in_progress` answers a `ChooseFace` with a cast bit with its caster (the cast has begun:
CR 601.2a-b, 712.11b, 715.3), so the hand's mana sources are pinned as for a payment, and
`exile_filters_in_progress` adds the offered faces' alternative costs that exile a hand card.
**Who:** non-decider deals only (71.8); the Delver maindeck has no card with two castable faces
(Rough // Tumble is in the sideboard, which the Bo1 mirror does not use). **Test:**
`a_face_choice_pins_the_casters_hand_mana_source` (Brazen Borrower: 40 worlds of the opponent keep
the Guide; both faces cast and paid in each).

### 71.5 Teamwork with a Lumberjack

**The failure.** The belief fuzz's seed 14537 (`FUZZ_BELIEF=4 --profile fuzz`; a weighted world's
own random play after its deal, an ordinary legal position): We Say Thee Nay!'s teamwork ("tap
creatures with total power 2") offered, then `ChoosePermanent with no options`. **Cause:** the cost
check (`ChooseCost`, `crew_mana_ok`) taps no creature without a mana ability for its trial, and kept
Orcish Lumberjack's sacrifice-a-Forest mana (`LJ_FOR`, a shared class); the creature decision taps
Enduring Innocence or Aragorn for its trial, and `classes_without` dropped **every** Lumberjack
class whenever **any** creature was tapped - with the Forest already tapped and Mishra's Workshop's
mana for artifacts only, Gleemox alone could not pay {1}{U}. **An engine bug** (the check and the
decision disagreed). **Fix:** `Game::classes_without` lowers a shared class's count of Lumberjacks by
the Lumberjacks among the creatures tapped (the same conditions as `mana_classes`' `sac_by`),
dropping the class only when none is left. **Who:** real games with the cube's We Say Thee Nay! and
a Lumberjack; not the Delver deck. **Test:**
`teamwork_keeps_a_lumberjacks_mana_when_another_creature_is_tapped`.

### 71.8 Who a live search deals for

Verified in zero-core 2f0a2e8 (the pin): the only deal is `tree::deal(g, self.viewer, ...)` (uniform
`determinize`, or `determinize_with` the root's belief), from `set_base` (one world per decision)
and `simulate_with` (a world per simulation); the driver (`worker.rs`) resets a tree with
`p = game.to_move()`, `Tree::advance` sets the viewer to the next decider, and the driver keeps a
tree only while the same player decides next. Root-view leaves (section 67) evaluate the root
player's encoding **in the root player's world**, dealt once at the root where that player decides;
deeper opponent nodes reuse that world, nothing is dealt for them. Self-play, the league, h2h, the
evaluators and chance nodes (`force_chance` queues outcomes, it deals nothing) all run this driver.
The bindings' `Game.determinize(viewer, ...)` / `determinize_with` are called by tests and tools
only. So 71.3 and 71.4 affect non-decider deals in tests and analysis, never a live search; 71.1
affects live searches (the hand owner's tree), 71.3's miracle twin the other player's tree at a miracle trigger, 71.5
real games.

## 72. Who knows a library's top cards, in the encoding

Branch `top-known` (from main e08bade), 2026-10-30, CPU only; the user's decision after a question
about top-of-library knowledge in the Delver mirror ("a correctness issue": fix the input before any
belief over the opponent's top cards). Layout v5 is unchanged: six spare per-player floats, as
section 55 filled v4's. The rules engine is untouched (the encoding-free digest is equal).

### 72.1 The gap

`Obj.known` (section 10) says which players know a hidden card. What the card is stays hidden;
**who knows it is public**: every event that sets or clears a bit is seen by both players (a look
at the top N, a surveil kept on top, Brainstorm's put-back, a Mishra's Bauble at one's own library,
a shuffle, a draw). The encoding showed the viewer's own knowledge (the tops block's "known to the
viewer" and the card; the `*_KNOWN` bags) and, for the hand, which of the viewer's cards the
opponent knows (hand st[4]), but not who else knows a library card:

* **The opponent's library known to its owner.** The opponent Ponders and keeps, surveils and keeps
  (Dragon's Rage Channeler, Thundering Falls), Brainstorms, or looks at its own top with a Bauble:
  everyone knows the opponent knows its next draws, and the keep or the put-back says something
  about them. The viewer's input was identical to an untouched library, so neither the trunk nor a
  belief head could learn anything from it.
* **The viewer's library known to the opponent.** A Mishra's Bauble at a top card its owner knows
  is remembered by the looker (23.7); the owner's input did not show that the opponent knows its
  next draw.

The public-state gate (58.6) could not see it: it classified `Obj.known` as hidden as a whole.

### 72.2 The fix: six spare floats per player

`g5::TOP_OWNER` (per-player floats 16-18) and `g5::TOP_OTHER` (19-21): per position k of the top
three (`TOPS`, top first) of that player's library (per-player blocks viewer first), 1 if the
library's owner knows the card there, and 1 if the other player does. Two per-player floats stay
spare. For a viewer the floats about its own knowledge repeat the tops block's "known to the
viewer"; the new information is the other player's knowledge of both libraries.

Layout v5 is unchanged (37,620 floats; `layout_v5.json` declares `globals_v5` as a block), so the
encoding guard (61) accepts every v5 checkpoint and the shards' width is the same. As in 55.2, the
inputs were always 0 in training: their `TokenNet` weight columns are their initialisation (less
weight decay) until training gives them a meaning.

### 72.3 Hidden information

Who knows stays with a card's slot: `determinize` deals identities (`set_ident`) and
`force_library_card` swaps identities between cards nobody knows, so the floats are the same in
every world either viewer's `determinize` deals, and a viewer's input says nothing about what the
cards are. `Game::view_of` now lists, per library, the positions the other player knows (whose
changes the gate needs to see); the fuzz and the hidden-information checks compare it across
worlds.

### 72.4 The gate

`Obj.known` is classified public ("who knows is public, what it is is not: leak-tested") with four
perturbations, each through `Game::learn` (which keeps the clouds right): the owner learns its top
card; the other player learns a library's top card (its owner too: a library card the other player
knows its owner knows, 23.7); the owner learns a card below the top three (a **deliberate limit**:
below the top three the encoding has the viewer's own knowledge only, in the bags; that the other
player knows a deeper card is a mulligan's bottom cards, whose number the mulligans' count gives,
or a card put under others, never the next draws); the other player learns a hand card (hand st[4]
and `OPP_HAND_KNOWN`, already encoded).

`public_state_reaches_the_encoding` (240 positions: the cube, the Delver mirror, best-of-three, a
drafted match; 211 fields, 117 public, 6 hidden, 88 derived; 145 perturbations): the owner learns its
top card, 223 applied; the other player learns a library's top card, 240; a hand card, 218 - both
views and both encodings changed every time. Below the top three: 240 applied, both views changed,
the non-owner's encoding unchanged every time (the limit, as declared). In all: 135 encoded, 4
deliberate limits, 1 gap for the next layout (the graveyard's order, as before).

### 72.5 Tests

`tests/az.rs` `who_knows_a_librarys_top_cards_is_encoded` (the constructed card pool, both viewers,
20 worlds each per step): P0 Brainstorms, putting a Mountain and a Bolt back (P0's library
`[(1,0), (1,0), (0,0)]`, (owner, other), top first); P1's Mishra's Bauble at P0's top card, which P0
knows (`[(1,1), (1,0), (0,0)]`, P1 remembers it); P0 Ponders and keeps (P1 loses track of its card:
`[(1,0), (1,0), (0,0)]` after the draw); Polluted Delta's search shuffles (all 0). P1's library stays
all 0 throughout. The gate's tests (`public_state_reaches_the_encoding`, the classification table)
and `the_v5_facts_encode_no_hidden_information` run the new perturbations.

### 72.6 Encoding, digests, networks

Encoding-free behaviour digest **a634df1919e3c337, unchanged**; the full digest 11e873a3d2e4530a ->
**6b4bc88c864c4dd4** (`DIGEST_WRITE=1`: 1,825 of the 2,500 games encode differently at some
position).

The encoding gate (`tools/gate.py encoding`, `gates/45535f0adf75.json`): the build, both digests as
above, `--test az` 39 passed, the main line's checkpoint `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch/models/iter_0196.pt`
(read only) loads and plays 8 Delver games (h2h, CPU, 16 simulations, none unfinished), pytest 59
passed. Fuzz: 300 games of the default pool and 1,000 of the Delver pool (`FUZZ_POOL=delver`), clean.

**What a v5 checkpoint sees.** Unlike 55.2's v4 networks, the main line's descend from 60's exact
widen, which gave every v5 global a zero weight column, and a column whose input is always 0 never
moves: the columns of these twelve floats are exactly 0 in `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch` iterations 100
and 196 and in delver2's iteration 0 (`TokenNet.g`, inputs 160 + 24 side + 16..21). On 4,000 Delver
positions where they are set (a third of the decisions of mixed heuristic / random games, 1.7 set
floats a row), iteration 196's and 100's values and policies are those with the floats masked, bit for
bit (P(win) shift 0, policy KL 0, no argmax changed). So a re-pin changes nothing for the network until
training grows the columns, as it grew the used v5 globals' from 0 (cards drawn 0.3-0.95, attacked 0.5-0.6,
delayed triggers - a Bauble's draw - 1.9-2.1; the ones the mirror never sets are still 0). A network
built fresh has random columns there instead, which distilling from older shards (all 0 there) never
trains: a distilled student (62.9) moved onto this build should have them zeroed first, or it plays
with an untrained input (55.6's size of effect).

### 72.7 What this does not change

* A Mishra's Bauble at a card its owner does not know is still not remembered (23.7), and a
  shuffle followed by a draw still drops the cloud it made (10): the bot's own knowledge.
* The belief head (66) predicts the opponent's hand only and the weighted deal (69) tilts the hand;
  the opponent's known top cards are dealt uniformly. A belief over them is a later step, and now
  has an input to learn from.
* A run picks this up at a re-pin (an iteration boundary; checkpoints, the optimiser state and the
  window's shards load as they are); which run and when is the user's call.

## 73. Strength measurement for the Delver line (zero-core `feat/measure`: fixed Elo anchors, held-out losses, paired + sequential h2h; behaviour fingerprints)

User-approved 2026-10-30 after a Fable review found that the main line's yardsticks could not see its
progress (zero-core docs/az.md 20 has the framework's side: settings, formulas, tests). This branch
pins zero-core `feat/measure` and adds `tools/delver_fingerprints.py`, `mtgz.az.heldout` (the shim)
and `tests/test_measure.py`. Every new setting is off by default: the engine, the encoding, the
digests and every run of before are unchanged (73.9).

### 73.1 Why

The review's evidence on `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch` (paused at iteration 196):

* **The Elo pool** (`elo/cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv-b1m0.25/`): every 8 iterations each checkpoint plays k-1,
  k-2, k-4, k-8 for 25 games each at 32 simulations: +-50-115 Elo per rating, no fixed reference.
  The ratings of the evaluated checkpoints 128-192 wander 1448-1613 with se 47-70; the pooled pairs
  give 0.481 +- 0.015 = -1.9 +- 2.3 Elo per iteration - a plateau and +1 Elo a generation look alike.
* **The yardstick** is saturated: 92-98% against the heuristic since iteration ~100 (the user: stop
  testing against it).
* **h2h verdicts** (600 games, se 0.020) are too noisy for the effects the A/B program adopts: two
  features went in at 0.538 and 0.534 (the bar 0.541). The games alternate seats but are not paired:
  each game's deal is its own, so a mirror's opening-hand variance stays in the score.
* **A cheap learning signal** was missing: the held-out value loss against the true outcome z on a
  fixed set of fresh rows moved 0.4066 (iteration 111) -> 0.4012 (188) in the review's check.

### 73.2 What the pin adds (zero-core docs/az.md 20)

* **Fixed anchors** (`--elo-anchors label=path,...`, `--elo-anchor-games`, `--elo-anchor-elo`,
  `--elo-anchor-calib-games`, `--elo-anchor-from`): frozen checkpoints every evaluated checkpoint plays;
  the first anchor's rating set, later ones calibrated once against it and frozen (sha256 kept); the
  fit of the pool's whole results with them fixed -> `elo_anchored` (metrics, evals.jsonl, log),
  `anchored.json`. Shipped to the Mac's mirror for `--eval-remote mac`. `--eval-games 0` drops the
  heuristic's games; every Elo match is still played (tested).
* **`--elo-paired 1`**: the run's Elo matches as paired games (even game counts).
* **Held-out losses** (`--heldout-shards`, `python -m mtgz.az.heldout make | eval`): value CE /
  accuracy / Brier against z and policy CE / top-1 against the recorded targets on a frozen row set,
  decision and value-only rows apart, every evaluated iteration (`heldout` in the metrics, a log line).
* **zero.h2h** (`python -m mtgz.az.h2h`, the same module): `--paired`, `--sprt E0,E1` (+ `--alpha`,
  `--beta`, `--batch-games`, `--max-games`), `--target-se`, `--a-sims` / `--b-sims`.

### 73.3 Paired h2h on the Delver mirror: the variance it removes

**Method.** Checkpoint 196 (A) against 188 (B) of the line, 32 simulations, each side its run's
evaluation search (config.json next to models/: the 'cq' rule n4 at 0.3, root-view leaves, the belief
tilt 1 mix 0.25 on every search), `chance_k` 0 (the run's evaluation; h2h's default 2 hit the engine
panics of 73.8), the Delver spec (**correction, section 74**: the jobs passed no `--spec`, so `zero.h2h`
played the package's `mtg` spec, random cube decks; the numbers below are of cube games played by the
Delver line's checkpoints, not of the mirror); batches of 200 games on the Mac (`nice -n 19`, beside the fuzz
farm: 6.5 min each) and one on the desktop CPU (22 min), each batch its own seed (11-14, 21); paired,
and one unpaired batch for the check.
(`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/pool_batches.py` pools them: the pentanomial counts add up.)

| batch | games | A's score | se (paired) | se_games (unpaired formula) | variance_ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| paired seed 11 | 200 | 0.490 | 0.0246 | 0.0353 | 0.48 |
| paired seed 12 | 200 | 0.500 | 0.0293 | 0.0354 | 0.68 |
| paired seed 13 | 200 | 0.470 | 0.0264 | 0.0353 | 0.56 |
| paired seed 14 | 200 | 0.460 | 0.0232 | 0.0352 | 0.43 |
| paired seed 21 (desktop) | 200 | 0.545 | 0.0247 | 0.0352 | 0.49 |
| **paired, pooled** | **1,000** | **0.493** | **0.0115** | 0.0158 | **0.53** (95% bootstrap 0.46-0.61) |
| unpaired seed 11 | 200 | 0.470 | - | 0.0353 | - |

The 500 pairs: 63 both won, **367 split (73%)**, 70 both lost, no draw (pentanomial [70, 0, 367, 0,
63]); the unpaired batch agrees (0.470 +- 0.035). In three pairs of four each side won with the same seat's deal - the deal (who is on the play,
the two hands, the library) decides most mirror games, and pairing takes that variance out:
**var(pair score) = 0.53 x var(game) / 2**, so a paired h2h of N games is as precise as an unpaired
one of 1.9 N. At 600 games the se falls from 0.020 to 0.015 and the 2-se bar from 0.541 to 0.530. (By
the way: 196 scored 0.493 +- 0.012 against 188 - -5 +- 8 Elo: eight iterations without a measurable
gain.)

**What it does to the A/B verdicts** (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/sprt_sim.py`: 8,000 simulated tests
per row; pair scores from the 3-point law with the ratio 0.54 of the first four batches, games from a
Bernoulli; zero.h2h's LLR
and bounds): the share of forks adopted and the mean games played, for a fork that is truly E Elo
better -

| true E | score | 600-game 2-se bar, unpaired (today) | ... paired | SPRT(0, 20), <= 2,400 games, unpaired: H1 / undecided / games | ... paired |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -10 | 0.486 | 0% | 0% | 0% / 3% / 1,282 | 0% / 0% / 836 |
| 0 | 0.500 | 2% | 2% | 2% / 29% / 1,804 | 2% / 9% / 1,354 |
| +10 | 0.514 | 10% | 15% | 20% / 60% / 2,107 | 30% / 39% / 1,831 |
| +20 | 0.529 | 28% | 46% | 69% / 30% / 1,791 | **90% / 8% / 1,343** |
| +30 | 0.543 | 54% | 80% | 96% / 3% / 1,266 | 100% / 0% / 841 |
| +40 | 0.557 | 79% | 97% | 100% / 0% / 926 | 100% / 0% / 655 |

Today's readout adopts a real +20 Elo fork 28% of the time; paired + SPRT(0, 20) adopts it 90% of the
time in 1,343 games on average (2.2 batches of 600), with the same 2% false adoptions of a null; a
+30 fork is decided in 841 games. SPRT(0, 15) with up to 3,000 games: +20 adopted 97% (1,448
games), +10 43%, a null 2% (1,935 games, 18% undecided). The choice (73.6) is SPRT(0, 20), alpha =
beta = 0.05, batches of 600, at most 2,400: the effects the program has adopted (0.534-0.538, +24-26
Elo) are inside its power, its false positives are the old bar's, a lopsided result still costs one
batch of 600 and a close one up to four (~76 min on the GPU).

### 73.4 Held-out losses of the main line

The set: `python -m mtgz.az.heldout make --from runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch/data/iter_0191 --rows 8192
--seed 0` -> `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/heldout/r3-2b_iter0191_8192.npz` (8.8 MB; set
`463ad8eefa5c`: 5,407 decision rows, 2,785 value-only rows of iteration 191's 800 games, generated by
checkpoint 190). Iteration 191's rows trained checkpoints 191-196 only (window 6): held out for every
checkpoint up to 190 and for all the line's next ones (197 on). All 110 checkpoints of the line's
models/ (83-196), CPU, 2.4 s each:

| checkpoint | decision value_ce | acc | policy_ce | top-1 | view value_ce | acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 83 | 0.3933 | 0.796 | 0.522 | 0.843 | 0.4103 | 0.785 |
| 96 | 0.3876 | 0.801 | 0.490 | 0.859 | 0.3995 | 0.792 |
| 112 | 0.3872 | 0.800 | 0.467 | 0.872 | 0.3908 | 0.805 |
| 128 | 0.3865 | 0.800 | 0.444 | 0.882 | 0.3938 | 0.794 |
| 144 | 0.3839 | 0.804 | 0.425 | 0.890 | 0.3916 | 0.797 |
| 160 | 0.3852 | 0.801 | 0.402 | 0.906 | 0.3950 | 0.797 |
| 176 | 0.3842 | 0.798 | 0.383 | 0.926 | 0.3974 | 0.788 |
| 188 | 0.3839 | 0.808 | 0.363 | 0.947 | 0.4053 | 0.787 |
| 190 | 0.3878 | 0.801 | 0.360 | 0.951 | 0.4099 | 0.782 |
| 191 (trained on it) | 0.3593 | 0.823 | 0.361 | 0.948 | 0.3746 | 0.805 |
| 196 (trained on it 6 x) | 0.3192 | 0.857 | 0.357 | 0.948 | 0.3309 | 0.841 |

* **The value head learns slowly**: decision rows' value CE 0.393 (83) -> 0.384 (188), a linear fit
  over the clean checkpoints (83-190) -0.009 per 100 iterations, with a checkpoint-to-checkpoint
  scatter of ~0.003 (120: 0.394). The view rows' value CE does not improve at all (-0.0015 per 100
  iterations).
* **Contamination is large**: the checkpoints that trained on the set's rows fall to 0.319 (196, six
  windows) - the value head memorizes the outcomes of games it trained on, 0.065 nats in six
  iterations against 0.009 of real progress in a hundred. A set must be fresh for the checkpoints it
  measures: iteration 191's is for 197 on.
* **The encoding moved under it**: the set's rows were encoded before section 72's top-card floats (six
  per-player globals, set at about a third of Delver decisions; 0 in the set). The line's checkpoints
  have zero weights on those columns (72: their outputs bit for bit unchanged), so they read the set
  as before; once training moves those weights, a set built from a relaunched iteration (held out from
  six iterations after it) measures the new inputs too - keep iteration 191's for the history.
* **policy_ce is agreement, not strength**: it falls steadily (0.522 -> 0.360) towards checkpoint 190,
  the search that recorded the targets, and stays there after; the line's next checkpoints will move
  away from 190's search whether they improve or not. Read it as drift (a collapse or a jump shows),
  `value_ce` as the learning signal.

### 73.5 Behaviour fingerprints (`tools/delver_fingerprints.py`)

`python tools/delver_fingerprints.py r3-2b-beliefsearch` (bands of 20 generations; `--band`,
`--min-gen`, `--max-gen`, several runs, `--json`). The replays are the Delver AI publisher's
(runs/<run>/replays: 6 games of every even generation against itself, 64 simulations), both seats
counted; a cell is rate (n). The metrics' exact definitions are in the tool's docstring; in short:

* **fetch cracked now**: of the fetches played and cracked, the share cracked with nothing between.
* **brainstorm w/ shuffle**: of the Brainstorms cast, the share with a shuffle to follow (its own
  fetch ability on the stack - `bs in resp. to fetch` -, an uncracked fetch of its own, or a fetch
  in hand with the land drop unused in its own turn before the end step).
* **murktide delve best**: of the Murktides cast, the share that exiled as many instants and
  sorceries as it could (min(5, those in its graveyard)).
* **fow pitched fow**: of the Force of Will pitch payments that offered a second Force of Will AND
  another blue card, the share that pitched the Force of Will.
* **tap-out into Daze**: of the spells cast in the caster's own main phase (empty stack, turn >= 3,
  free spells excluded) while the opponent - at its first decision after the cast - held Daze and an
  Island, the share with no untapped land left (Wasteland and uncracked fetches count as mana);
  `tapped out: dazed` = of those, the share actually Dazed.
* **T1-2 Volcanic, U only**: of the fetch searches in the fetcher's own turns 1-2 with the basic Island
  still in its library, whose turn then cast only non-red spells, the share that took Volcanic Island
  (`... nothing cast`: the turn cast nothing more).
* **mulligans**: opening sevens, keep rate by lands and play / draw, the network's mean prior on
  Mulligan and how often the search visited it.

Fixed against the review's scripts: their turn 1-2 was global turns 1-2 and read the Island's zone
after the fetch had found it (a found Island never counted as "in the library": the Volcanic share was
100% by construction); the tap-out count ignored Wasteland and uncracked fetches and read the state
one step after the cast (mana payment not always finished); Murktide's delve skipped countered casts;
the Brainstorm shuffle needed the main phase (most Brainstorms are cast in the upkeep or draw step).

What it says: the line cracks fetches at once ~90% of the time and so almost never has a shuffle for its
Brainstorm (11-16%, never in response to a fetch); it pitches a second Force of Will over another blue
card 56-91% of the time; it taps out into a live Daze about half the time and is Dazed about half of
those; it takes Volcanic Island over the basic on its first two turns when only blue was needed 60-83%;
it keeps nearly every seven with 2+ lands (85-100%) and 54-92% of one-landers; Murktide's delve leaves
an instant or sorcery behind in about a third of the casts. None of these moves across the 106
generations beyond the noise of a few dozen games a band (n in each cell): the review's reading of a
behavioural plateau holds. The fingerprints are descriptive (a Volcanic Island fetch can be right);
their use is to see a change after a fix or a new training setting.

### 73.6 The A/B driver (`runs/ab-r3/ab_driver.py`, not edited here)

The driver (read-only here) builds `python -m mtgz.az.h2h FORK CONTROL --games 600 --sims 32 --spec S
--device cuda --threads 8 --seed 7 --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3 --b-cq-c-scale
0.3` (+ the leaf views) and adopts the fork at `a_score >= 0.5 + 2 se`. To use paired + sequential
games, change two places:

1. `h2h()`, the command (lines 157-158):

   ```python
   cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'mtgz.az.h2h', a, b, '--games', str(games), '--sims', '32',
          '--spec', spec, '--device', 'cuda', '--threads', '8', '--seed', '7',
          '--chance-k', '0', '--paired', '--sprt', '0,20', '--max-games', str(4 * games)] + H2H_SELECT
   ```

   (`games` = ab_config's `h2h_games` 600: batches of 600, at most 2,400; `--chance-k 0` is the run's
   own evaluation setting - h2h's default 2 is what hit both engine panics, 73.8; drop it to keep
   round 3's searches.)
2. `main()`, the verdict (lines 264-268):

   ```python
   score = r.get('score', r.get('a_score'))
   se = r.get('se', r.get('a_se', 0.0))
   sprt = r.get('sprt') or {}
   win = sprt.get('decision') == 'H1' if sprt else (score is not None and score >= 0.5 + 2 * se)
   new_main = fork if win else main_run
   verdict = ('FORK WINS' if win else 'control kept' + (' (undecided)' if sprt.get('decision') == 'undecided' else '')) \
       + (f' (score {score:.3f} ± {se:.3f}, {r.get("games")} games, llr {sprt.get("llr")})' if score is not None else '')
   ```

   and `write_results`' method line (line 179, 'The fork wins at score >= 0.5 + 2 se.') to 'Paired
   games (each deal from both seats); the fork wins when the SPRT of +20 Elo against 0 (alpha = beta =
   0.05) accepts +20 within 2,400 games; undecided = control kept.'

The minimal change is `'--paired'` alone in the command: the old rule then reads the paired se (`se`)
unchanged - the same bar with the variance of 73.3. The subprocess timeout (4 h) covers 2,400 games on
the GPU (600 games took 19 min in round 3). An undecided SPRT means |effect| below ~15 Elo after
2,400 games: the user's "principled fix" adoptions remain a judgement call on `a_score` +- `se`.

options, and Barrowgoyf's mill shuffled by Blightsteel Colossus between its cards - cube cards both:
these h2hs, given no `--spec`, played the cube spec, not the Delver mirror, 74's preamble.)

The variance measurement's first runs used h2h's default `chance_k` 2 (the A/B driver's too) and
all three died on an engine panic inside a search (`search worker panicked`; the driver then fails

| run (Mac, checkpoints 196 vs 188, 32 sims, the line's evaluation seats) | game | panic |
|---|---|---|
| `--paired --seed 7`, 600 games | 37 | `ChooseGraveyardCard: duplicate action ids [Opt { action: 0, choice: Pass }, Opt { action: 347, choice: Card(CardIdx(8)) }, Opt { action: 350, choice: Card(CardIdx(14)) }, Opt { action: 350, choice: Card(CardIdx(14)) }, Opt { action: 352, choice: Card(CardIdx(24)) }]` (engine/src/flow.rs:215) |
| `--seed 7` (unpaired), 600 games | 510 | `a card with another face` (an `other_face(..).expect`: engine/src/faces.rs:388 / 510, flow.rs:689) |
| `--paired --seed 8`, 600 games | 138 | `a card with another face` |

The first reproduces on the desktop CPU, the same game and message (`python -m mtgz.az.h2h
E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/r3/models/iter_0196.pt E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/r3/models/iter_0188.pt
--games 38 --sims 32 --paired --seed 7`, the line's config.json next to models/: ~10 min on 6
threads), so it is deterministic and not the Mac's. Neither is this branch's (no engine change; the
unpaired run's driver is byte for byte the old one). Both happen in a search's simulation, i.e.
in a sampled world, and look like section 49.6's class (a world inconsistent with a choice in
progress: a graveyard card listed twice by a delve; a card dealt without the face a decision names -
Tamiyo // Seasoned Scholar is the deck's double-faced card). The suspect is `chance_k` 2's forced

`chance_k` 0 (config.json) and its Elo matches never hit them, and the measurement's six batches at

triage's job, with the reproduction above); until then an h2h of these checkpoints should pass

## 74. The two engine panics of h2h's `chance_k` 2 (73.8): a Citadel look after its options, a mill that was not one action

Branch `chance-panics` (from main f52c0bb). Section 73.8's two panics, both in a search's simulation of
`python -m mtgz.az.h2h` at its default `chance_k` 2, both reproduced, both caused by the same mechanism
meeting an older engine flaw: zero-core's `chance_k` replays (`force_chance`) an outcome recorded in
another world of the same node, and the engine's forced draw / look / reveal swaps the recorded
identity into the card about to be seen (section 10's `force_chance`). That is sound only when nothing
already depends on the card's identity, and in two places something did. Each is fixed at that place,
with tests that fail on main (and identically at d0b62b1 and 6f871ac: 74.4).

**The games were cube games, not the Delver mirror.** `zero.h2h` plays the game package's spec unless
`--spec` is given (its module docs), and `mtgz`'s `mtg` spec is the cube's
(`{"max_turns": 60, "eval_decks": 16, "eval_seed": 1}`: random cube decks every game). The measurement's
jobs (73.3's batches, `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/mac_jobs*.sh`, the Mac's `~/mtgz-measure/jobs*.sh`)
passed no `--spec`: checkpoints of the Delver line played random cube decks - the paired seed-7 game's
log holds Barrowgoyf, Griselbrand, Blightsteel Colossus, Formidable Speaker, Emperor of Bones, none in
the Delver 60, and the faces panics need Bolas's Citadel (74.1), not in it either. 73.3's numbers
(the variance ratio, the scores) are therefore of cube games, not of the mirror the text names; the
A/B driver's h2h passes the Delver spec (`runs/ab-r3/ab_driver.py`, `--spec`), so round 3's
adoptions are of the mirror. This is also why round 3's h2hs at `chance_k` 2 on 6f871ac and d0b62b1
never died: the two cards involved (Citadel; Blightsteel with a mill that names its cards) are not in
the Delver deck.

### 74.1 "a card with another face": Bolas's Citadel's look came after the options it shapes

**The panic.** `faces.rs:510` (`choose_face`, "the other face" answered: paired seed 8, game 138) and
`flow.rs:689` (Priority's `CastFace`: unpaired seed 7, game 510), both an `other_face(..).expect`.

**Cause.** With Bolas's Citadel its controller may cast or play the top card of their library, so
Priority's options name that card by what it is (`top_options`: cast it, play it, its faces -
`Faces(card, mask)` when both of an MDFC's or an Adventure's faces can be cast). Its controller "looks at
it any time": `Game::look_tops`, run at the end of `advance` - **after** the pending decision was
computed. Without a forced outcome that order is harmless (the look learns the card, it changes
nothing). With one, the look's `force_library_card` swaps the recorded identity in **after** the
options were computed from the old one. In the test's two worlds (below): the replaying world's top
card was a Brazen Borrower, the options offered its face choice (`LIBRARY` + 0), the forced look made it
a Lightning Bolt - the recorded world's card -, the legal actions were the same ids (the same node), the
search walked `LIBRARY` + 0, the face choice asked for "the other face" of a Bolt: the panic, with the
h2h's message at the h2h's line; a `CastFace` option (only the other face castable) panics at
`flow.rs:689` the same way. The same stale option
as a cast gives the other failures the chance fuzz found (74.3): "no legal target for a required
target" (a Force of Negation's cast offered for what had been a castable card), "cast Forest".

**Introduced** by a2fa790 (2026-10-24, M7d: the Citadel, "keyed and forced like any look"), the first
commit with the look; neither of 73.8's builds' window.

**Fix** (`flow.rs`). `priority_ask` looks (`look_tops`) before computing its options: the forced
identity is in place when the options are made, and the replaying world's decision is the recorded
one's (the same options for the same card). `advance`'s look stays for every other decision; no other
decision's options read a top card its controller has not looked at (`top_options` is Priority's
alone), and debug builds now check it: when `advance`'s look swaps an identity, the decision refreshed
in a clone must equal the pending one (`look_tops` reports a swap). Real play (no queued outcome) is
unchanged but for the keys: the Citadel controller's `KEY_LOOK` is now emitted before a Priority the
engine answers (`KEY_AUTO`, one option) instead of at the next decision, and a top card that changes
before that decision is looked at too (74.6).

**Tests** (`engine/tests/rules_chance.rs`, the search's two worlds - the recorded one and the replaying
one, its keys forced - on real cards): `a_forced_look_at_the_citadels_top_card_comes_before_the_options`
(the Borrower made a Bolt: the same actions, `LIBRARY` + 0 casts the Bolt, which resolves; on main the
walk panics `faces.rs:510` "a card with another face", the h2h's message),
`a_forced_look_at_the_citadels_top_card_leaves_no_stale_cast` (a Bolt made a Forest: no option for the
top card, as in the recorded world; on main "340=cast Forest#3").

### 74.2 "ChooseGraveyardCard: duplicate action ids": a mill shuffled its library between its cards

**The game** (paired seed 7, game 37, reproduced with the game log - the spec's `"log": true`):
Barrowgoyf deals 7 combat damage, "you may mill that many cards. If you do, you may put a creature
card from among them into your hand" (`Ext::MayMillThenTakeCreature`). The second card milled is
Blightsteel Colossus: "if it would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, reveal it and shuffle it into
its owner's library instead".

**Cause.** The mill moved its cards one at a time from the top, and the Colossus's replacement
shuffled the library **at once** (`shuffle_in_instead`): the cards milled after it came from the
shuffled library, and the mill's pile (the cards "among them") kept the Colossus's card although it
went back. In the search's replaying world each forced reveal makes the top card the one the recorded
world milled there; after the shuffle the Colossus's card came to the top again, unknown to everyone
(the shuffle's cloud), and the queued reveal made it a Griselbrand - a legitimate swap with a
Griselbrand elsewhere in the library, unknown too, in the same cloud - which was milled: the pile held
card 14 twice, and "a creature card from among them" offered it twice. Two flaws: the mill was not one action (CR 701.13a:
the top N cards are put into the graveyard together; a replacement that shuffles one of them into the
library does so as part of that event, not between its cards), and the pile counted a card that never
reached the graveyard.

**Not only the search's.** At `chance_k` 0 the duplicate cannot happen (no forced reveal, the
Colossus's card stays a Colossus and goes back each time), but the rules bug does, in real games: any
mill that reaches a Blightsteel Colossus before its last card milled the rest from a shuffled library
(cards that were not among the top N, possibly the Colossus again). Cube pools only (the Colossus is not
in the Delver deck, which mills nothing).

**Introduced** by 302a05f (2026-10-24, Blightsteel Colossus's shuffle-instead) on b7fc16d's mill
(2026-10-22, Barrowgoyf, its milled cards forced and revealed); neither of 73.8's builds' window.

**Fix** (`game.rs`). `Game::mill(p, n, forced)`: the top `n` cards together - each (with `forced`) given
its queued outcome and revealed, then moved with `pile_moving` set, so a shuffle-instead replacement
leaves its card where it is and the library is shuffled once all `n` have moved (`flush_pile_shuffles`,
the mechanism a looked-at pile's surveil already used: section 51). It returns the cards milled; every
mill loop of the engine uses it: `Ext::Mill`, `MillTwoWhileShareColor`, `MayMillThenTakeCreature` (its
pile is the cards put into the graveyard), `MillAttackPump`, `LetDrawElseMill`, `MillThenLandToHand`;
which of them force is as before (the two that did).

**Tests.** `a_mill_takes_the_top_cards_together_and_shuffles_blightsteel_in_after_cr_701_13a`
(Barrowgoyf's mill of 2 over the Colossus and a Test Bear, 24 shuffle seeds: the Bear milled every time,
the Colossus in the library, offered once; on main the second card came from the shuffled library),
`a_replayed_mill_offers_each_milled_card_once` (256 pairs of worlds, the second replaying the first's
keys: the same keys, the Bear offered once; on main one replay panics in `ask`, "ChooseGraveyardCard:
duplicate action ids", the h2h's message).

### 74.3 The chance-node fuzz (`FUZZ_CHANCE=n`)

`engine/tests/fuzz.rs` had no forced outcome anywhere: random play never replays a key, and section 10's
`force_chance` checks (tests/az.rs) replay single transitions of mid-game states. `FUZZ_CHANCE=n`
(one decision in `n`, its own generator; the games are the same with or without it) runs a **chance
walk**: two worlds of the decider, each dealt as a simulation's (uniform or, one time in two, by random
weights: the belief-weighted search), walk one random path while they are at one node of the tree
(the same next decider and legal actions, equal keys so far); at each step one world takes the action
freely and the other replays its keys (`force_chance` for the whole search transition, single-option
decisions answered, as `tree::transition` does), the roles swapping at random; a replaying world whose
keys or next actions differ is in another node, and plays on alone for 20 steps. After every step
both worlds' invariants and knowledge hold and the legal actions are sorted and unique; every option
of the replaying world's decision completes whenever the force changed its outcome (one time in four
otherwise); a panic is reported with the walk's path and its forced keys. It prints the walks, their
steps at one node, the replays whose outcome the force changed (the replaying world, unforced, would
have had other keys) and the walks split by the keys; with 100 games or more some replay must have
taken a forced outcome. Games only (the h2h's games are best-of-one).

Found on main (release, `FUZZ_CHANCE=2`): the first failure of each 1,000-seed chunk of the interactions
pool's seeds 0-2,999 - 81, 1238 and 2304, all 74.1's class (a stale Citadel cast, "no legal target for a
required target": Force of Negation, Invert Polarity; the completion check reached it before the walk's
random step); the walk's first version (it stopped at a split) found 81 and nothing in 6,000 default-pool
and 2,000 Delver games. On this branch those seeds pass.

**Not fixed here.** Interactions seed 523 (`FUZZ_POOL=interactions FUZZ_CHANCE=2 FUZZ_FIRST=523
FUZZ_GAMES=1`): a Toxic Deluge cast from the Citadel's top under Thalia, Guardian of Thraben, the X life
option 5 offered and then "PayMana: no way to pay {1}" - the farm's `PayMana` bucket (its config's
`expected`), a cost check that disagrees with the payment, reached in a forced world but not caused by
the force (the state is an ordinary legal one). Not in the default or Delver pools.

### 74.5 Found by the fuzz: Urza's Bauble's look beside a known twin

The Delver pool's seed 16246 (`FUZZ_POOL=delver FUZZ_FIRST=16246 FUZZ_GAMES=1 cargo test --profile fuzz -p
engine --test fuzz fuzz_random_games`, with or without `FUZZ_CHANCE`: the information-set check of a
checkpoint, not the walk): `same keys, different views` of the player whose Urza's Bauble looked at a card
at random in the other's hand. That player already knew one card of the hand, and the look marked the
card seen as known (`learn`) - in a world where it saw the other copy of that identity, it now "knew" two;
where it saw the known one, one. A hand's cards are not told apart (section 10), so seeing "a Lightning
Bolt" beside the Bolt already known says nothing new: the two worlds were one node (the same
public key) with different knowledge, encodings and searches. **Cause**: the look's knowledge, older than
71.1 (which keyed the look public for the owner; the looker's own key was always its own). **Fix**
(`Ext::LookAtRandomHandCard`): no card is learned when the looker already knows another card of that
hand with the identity seen. **Who**: every pool with Urza's Bauble, the Delver mirror included (one in
the 60): a search of the looker with a card of the other's hand already known (an earlier look, an
Island returned by Daze) merged worlds that knew one or two copies. A search-quality fix; no network input or
layout change. **Test**: `a_random_look_at_a_twin_of_a_known_card_knows_no_more_than_one` (48 worlds of
the looker, a known Bolt and a second one in the hand: equal keys, equal views, one Bolt known whenever
a Bolt was seen; fails on 38a0fa1, i.e. main's look).

## 76. The position lab: a real spot, each candidate played to the end (`start`, `tools/position_lab.py`)

Branch `position-lab` (from main 5f7e427; section 75 is the `explore` branch's, not merged here). The
user approved it on 2026-10-31 as a way to check their judgement about the network's play - take a spot
from a real game, and for each candidate play, play a few hundred games to the end from there with the
network on both sides, every candidate on the same hidden-card deals - and later perhaps to teach the
network a trick. The first demo is measure-play's finding (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure-play/`,
report.json): the network never Baubles its own library before cracking a fetchland (0 looks before
203 / 627 / 336 cracks with a Bauble castable), and 14 +- 2% of the cracks with a Bauble available fetched
a land that stayed untapped that turn (31 spots in the 222 recent replays, gen >= 240). Was the look
worth anything? Two later additions (the coordinator, user-approved): the same spots searched deeply at
`chance_k` 0 and 8 (76.6), and the canonical turn-1 position built from game seeds (76.7).

### 76.1 The `start` block (`engine/src/az/lab.rs`)

A game-spec extension, chosen over a Python driver because zero-core's match driver then plays these
games batched, seeded and paired like any other, and the same mechanism can seed self-play later: an
optional `start` object in the `mtg` spec (`MtgSpec::start`; `new_game` -> `MtgAz::from_start`). Without
it nothing changes: `MtgSpec::parse` of every existing spec is what it was, `MtgAz::lab` is `None`,
`legal_actions` and `step` take their old path (one `is_none` test), the spectator view has no `lab`
field; the digests and the network's play are byte-identical (76.10).

```json
"start": {"seed": 889364660, "actions": [384, 0, 97], "deal": "belief", "deal_seed": 7,
          "pred": [... 1024 floats ...], "tilt": 1, "clip": 20, "mix": 0.25,
          "hold": ["Daze"], "exclude": [], "top": [["Brainstorm"], []], "top_known": true, "tries": 100000,
          "forced": ["Cast Mishra's Bauble", "resolve", "Activate Mishra's Bauble", "Target P2", "resolve"],
          "follow": {"rule": "bauble_fetch", "land_min": 4, "fetches": ["Flooded Strand", "..."],
                     "bad": ["..."], "good": ["..."]}}
```

* **The spot.** The source game is `MtgAz::new` of the same spec without `start`, game seed `seed`;
  `actions` are taken in order, each after the single-option decisions before it are auto-stepped (as
  zero-core's transitions and a replay's frames have them: `tools/root_view.py`'s `rebuild`), and the
  single-option decisions after the last too. An action the source game does not offer is an error naming
  its index. The player to move there is the decider (`viewer` overrides). A replay's frame k is the spot
  of its first k frames' actions; the rebuilt spot's spectator state, log included, equals the replay's
  stored state for frame k (every demo spot; every tenth frame of the last three main-line replays in the
  tests).
* **The deal** (`deal`), from its own stream - `split64(deal_seed ^ salt)`, the deal seed given (else the
  driver's game seed): two games with the same deal seed deal the same world whatever their candidate and
  gid (the pairing).
  * `belief` (the default): `MtgAz::determinize_belief` for the decider with the network's prediction
    `pred` (the `belief` aux target's 1,024 floats, `MtgAz::AUX` order) - exactly the search's world
    (ENGINE.md 69): everything the decider cannot see dealt again, the opponent's hand by the belief's
    weights, tilted and clipped; a share `mix` of the deals uniform, one `unit()` draw per deal when mix > 0,
    as zero-core's tree draws it. The lab passes the run's evaluation settings (tilt 1, clip 20, mix 0.25)
    and the head's prediction at the spot for the decider (`encode(decider)` as a root belief row: what the
    search's own root asks). The decider's own unknown library order is dealt again too.
  * `uniform`: `determinize` for the decider (for comparison).
  * `actual`: `Game::redeal_unknown_library_orders` (hidden.rs): every card stays where it is - both hands,
    every card some player knows exactly - but the library cards nobody knows, whose identities are
    shuffled among themselves within each group of library cards every cloud treats alike (the same
    membership in each cloud's domain, as `force_library_card` swaps), so each cloud's identities stay in
    its domain; the state's stream is reseeded. The opponent's real hand: a hindsight check.
  * `none`: the source game itself, its stream continuing (tests, building).

  `hold` (a multiset of names) / `exclude` (names): the opponent's hand must hold at least these and none
  of those; `top` ([[P1's], [P2's]] names, top first): each library starts so, and with `top_known` its
  owner knows those cards (as after a Brainstorm's put-back). All three **condition** the belief (or
  uniform) deal by rejection: deals are drawn from the same stream until one fits (at most `tries`, default
  100,000), so a pinned deal is the belief's distribution restricted to the worlds that fit (a held Force
  of Will makes two more likely than the belief alone would, as Bayes says). A pin no world can hold - more
  held cards than the hand has, or than the decider's unknown pool and its known hand cards offer - is an
  error at once. Every deal ends with `Game::check_knowledge` (an error, never a silent world) and without
  determinize's observer (`after_deal` sets it to mask later private keys; the dealt world is a real game
  from here).
* **The forced line** (`forced`): the decider's next non-minor decisions (not `PayMana` / `PayPool`) take
  these options in order: an option label (`view.rs`'s `option_text`, now `pub(crate)`), an action id,
  `"*"` (the network's own choice there), or `"resolve"`: pass whenever the decider has priority with
  something on the stack, the network answering any other question on the way (a trigger's surveil, a
  Daze's tax), done at the first decision with an empty stack, whoever's - the next item applies at the
  decider's next decision. `legal_actions` offers that option alone, so zero-core's driver steps it without
  a search (no sample, no tree); `step` moves the line on. When the next item is not among the options (the
  opponent's answer changed the decision) the line is broken (`Lab::broken`): the network plays on from
  there, and the follow rule never starts. **A label that names two options is an error** (at the spot when
  the game starts, later in `step`: give the action id) - two "Activate Clue", two "Target Volcanic
  Island" are common. Two lessons on the way: a first version's `"Pass priority"` after the Bauble broke
  the line whenever a trigger sat above it (a Dragon's Rage Channeler's surveil, a Cori-Steel Cutter's
  Monk: 2 of the first 8 demo spots), hence `"resolve"`; and the engine asks no decision whose only option
  is a pass, so `"resolve"` cannot wait for the decider's own empty-stack priority (after Tamiyo resolves
  on turn 1 with nothing else to do it never comes - a trailing `"resolve"` then stayed pending into the
  opponent's turn and forced passes there; found by the turn-1 lines' scripted check, fixed before their
  play-outs).
* **The follow rule** `bauble_fetch` (`follow`; one rule): at the decider's first decision after the line,
  if it knows its library's top card (a Mishra's Bauble look resolved) the rule holds while that card stays
  its known top card. The card is **bad** if it is a land and the decider has at least `land_min` lands
  (battlefield + hand, the fetches included): its next priority with an option to activate one of
  `fetches` activates it (the lowest action id) and the rule ends. Else it is **good**: the decider
  activates no fetch of its own accord (an empty stack or its own item on top) until the card is drawn or
  moved; in answer to the opponent's spell or ability (a Daze's tax, a Wasteland) the network decides, and
  a crack there ends the rule. With `bad` / `good` (forced lines) the verdict's line continues the forced
  line from that decision first - a branch ("a land seen: play the fetch, crack it, cast Tamiyo; else play
  the Island, cast Tamiyo"), the rule as above after it. With no known top card at that decision (the look
  was answered) the rule ends. The rule reads the true identity of a card the decider knows - no leak.
* **The line and the rule are game state** (`MtgAz::lab`, cloned with the game): the searches' worlds keep
  them, so the root decision is the same in every world of the decider's (zero-core checks it; the rule's
  verdict reads the decider's own known card, which `determinize` keeps). The opponent's search sees the
  decider's scripted moves too - a small leak (it "knows" the decider will activate the Bauble, or will not
  crack this turn; in its worlds the decider's top card is dealt again, so it does not know the verdict's
  card). Clearing them in search worlds would change the root decision (the driver's error) and model a
  decider who might not follow its own script. A lab game's spectator view has a `lab` field: the line's
  state, the rule's, the seen card and both libraries top first (diagnostics, the tests).

Best-of-one only (`start` with `"seed"` or `"format": "bo3"` is an error).

### 76.2 `tools/position_lab.py`, and its API

```
python tools/position_lab.py spot   --model M (--replay R --frame N | --site-id ID --frame N | --record F[:i])
                                    [--modes belief,actual,pinned --hold X --exclude Y] [--top-k 3] [--cand ...]
python tools/position_lab.py bauble --model M --record spots.jsonl [--land-min 4] [--deep-sims 800 ...]
python tools/position_lab.py t1     --model M [--seeds 1-60000 --spots 4 | --scenario S.json ...] [--draw] [--one-ply 300]
python tools/position_lab.py canary [--replays DIR] [--selfplay fp_*.json ...] [--out F]
python tools/position_lab.py show   --report R.json
```

* **Spots**: a zero-replay/1 file and a frame (the state before that frame's move; the game seed from the
  replay's seed and game index as zero.replay derives it); a site replay id, mapped to the local file the
  publisher saved by its log (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/delverai-publish.log`: each "recording N games of
  iteration I (checkpoint)" block's "uploaded ... id" lines in game order, the file
  `<run>/replays/*-<recorded HHMMSS>_<game>.json.gz` whose title is "Generation I"; the site is not asked);
  a position record (`{"replay" | "file", "frame" | "k"}`, a JSON line - measure-play's frame index `k`); a
  scenario (`position-lab/1` JSON: `save_scenario` / `load_scenario`, the lab's own format for built
  positions); or an opening built from a game seed (76.7). Every spot is rebuilt and checked against its
  stored state first (a mismatch is an error).
* **The network's view** at the spot: the prior per option and the value, the belief's expected opponent
  hand (n x the head's distribution) beside the real one, and `--view-reps` (4) searches of `--view-sims`
  (64) simulations with the run's evaluation seat (`zero.h2h.run_rule` of the checkpoint's run: the cq rule
  with its guard 4 and scale 0.3, root-view leaf values, the root belief at tilt 1 / mix 0.25): mean visits
  and Q per option, the rule's moves; per mode, the share of the played deals in which the opponent holds
  each card (the uniform deal beside them). The deep view (`--deep-sims`, 76.6): seeds x settings of a
  large search (`chance_k`, a root floor of visits).
* **Candidates**: the network's `--top-k` options by prior, `--cand` (a label, a ';'-separated forced
  sequence, or a JSON object with `forced` and / or `follow`); `bauble` and `t1` build their demos'
  candidates; a deep setting's pick joins them (forced alone, the network on) unless it already is one.
  Every candidate's start game is built at the spot before any play-out (an ambiguous or unknown first
  label: an error there).
* **Play-outs**: both seats the checkpoint at the run's evaluation search (`--sims`, default 32;
  `chance_k` 0, c_puct 1). One zero-core driver per (spot, candidate, mode) - a rolling `queue_only` driver
  (search.md 2.9: a classic driver starts its first games with the driver's spec at construction, before
  anything is queued) with one queued setup per deal i, the deal seed of deal i the same for every
  candidate and mode of the spot; every candidate's driver has the same seed and queue order, so its game
  gid is the other candidates' game gid: the same deal and the same search streams, which part where the
  games do. The drivers run in `--procs` worker processes (`--threads` torch threads - 2: 4 gain nothing on
  this network -, `--search-threads`, below-normal priority, CPU only: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` is set
  before torch is imported), mode-major (the first mode complete for every spot first). `move_log` 150
  lets each game of a forced line be replayed afterwards (`diagnose`: did the line hold, what the Bauble
  showed, the rule's verdict, whether the network cracked a fetch while the seen card was still on top).
  `--cache DIR` keeps each finished job's games and each deep view (a job is reused only when everything it
  depends on - the spot, the start block, the seat, the checkpoint's sha256 - is the same): a stopped lab
  resumes; `--cached-only` reports what is there; `--play-cands` plays some candidates only (beside a
  running lab).
* **Report** (JSON + a text table): per spot, mode and candidate the score from the decider's seat (a win
  1, a draw 0.5) +- its se, the difference to the best candidate and to the first (the actual play) +- the
  **paired** se (the sd of the per-deal differences / sqrt(n)), games, the mean final turn and turns played
  from the spot, the per-deal results; pooled over spots (equal weight: the mean of the spots' mean
  differences, its se stratified by spot).
* **The API** (the CLI's own functions, `import position_lab as L`; the lab UI at
  `C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/delver-lab` builds on it): `build_position` (a replay + frame, a site id, a
  record, a scenario or an opening seed), `save_scenario` / `load_scenario`, `search_params` +
  `evaluate_position` (prior, value, searches with explicit settings - sims, chance_k, c_puct, the root
  belief, the leaf view, a root floor, the rule, seeds -; results keyed by action id, the label a display
  field: two options may share one), `sweep` (a grid of them), `play_out` (candidates from a position in
  one deal mode, `progress(done, total)` and `cancel()` callbacks), `opening_spot` / `opening_spot_draw`,
  `one_ply_t1`, `t1_canary`, `run_lab` (the whole lab).

### 76.3 What a lab game is, and is not

* **A real game from a dealt world.** From the deal on, both seats play the network at the run's
  evaluation search; each search determinizes from its own player's view as in any game. In `belief` and
  `pinned` the opponent's hand is one the decider's belief finds plausible: the opponent "knows" it (its
  known bits stay on its hand's slots); its past play was its real hand's, and the belief head's read of
  that past is exactly what weights the deal (ENGINE.md 66, 69).
* **The scripted lines leak to the opponent's searches** (76.1): its tree models the decider as following
  its script. For the demos' lines this is the Bauble's activation and target and, under the rule, "no
  fetch of the decider's own accord while the seen card is on top" - which the opponent's worlds evaluate on
  their own dealt top card, so it does not learn the seen card.
* **The rule is a script, not a player**: it reads one card and a land count. It cracks at once when the
  card is bad and holds otherwise until the card is drawn, but lets the network answer the opponent - and
  the network uses that to crack anyway (76.5).
* **The play-outs are the network against itself**: a candidate's score is "what this network wins from
  here after that move". A move the network cannot follow up scores low for that reason; (b) against (c)
  separates the move from the network's follow-up.

### 76.4 Tests

* `engine/tests/lab.rs` (13): a spec without `start` is the spec of before (`new_game` = `MtgAz::new`, the
  same legal actions and spectator states for 400 random moves, no `lab` field); the block's checks; the
  spot is the source game after its actions (deal `none`; an action the game does not offer is an error
  naming its index); `actual` keeps everything a spectator sees and every known library card (12 deal seeds,
  >= 20 distinct library orders, `check_knowledge`); deals paired by the deal seed whatever the forced line
  or the game seed; held cards in every dealt hand, excluded ones in none, an impossible pin an error; the
  belief deal toward a constructed prediction (Force of Will 0.5 of the hand: uniform < mix 0.5 < belief,
  belief > 1.8 x uniform); the forced line and `bauble_fetch` on a random game's Bauble + fetch spot (a land
  forcing the crack and ending the rule, a spell masking every crack, the decider's own worlds offering the
  same options, both verdicts seen, a missing label breaking the line); the branch (`bad` / `good` lines);
  `resolve` passing until the stack is empty; an ambiguous label an error, its action id fine; `top` pins
  (the cards on top, known to their owner); lab games played to the end by random play.
* `tests/test_position_lab.py` (15): the rebuilt spot matches the replay frame (a recorder-shaped random
  game; a changed state an error) and every tenth frame of the last three main-line replays; paired deals
  identical across four candidates (both hands, both libraries); `actual` keeps the hands and re-deals the
  decider's library order; pins; belief toward a constructed prediction; no start block = the same game
  move for move; forced lines through zero-core's driver (queued setups, every row tagged, the line's option
  alone, deals paired; `UniformEvaluator`); deal summaries; paired summaries; spot-stratified pooling; site
  ids through a publisher log; candidate parsing; the turn-1 compositions, the opening spot and scenarios;
  the canary reading a scripted Bauble look.

### 76.5 The first demo: Mishra's Bauble before the crack, at replay spots

**The spots** (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/position-lab/bauble_spots.jsonl`): measure-play's 31 "fetched land
unused that turn, Bauble available" cracks in the main line's replays of generation >= 240
(`raw_replay.jsonl`'s fetch activations with a Bauble castable or on the battlefield, no own look that
turn, the fetched land untapped for the rest of the turn; all 31 in the cracker's own first main phase with
an empty stack), rebuilt: **in 8 of the 31 the decider already knew its library's top card** (a
Brainstorm's or a surveil's put-back: Unholy Heat, Force of Will twice, Daze, Volcanic Island twice,
Thundering Falls twice - the card is the same in every deal of its library), so a Bauble look there tells
it nothing and measure-play's 14% overstates the spots the trick applies to (23 of 31: 10.5 +- 2% of the
cracks); and 4 of those 8 shuffled away a known *good* card (Unholy Heat, Force of Will twice, Daze) - the
same habit without the Bauble. The demo takes 8 of the 23 with an unknown top card: 5 with the Bauble in
hand (turns 1, 3, 6, 8, 11) and the 3 there are with it on the battlefield (turns 3, 8, 14); 8 games,
generations 240-308. Each is the frame where the network chose "Activate <fetch>".

**The candidates** (`position_lab.py bauble`): (a) the actual play, the crack; (b) the Bauble at the
decider's own library first - `Cast Mishra's Bauble`, `resolve` when it is in hand, then `Activate Mishra's
Bauble`, `Target P<decider>`, `resolve` - and the network on from the decision after the look; (c) the
same line with `bauble_fetch` at `land_min` 4 (crack iff the seen card is a land and the decider has >= 4
lands in play + hand, else hold the fetch until the card is drawn). (At the 4 earliest spots no deal gives
4 lands, so there (c) is "Bauble, then hold the fetch until the seen card is drawn" whatever it was.)

**The run**: checkpoint 308 of r3-2b-beliefsearch (a read-only copy with its run's config.json:
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/position-lab/run/`) on both seats at the run's evaluation search (32 simulations; cq
rule, guard 4, scale 0.3; root-view leaves; root belief tilt 1 / mix 0.25); 200 deals per spot in `belief`
and `actual`, 100 in `pinned` with `--hold Daze` (the opponent holds a Daze: the line exposes a Bauble cast
from hand to it, and a held fetch is no mana for its tax - the most direct interaction with the trick; N
halved for CPU time, 76.9); 5 worker processes x 2 torch + 1 search threads, below-normal priority, CPU
only (the pinned run on 5 processes too). Every rebuilt spot equals its replay frame; every forced line
held in every game of every mode (the opponent never countered the Bauble, even holding a Daze).

**The deals differ from the uniform deal where the belief has something to read**: the share of deals in
which the opponent holds Force of Will is 0.47 against 0.245 uniform at the turn-8 spot `015056_000@70`,
0.305 against 0.185 at turn 14; Daze 0.415 against 0.155 at turn 11; at turn 1 (nothing seen yet) the two
are close (Tamiyo 0.445 against 0.47).

hand +0.004 +- 0.017 (Bauble first) and -0.001 +- 0.018 (+ the rule). **None is distinguishable from zero at +-0.012 pooled** (+-0.017 pinned; +-0.03-0.06
per spot): at these spots the look is worth at most ~2-3 points of win rate, and the network's habit of
cracking first costs little in its own games. Of the 72 per-spot comparisons (8 spots x 3 pairs x 3 modes)
one passes 2 paired se (the turn-1 spot's (c) - (b) with a Daze held, -0.120 +- 0.059) and four more reach
1.8-2.0 (both signs) - about what chance gives.

**What the network does after a forced look** (`diagnose` over the move logs): in (b) it cracks a fetch
while the seen card is still on top in 24-100% of the games by spot and mode (100% at turn 1, 95-97% at
turns 3 and 8 with the Bauble on the battlefield, 50-84% at turns 3-8 from hand, 24-60% at turns 11-14) - it
seldom keeps a card it saw, whatever it was (measure-play's cf probe saw the same: 65% after a good card,
89% after an excess land); in (c) the script holds, but the network still cracks "in answer" to an
opponent's spell at one spot (turn 3 from hand: 68-93% of its games by mode), 0-27% elsewhere. The script's own verdicts at the late spots: bad 27-62 of 200
(cracked), and its bad and good branches score alike (e.g. 0.852 / 0.856 at turn 3, 0.113 / 0.116 at
turn 8).

### 76.6 Deep search at the same spots (`--deep-sims 800 --deep-k 0,8 --deep-floor 100`)

The question (the coordinator, user-approved, after a whole-game h2h of a gen-304 network at `chance_k` 4
against 0, 64 simulations, came out 0.490 +- 0.014): is searching hypothetical states further after a
hidden outcome a blind spot that a deeper search fixes here? At each spot, 8 seeds of 800 simulations
(the same seeds for every setting: paired searches) with the run's evaluation seat otherwise (cq rule,
guard 4, scale 0.3; root-view leaves; the root belief at tilt 1 / mix 0.25), at `chance_k` 8 and 0, and the
same two with a **root floor** of 100 visits per option (search.md 3.5's forced walks, at most half the
budget). Without the floor an option of prior ~0.0001 gets no visit at 800 simulations - the Bauble at 5
of the 8 spots, whatever `chance_k` (the PUCT term c P sqrt(N) / (1 + n) is ~0.003 there) - so its Q is

the crack; the turn-6 spot's "Pass priority, network on" +0.065 +- 0.035. Pooled over the 8 spots (a spot whose
deep pick is the crack contributes 0): the deep k=8 pick +0.006 +- 0.006, the deep k=0 pick +0.008 +- 0.004.

### 76.7 The second demo: the turn-1 Bauble position, built from game seeds (`position_lab.py t1`)

The user's canonical case, cleaner than the replay spots: on turn 1 our hand holds an Island-type land
(Island or Volcanic Island), a fetchland that can fetch it, Mishra's Bauble and Tamiyo, Inquisitive
Student. The expert line: cast the Bauble (free) and look at our own top card; a good card - play the
Island-type land and cast Tamiyo, keeping the fetch; a bad card - play the fetch, crack it (shuffling the
card away), fetch a blue land, cast Tamiyo. Tamiyo comes down on turn 1 either way, and the land choice
uses the information.

**The spots** are built without replays: `opening_spot(spec, seed)` plays a seed of the Delver mirror's
spec to the starting player's first main-phase priority (the chooser plays first, both keep their seven,
priority passes - only the shuffle and the deal, ~0.3 ms a seed); `t1_composition` keeps the **clean**
hands - exactly one Island-type land, one fetchland, one Mishra's Bauble, one Tamiyo, and three cards of
Force of Will, Daze, Cori-Steel Cutter, Murktide Regent, Prismari Charm (none castable on our turn 1;
Force of Will and Daze reactive only; no Dragon's Rage Channeler, Brainstorm, Ponder, Lightning Bolt,
Unholy Heat, second land, Urza's Bauble or second Mishra's Bauble). Seeds 1-24,006 hold 12 such hands on
the play (about 1 in 2,000); the demo takes four, two with each Island-type land: `seed1754` (Cori-Steel Cutter, Force of Will, Force of Will, Mishra's Bauble, Polluted Delta, Tamiyo, Volcanic Island); `seed2100` (Daze, Daze, Flooded Strand, Force of Will, Mishra's Bauble, Tamiyo, Volcanic Island); `seed19613` (Cori-Steel Cutter, Daze, Force of Will, Island, Mishra's Bauble, Misty Rainforest, Tamiyo); `seed20416` (Daze, Island, Mishra's Bauble, Murktide Regent, Murktide Regent, Polluted Delta, Tamiyo).
On the draw (views only - the network's view, the deep search, the one-ply check; no play-outs, for time) (`--draw`, `opening_spot_draw`): the second player's seven and its draw (its library's top
before the turn) filtered first (cheap), then the starting player's turn 1 played by the network's
evaluation search to the second player's first main phase, its eight cards filtered again; seeds
1-25,702 hold 6 (both demo spots' opponents played a land and Tamiyo on their turn 1): the demo views two of them, `seed2604d` (Daze, Flooded Strand, Force of Will, Mishra's Bauble, Murktide Regent, Prismari Charm, Tamiyo, Volcanic Island); `seed17385d` (Cori-Steel Cutter, Cori-Steel Cutter, Daze, Force of Will, Mishra's Bauble, Misty Rainforest, Tamiyo, Volcanic Island).
Each spot is kept as a scenario (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/position-lab/t1_spots/`); everything a player knows
is kept, and each play-out re-deals the unknown libraries (and, in `belief`, the opponent's hand), paired
across candidates.

**The candidates**: (a) the network's own play (`"*"`); (b) no Bauble: play the fetch, crack it, cast
Tamiyo (`[Play F, Activate F, resolve, Cast Tamiyo, resolve]` - the fetch's find is the network's); (c) no
Bauble: the Island-type land and Tamiyo, the fetch kept; (d) the Bauble at our own library first
(`[Cast Mishra's Bauble, resolve, Activate Mishra's Bauble, Target P<us>, resolve]`), then the network; (e)
the same with the branch rule (`bauble_fetch`, `land_min` 0, `bad` = (b)'s line, `good` = (c)'s: a land
seen - the fetch, cracked, Tamiyo; a nonland seen - the land, Tamiyo, the fetch kept); (f) the deep
searches' pick (800 simulations x 8 seeds at `chance_k` 8 and 0, with and without a floor of 100: 76.6's
settings), forced alone and the network on. Belief deals, 100 per spot (every candidate the same deals).

view) at the first decision after Tamiyo resolved (the opponent's turn 2 when we have nothing left to do).

of deals where "keep" is valued higher:
