**Reading it.**

* **The network's own play** on turn 1 is a land, never the Bauble: with a basic Island it plays the Island
  and keeps the fetch (prior 1.000 at both spots); with a Volcanic Island it plays the Volcanic Island
  beside a Flooded Strand (0.925) but plays the Polluted Delta beside a Volcanic Island (0.988) - a land
  choice that reads the hand, never the top card. The Bauble's prior is 0.000 at every spot.
* **Deep search does not find Bauble-first** here: at 800 simulations x 8 seeds its share is 0 at every spot
  and either `chance_k`; with the floor its Q is below the best land's at every spot (by 0.02-0.06 on the
  play, 0.013 and 0.077 on the draw) - above the fetch's at one (`seed20416`: 0.609 against 0.593) -,
  `chance_k` 8 against 0 moving it by at most 0.002. The deep picks are the 64-sim search's moves but on the
  draw at `seed2604d`, where k 8 splits 5 / 3 toward the Flooded Strand and k 0 4 / 4.
* **Played out**, the expert line (e) scores -0.033 +- 0.028 against the network's own play pooled over the four
  spots on the play, Bauble-first with the network's follow-up (d) -0.015 +- 0.027, and the two no-Bauble lines
  (b) +0.020 +- 0.027 and (c) +0.025 +- 0.024 - none beyond 1.3 paired se, at +-0.024-0.028 pooled (+-0.04-0.07 per
  spot, N = 100). The branch's own verdicts: a land seen in 24-38% of the looks, and its two branches score
  alike (e.g. 0.694 bad / 0.609 good at `seed1754`, 0.500 / 0.618 at `seed2100`).
* **The one-ply check: the value network alone leans the right way, weakly.** After a forced look it values
  "crack" above "keep" when a land was seen (keep preferred in 35-52% of the land deals by spot on the play,
  19-40% on the draw) and "keep" above "crack" when a spell was seen (58-69% on the play; 42-56% on the
  draw) - by card on the play strongest for a cantrip seen (Brainstorm 0.96-1.00, Ponder 0.80-0.87 keep), a
  Volcanic Island seen leaning crack (0.27-0.32), but a Wasteland seen leaning keep (0.68-0.86: the value net
  counts it a good card) and Lightning Bolt split (0.24-0.84); on the draw at `seed17385d` the classes hardly
  separate (40% / 42%) and a Volcanic Island seen leans keep (0.71). The mean value gaps are small (0.01-0.04), and casting
  the Bauble itself costs ~0.1 of value in the network's eyes at `seed1754` (0.605 at the spot, 0.509 after
  the cast, 0.48-0.54 after the look by the seen card) - a state the network almost never visits.

**In one line (the coordinator's question 3):** deeper search after the look (`chance_k` 8 at 800
simulations) does not find Bauble-first - with prior ~0 it is never searched, and forced into the tree it
still values below the land plays, `chance_k` changing nothing - and Bauble-first does not win more when
played out (replay spots: +0.004 +- 0.012 belief, -0.004 +- 0.012 actual, +0.004 +- 0.017 with a Daze held, pooled over 8 spots; turn 1: -0.015 +- 0.027 with the network's follow-up, -0.033 +- 0.028 with the expert branch, pooled over 4 spots); the value net's raw one-ply
preference after a look is in the expert's direction but small.

### 76.9 Cost

CPU only, below-normal priority, beside other agents' runs (the desktop's GPU and the Mac on the live A/B):
a play-out costs ~8 process-seconds per game from a mid-game spot (`--threads 2 --search-threads 1`: one
process ~1,050-1,800 network rows a second, about 1.3 cores - this network's CPU inference does not scale
past 2 torch threads, so the lab scales by processes), ~13.5 from turn 1 (16 turns to play). A job (one
spot, one candidate, one mode, 200 deals) took 685 s (turn 14) to 2,390 s (turn 1), typically 1,300-1,900
s; **a typical lab query** - one spot, three candidates, one mode, 200 deals - is ~600 games, about 25-40
minutes on 3-5 processes. The first demo's belief + actual runs: 10,000 games, 78,600 process-seconds,
~4.4 h on 5 processes; pinned (N halved to 100 for time) ~1.3 h; the turn-1 demo 2,400 games, 32,500
process-seconds, ~3 h on 3 processes; the deep searches ~50 s a spot (4 settings x 8 seeds x 800
simulations); the one-ply check ~5 s a spot (300 deals); the canary 3 s over 1,194 games. The spot search
over seeds: ~0.3 ms a seed on the play (24,006 seeds in 6 s for 12 clean hands), on the draw ~25 s for
80,000 seeds (a network search per hit).

### 76.11 Building an arbitrary position (an assessment, not built)

What it would take to start a lab game from a description - cards per zone from the two fixed 60-card
decks, tapped / counters, life, turn / step / active player, the known library top, the opponent's hand
known or unknown: `engine/src/testkit.rs`'s `Scenario` already builds a `Game` at a chosen step from card
names per zone (library in order, hand, `hand_known`, battlefield without summoning sickness, graveyard,
exile, counters, life, lands played, mana pool, turn number, active player, monarch, ...) and `start()`
runs the step's turn-based actions to the first decision. Missing for the lab: (1) a `start.build` JSON
schema feeding it, wrapped as an `MtgAz` (the match state from the spec, `set_known_pools`); (2) the deck
partition - best-of-one decklists are open, so every one of each deck's 60 cards must be placed (the rest
into the library, unknown), and the description checked against the list; (3) setters it lacks: tapped,
"entered this turn" (summoning sickness), per-turn history the rules and the encoding read (spells cast
this turn - Cori-Steel Cutter's flurry, prowess -, cards drawn, a declared mulligan, damage), a known
library top (`learn`) and partial knowledge (clouds - leave out); (4) the stack (start at an empty stack,
or build it by actions); (5) checks: `Game::check_invariants` and `check_knowledge`, the encoding's leak
tests on a built state, and a fuzz of built positions played to the end. About a day, mostly (2)-(3) and
their tests; the risk is states no game could reach (inconsistent per-turn counters), which the checks
reduce but do not rule out.

### 76.12 Risks, limits, open questions

* **The scripted lines leak to the opponent's searches** (76.3): small here; a candidate whose point is
  surprise (a bluff, a held counter) would be measured against an opponent that knows the script.
* **The score is the network's against itself**: a better move the network cannot follow up scores low;
  (c) / (e) against (b) / (d) isolate the follow-up for the Bauble. The script's "hold" lets the network
  answer the opponent - and it cracks then (76.5), so (c) is not a pure hold at every spot.
* **N and power**: N = 200 (100 pinned, 100 turn 1) gives +-0.03-0.05 per spot and +-0.012 pooled (replay
  spots) / +-0.025 (turn 1); an effect of 1-2 points of win rate is below that. The paired streams help only
  until the candidates' games part (the first move here).
* **One checkpoint for every spot** (308), while the replay spots come from generations 240-308's games.
* **`actual` is hindsight**: N library orders of one real hand; its se says nothing about other hands.
* **The site-id mapping reads the publisher's log** (its line formats); ids not in the log are not found (an
  error, never a guess). The site is not asked.
* **Pins and `top` condition by rejection**: an unlikely pin costs up to `tries` deals per game (100,000 x ~6
  us = 0.6 s at worst) before the error; the report has the deals' card shares.
* **Seeding self-play** with `start` blocks works as specs do (no deal seed: the driver's game seed deals;
  forced moves are single options, never recorded): a run could play from a pool of real spots. Teaching a
  trick needs more - the forced move itself is no training sample (a single option has no search and no
  target); a recorded root at the spot with the trick forced into its tree, or a policy-target override,
  is not built.
* **The value net's view after a self-look is off its distribution** (76.7: casting the Bauble on turn 1
  costs ~0.1 of value; the network never does it in self-play), so the deep searches' Q of Bauble-first
  inherits that bias - which is also the most likely reason the habit persists: nothing in self-play ever
  measures the line.

## 78. CUDA graphs of the token network's inference (zero-core `feat/token-graphs`, opt-in)

Branch `token-graphs` (from main 1605436), zero-core `feat/token-graphs` 2b79780 (code 3d5875e, docs
2b79780; from c15e3d0; its docs/az.md 10.6 has the design, the numerics and every measurement),
2026-10-31. Nothing live changed:
the runs, their pinned worktrees and the Mac untouched; checkpoints copied read-only to
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/token-graphs/`.

### 78.1 Why, and what

The desktop GPU's eager inference of the Delver line's token network (128 x 4, the belief head) is
bound by its ~445-585 kernels and 13-15 host syncs a forward, not by its arithmetic (62.2, zero-core
az.md 10.5); it is the desktop's self-play share and every head-to-head and Elo match run on the RTX
5090 (a 2,400-game paired h2h at 32 simulations: ~80 minutes on 2026-10-31). zero-core's
`TokenGraphRunner` captures the network's inference in CUDA graphs: the host packs each batch
(present slots, token counts and positions), one graph per padded (rows: multiple of 64, tokens:
multiple of 16) shape runs a static-shape forward (156 kernels, no sync) with the belief head's
predictions and value-only rows; float32; the answers are eager's to float32 rounding.

### 78.2 How to turn it on (off by default)

* **h2h**: `python -m mtgz.az.h2h A B ... --device cuda --graphs 1` (both sides; `--a-graphs` /
  `--b-graphs` for one side). The output then has `graphs_a` / `graphs_b` (each side's share of batches
  through the graphs: 1.0). Note for the line's matches: `--select` replaces a side's run rule, so pass
  the leaf view as the A/B driver does (`--a-leaf-value-view root --b-leaf-value-view root`).
* **A run** (its desktop self-play and evaluations): the env `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1` on the command that
  starts it - `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1 MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py
  "$RUN/supervisor_console.txt" python tools/supervise.py "$RUN" ...`: the supervisor passes its
  environment to the run, whose `stdout.txt` then says `zero.infer: token network CUDA graphs on ...`
  for each evaluator. No run setting (zero-core's run.py is being changed on another branch); the
  Mac's workers are not affected (they infer on their CPU). It needs the run's pinned build to have
  zero-core 3d5875e or later - a re-pin, the orchestrator's call.
* **bench**: `python -m mtgz.az.bench infer | selfplay ... --device cuda --graphs 1`.
* Off: `ZERO_CUDA_GRAPHS=0` turns the env off (said on stderr); on a CPU evaluator the env is said
  and ignored; `--graphs 1` with `--device cpu` is an error.

### 78.3 Measured (the desktop GPU shared with r3-2b-beliefsearch's training and self-play and another session's h2h; eager and graphs interleaved)

| what | eager | graphs | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| inference, leaves/s at batches of 64 / 144 / 192 / 512 | 3,034 / 4,291 / 5,305 / 6,871 | 21,790 / 27,054 / 25,680 / 26,690 | 7.2x / 6.3x / 4.8x / 3.9x |
| h2h, 200 games, 32 simulations, 200 in flight (batches of 36) | 1,753.7 s | 261.3 s | 6.7x |
| self-play at the line's settings (192 in flight, batches of ~145), leaves/s | 2,195, 2,004 | 6,457, 8,028 | 3.4x |
| h2h, 2,400 paired games (the A/B driver's shape, 1,024 in flight) | ~80 min (that morning's; not interleaved) | 27.8 min | ~2.9x |

* **Numerics** (iteration 328 on the 8,192 held-out rows, batches of 1-1,024): max abs. differences
  priors 2.9e-6, value 9.5e-7, margin 2.4e-6, belief 5.1e-7 (means 1e-7 or less), the same at every size;
  replays deterministic.
* **Equivalence**: iteration 328 against itself, A graphs, B eager, 400 paired games: **A 0.4975 +-
  0.0043** (pairs' se), 197 of 200 deals split, the 3 others 1 for A and 2 for B.

  sparse feed from the driver is the next step (zero-core az.md 10.6).

## 80. The exhaustive lookahead per information set in Rust, a lookahead player (zero-core `feat/lookahead`, opt-in)

Branch `lookahead` (from main e057c87), zero-core `feat/lookahead` (from main c6b959b; its docs/search.md
3.9 has the design and the API), 2026-11-01, approved by the user that day. Nothing live changed: the
main line r3-2b-beliefsearch is stopped (the user's call), its pinned worktrees, the Delver Lab (:5360),
the Delver AI publisher, the other experiment (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead-teacher/`) and the Mac
untouched; the network is a read-only copy of iteration 475 with its run's config in
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead/models/r3-2b-beliefsearch/`. Off by default; no merge, no push.

### 80.1 Why

The Delver Lab's x-ply lookahead (delver-lab `delverlab/xply.py`, `xply_is.py`, Python over the bindings)
found lines the network's MCTS misses - Mishra's Bauble first at a turn-1 spot, with a card-dependent
follow-up -: it ignores the prior (every option expanded), decides our moves per information set (the
value of information) and searches every reply. It walks every node in Python and values the leaves on
the CPU (~1,500 positions/s): ~5-30 s a 6-ply decision. The goal: fast enough to play whole evaluation
games with it (a lookahead player), later to produce self-play targets, and to speed up the lab.

### 80.2 What (zero-core docs/search.md 3.9)

`crates/search/src/lookahead.rs` ports the lab's lookahead exactly: plies = decisions with >= 2 options of
either seat (single-option ones stepped by the transition, mana payments - `minor_decision` - the network's
top prior, no ply); horizons `plies`, 'turn', 'next_turn' (`max_plies` 40, `cut` counted); every option or
top-k by prior (`topk_root`, `topk_from_turn`); our decisions per information set (members grouped by an
exact hash of `encode(R)` and the legal options, one choice per group, the max of the group's average) or
per world; the opponent per world by 'min' (best reply), 'expect' (policy-weighted) or 'top'; worlds dealt
from the root decider's view by the seat's root belief (tilt 1 / clip 20 / mix 0.25 for the Delver line's
evaluation seat), explicit seeds in the position API; leaves the value head on `encode(R)`
(root-view), terminals `result()`; a node budget with stages (top-k 4 below the root, then shallower,
then the seat's MCTS) and counters. It is a seat type of zero-core's driver (seat key `lookahead`): its
leaf and prior rows go through the same batches as MCTS leaves, so every game in flight shares one GPU
batch. Leaf values are shared by observation (`dedup`: worlds R cannot tell apart after the same moves
share one row; exact up to float rounding).

What MTG needs: `SearchGame::active_seat` (the active player, for 'next_turn'; engine/src/az/mod.rs, test
`active_seat_is_the_active_player` in tests/az.rs), the existing `minor_decision` (PayMana / PayPool) and
`determinize_with` (the belief head's deal); observation hashing is zero-core's generic hash of the
encoding (the lab's key), no MTG hook. `mtgz/az/lookahead.py`: zero.lookahead with MTG's `reveal` (the
draws / looks a line's move showed, from its chance keys) for the position API's lines. h2h: zero.h2h's
flags pass through `python -m mtgz.az.h2h`.

### 80.3 How to use it

* **A match**: `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1 python -m mtgz.az.h2h A B --a-lookahead plies=4,worlds=8,opp=min,budget=100000
  --sims 32 --chance-k 0 --device cuda --graphs 1 --paired --spec "$SPEC" --threads 12 [--conc N --groups G
  --max-rows 1024]`: side A decides by the lookahead (its MCTS settings - the run's evaluation seat, read from
  the checkpoint's run config - deal its worlds by the belief and play its final fallback), B by MCTS. The
  output adds `lookahead_a`, `lookahead_tag_a`, `look` (decisions, nodes, rows, fallbacks per stage, peak live
  games, the search threads' lookahead time).
* **A position** (the lab's call): `from mtgz.az import lookahead as LA; LA.evaluate_position(game, ev,
  {'plies': 6, 'worlds': 8, 'opp': 'min'}, seeds=range(8), belief_tilt=1, belief_clip=20, belief_mix=0.25)`
  -> per root option the value per world, mean +- sd, the modal principal line with labels and reveals, the
  counters; `worlds=[...]` instead of `seeds` takes worlds dealt elsewhere (the parity runs feed the lab's
  code and this one the same worlds).
* Settings: `plies`, `horizon`, `max_plies`, `worlds`, `topk`, `topk_root`, `topk_from_turn`, `opp`
  (min | best | expect | policy | top), `mode` (infoset | world), `budget`, `fallback_topk`, `fallback_plies`,
  `fallback` (mcts | prior), `rows`, `dedup` - an unknown or bad one is an error.

### 80.5 Throughput

**One position at a time** (the position API, the lab's call: one game in flight; the GPU's token graphs,
`scripts/bench_look.py`; 13 positions - the 5 parity spots on turn 1 and 8 of gen 418 #2 from turn 3 on, >= 4
options; 8 worlds, best reply; the desktop shared with this branch's own h2h):

| plies | branching | s / decision (turn 1 / mid-game) | nodes / decision | nodes / s | value rows shared |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | every option | 0.19 (0.13 / 0.22) | 2,113 | 11,271 | 75% |
| 4 | top-k 4 | 0.10 (0.08 / 0.11) | 1,352 | 13,709 | 70% |
| 5 | every option | 0.37 (0.25 / 0.45) | 6,252 | 16,723 | 74% |
| 5 | top-k 4 | 0.24 (0.18 / 0.28) | 3,562 | 14,728 | 68% |
| 6 | every option | 0.80 (0.46 / 1.02) | 18,142 | 22,650 | 72% |
| 6 | top-k 4 | 0.53 (0.40 / 0.61) | 9,357 | 17,824 | 67% |

The lab's Python took 7-10 s for the user's spot at 6 plies (17,598 nodes, CPU); the same lookahead here
0.64-1.2 s on the GPU. One position is bound by the lookahead's own CPU work on one thread (clones,
transitions, encodings and their hashes: ~40-60 us a node), not by the network.

**Many games in flight** (the driver, `scripts/bench_driver.py`: the h2h's shape - the lookahead seat against
the run's MCTS evaluation seat, paired games, sparse batches, 4 groups, 12 search threads; best reply):

| plies | branching | 1 game in flight: decisions / s (s a decision) | 64 in flight: decisions / s | nodes / s | rows / s | evaluators' share |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | every option | 17.3 (0.058) | 104 | 83k | 29k | 0.50 |
| 4 | top-k 4 | 18.1 (0.055) | 126 | 76k | 29k | 0.67 |
| 5 | every option | 12.5 (0.080) | 65 | 143k | 48k | 0.45 |
| 5 | top-k 4 | 13.6 (0.074) | 87 | 139k | 48k | 0.56 |
| 6 | every option | 5.6 (0.177) | 40 | 242k | 79k | 0.55 |
| 6 | top-k 4 | 8.6 (0.117) | 55 | 225k | 79k | 0.64 |

(60 s from the games' start each - mostly the first turns, ~580-6,000 nodes a decision; the desktop otherwise
idle.) Many games in flight multiply the decisions per second by 6-7: the GPU batches every game's rows
together (79k rows/s at 6 plies, against ~27k leaves/s for MCTS's batches of a few hundred rows in 78.3).
The speed-ups that got there (zero-core, opt-in): **sparse batches** (each row's ~150 non-zeros instead of
37,620 floats: the batches' assembly into fresh memory had been 59% of a 4-ply match's wall time; a 32-game
match 165 s -> 89 s, the same games), **4 driver groups** (89 s -> 65 s), the evaluator's `max_rows` pieces
two in flight, the graphs' host copy over 4 threads for big dense batches, leaf values shared by observation
(57-81% of the leaves), encoding in place in the batch buffer.

**CPU only** (eager CPU network, 8 torch threads, 8 positions - the 5 of turn 1 and 3 mid-game -, the desktop
idle): 4 plies 0.15 s a decision (GPU 0.12), 6 plies 1.04 s (GPU 0.58; 28,872 nodes a decision at these
positions): one position is mostly the lookahead's own CPU work, the GPU's edge is in batching many games.


### 80.6 First lookahead player against the MCTS player

The same network for both sides (iteration 475's copy), the run's spec, `--chance-k 0`, paired games. B = the
run's evaluation seat: 32 simulations, the 'cq' rule with select_min_visits 4 and select scale 0.3, root-view
leaves, the root belief (tilt 1, mix 0.25). A = the same seat with `--a-lookahead`: per information set, 8
worlds dealt by its belief, every option, the stated opponent model and budget (fallback: top-k 4 below the
root, then 2 plies fewer, then the seat's MCTS). Scores are A's (+- 1 se of the pair scores).

| A (the lookahead side) | pairs | A's score | Elo | wall / 100 games (in flight) | A's decisions; nodes / rows a decision | fallbacks (top-k / MCTS) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 4 plies, best reply, budget 100k | 100 | **0.315 +- 0.030** | -135 | 693 s (200; dense) | 23,875; 852 / 262 | 6 / 0 |
| 4 plies, policy-weighted, budget 100k | 100 | **0.390 +- 0.034** | -78 | 540 s (200; dense) | 22,598; 821 / 348 | 7 / 0 |
| 6 plies, best reply, budget 150k | 50 | **0.470 +- 0.046** | -21 | 877 s (64) | 13,193; 6,638 / 2,118 | 80 / 0 |
| 6 plies, policy-weighted, budget 150k | 50 | **0.370 +- 0.045** | -93 | 910 s (64) | 10,979; 6,974 / 3,249 | 77 / 0 |
| guarded, 4 plies, 16 worlds, policy-weighted, 5 pp | 300 | **0.515 +- 0.015** | +10 | 365 s (100) | 71,427; 1,880 / 640; **1.9% overridden** | 15+ / 0 |
| guarded, 6 plies, 16 worlds, policy-weighted, 5 pp, budget 300k | 50 | **0.460 +- 0.035** | -28 | 2,583 s (64) | 12,387; 13,445 / 5,506; **2.3% overridden** | 112 / 0 |

(The first two ran on dense batches before 80.5's speed-ups, the rest on sparse batches with 4 driver groups;
"wall / 100 games" is the match's wall time per 100 games with that many in flight on the shared desktop.)

* **The pure lookahead player loses to MCTS at 32 simulations** at 4 plies by 80-135 Elo and at 6 plies by
  20-90: it picks the best of every option's lookahead value, and those values carry the value head's noise -
  the max over many of them is biased upward (the optimizer's curse). The teacher experiment
  (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead-teacher/results/summary.json`, another session's) measured the same from the
  other side: on 203 non-trivial decisions of generations 380-454 the 6-ply lookahead disagrees with the
  network's 8 x 64 MCTS at 37-42% and its moves played out worse there (-1.0 +- 0.6 pp best reply, -1.1 +- 0.7
  policy-weighted), predicting +2.4 pp; large predicted differences were well calibrated.
* **The guarded player** (the coordinator's ask after that finding; `guard`, docs/search.md 3.9 in zero-core)
  keeps the MCTS move unless the lookahead's best option beats the MCTS move's lookahead value by more than 5
  pp: at 4 plies it changes 1.9% of its decisions and scores 0.515 +- 0.015 over 300 pairs (0.555, 0.500, 0.490
  in three batches of 100 - the first one's +38 Elo was luck): even with MCTS-32, +10 Elo within 1 se; at 6
  plies (2.3% changed) 0.460 +- 0.035 over 50 pairs - no better. The few moves the lookahead is very sure of
  do not add measurable strength at these sample sizes.
* Best reply beats policy-weighted at 6 plies (0.47 against 0.37) and loses at 4 (0.315 against 0.39): at 6
  plies the lookahead sees the opponent's reply and our answer to it; at 4 the pessimistic reply ends many
  lines one ply after it.

### 80.7 What a 1,300-game evaluation would take

From the matches above and 80.5 (the desktop as it was: sometimes two matches sharing it; a game is ~115-125
lookahead decisions plus as many MCTS ones; 1,300 games = 650 pairs):

| the lookahead side | per 100 games (in flight) | 1,300 games |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4 plies, 8 worlds | ~150-200 s (64-100; sparse, 4 groups) | ~35-45 min |
| 5 plies, 8 worlds | ~1.6x 4 plies (80.5's decisions / s) | ~1-1.2 h |
| 6 plies, 8 worlds | 877-910 s (64) | ~3.2 h |
| guarded, 4 plies, 16 worlds | 365 s (100) | ~1.3 h |
| guarded, 6 plies, 16 worlds | 2,583 s (64) | ~9.3 h |

More games in flight (128-256) should shorten the 6-ply runs further (the batches grow; memory: ~11 KB a live
member game, the largest 6-ply decision held 230k at once - 2.5 GB). Top-k 4 below the root cuts 6 plies by
~30% (80.5).

### 80.9 What next (proposals, not done)

* The lookahead as a **training target**: not as the policy (its pure moves lose), maybe as a guarded
  correction or a value target at the root; needs its own A/B.
* **Fewer noisy maxima**: a lower-variance leaf (a few MCTS simulations per leaf instead of the raw value),
  the prior as a tie-breaker / regulariser at our decisions, or more worlds where the root options are close.
* **Speed**: within-decision parallelism (one position is single-threaded: the lab's latency), sparse batches
  for MCTS self-play and evaluation (their batches are bound by the same host copies, 78.3).

MCTS opponent in the same games, C = both seats of the control; rate (n).

| action profile (share of the choices) | L | M | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| own main phase, no land drop open | **pass 0.50**, cast 0.34, activate 0.17 | pass 0.33, cast 0.40, activate 0.27 | pass 0.31, cast 0.42, activate 0.27 |

**Decision-level disagreement.** 500 of L's decisions (mana payments apart: there it takes the top prior),
each searched again by MCTS-32 twice (seeds apart: the noise floor) and by the lookahead once more with new
worlds (its self-consistency):

| kind of decision | n | L vs MCTS | MCTS vs MCTS | lookahead again vs its move | most common (L, MCTS) at disagreements |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| priority, other steps | 154 | 0.273 | 0.013 | 0.117 | pass / cast 19, pass / activate 15, cast / pass 4 |
| response | 107 | 0.196 | 0.019 | 0.084 | pass / cast 8, pass / activate 5, activate / pass 3 |
| own main, no land drop | 74 | 0.365 | 0.000 | 0.284 | pass / cast 10, pass / activate 8 |
| own main, land drop open | 35 | 0.486 | 0.000 | 0.343 | another land 7, pass / land 3 |
| library selection | 33 | 0.242 | 0.061 | 0.152 | |
| other (yes-no, modes, triggers) | 25 | 0.400 | 0.040 | 0.200 | |
| targets | 23 | 0.413 | 0.130 | 0.174 | the other player / land |
| attacks | 18 | 0.389 | 0.000 | 0.111 | no attack / attack 5 |
| mulligan, play-draw, bottom | 12 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | |
| delve choices | 10 | 0.200 | 0.000 | 0.200 | |
| alternative costs | 6 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | |
| blocks | 3 | 0.5 | 0.33 | 0 | |
| **all** | **500** | **0.290** | **0.022** | **0.156** | |

Of the 136 decisions where L differs from both MCTS searches, it **passes where MCTS acts 68 times** (a cast 37 -
Lightning Bolt 9, Brainstorm 7, Unholy Heat 6 -, an activation 28 - fetches 17, Clues 6 -, a land 3) and acts
where MCTS passes 12 times. Its margin over the MCTS move, in its own re-run, is 1-3 pp in most kinds - inside
the value head's noise - and it does not reproduce 16% of its own moves with new worlds (MCTS-32: 2%).

**The most notable systematic differences** (the counts above):

1. **It defers: passes where MCTS acts** - own main phase with no land drop open 50% passes against 31-33%;
   at disagreements 68 passes against 12 actions. The horizon effect plausibly drives it: a held option
   (a card in hand, an uncracked fetch, open mana) keeps its value at a 6-ply leaf, while what acting buys
   (a threat that attacks next turn, a card drawn, a land thinned) is mostly past the horizon.
2. **It holds fetches**: cracked at once 64.5% against 87.5%, 57 held into the next turn against 1 (M) and
   12 (C, two seats).
3. **It blocks less** (52% against 64-68%) and attacks a planeswalker less (5% against 9-11%).
4. **It delves worse** with Murktide (best delve 72% against 81%) and plays a land when one is open less
   (68% against 78%), choosing another land 7 times in 35 sampled land-drop decisions.
5. **It looks at its own library with Mishra's Bauble more** (69% against 46-56%) and taps out into Daze less
   (49% against 55%; when it does, it is Dazed less, 34% against 47%) - the information it values.

**What plausibly explains the -36 Elo**: (1) and (2) - lost tempo and card flow in a tempo mirror, a
systematic bias of a fixed horizon - and the noise: half its disagreements with MCTS are not reproduced by a
re-run of the lookahead itself (16% of all its moves), small margins chosen by a max over noisy leaves (the
teacher experiment's optimizer's curse). (3) and (4) cost life and Murktide's size. (5) is not obviously a
cost (Bauble looks and Daze care are the kind of information play the lab found); the game lengths are the
same (16.65 against 17.02 turns). Mulligans and the play / draw choice are the network's (keep rates equal; it
chose to draw twice in 100).

**The guarded 4-ply player** (16 worlds, policy-weighted, 5 pp; 200 paired games the same way, 0.470 +- 0.023
here): it overrode 1.8% of its decisions (422 of 23,151), and its fingerprints are MCTS's within noise - fetch
cracked at once 0.868 against M 0.895 / C 0.874, Murktide delve best 0.783 / 0.821, Bauble looks at its own
library 0.473 / 0.474, tap-out into Daze 0.550 / 0.557 -: the guard removes the deferring along with the rest.

## 82. Sparse network batches in self-play (zero-core `feat/sparse-selfplay`, run setting `sparse`, opt-in)

Branch `sparse-selfplay` (from main 3d3b99a), zero-core `feat/sparse-selfplay` 6e93cd8 (code 141c2ba; its
docs/az.md 10.7 has the design, the equivalence and every measurement), 2026-11-01. Nothing live changed.

* **Why**: the desktop's share of the Delver line's self-play was one process moving zeros - each leaf a
  37,620-float row (~0.7% non-zero) assembled by the driver, copied into the CUDA graphs' pinned buffer
  and uploaded (zero-core az.md 10.6) - at under half a CPU core, the RTX 5090 at ~185 W of 575.
* **What**: zero-core run setting `sparse` (default 0) gives every driver the run builds the lookahead's
  sparse batches (ENGINE.md 80, zero-core docs/search.md 2.2): the same rows, games and samples. The
  Mac's remote spec sets `sparse: 0` in both its overrides (evaluations and self-play): its CPU
  evaluators would only densify a sparse batch, and it is not measured there.
* **Equivalence**: the Delver line's self-play from iteration 489 with the graphs, the first 24 finished
  games' samples and results hashed: dense d31a5acb09179104 twice, sparse the same.
* **Measured** (the line's own local self-play from iteration 489, the GPU shared with
  r3-2b-exploit475): dense 192 in flight 13.4k leaves/s; sparse 192: 25.0k (1.87x); sparse 384: 35.6k
  (2.66x); **sparse 768: 44.3k (3.31x)**; sparse 1,536: 41.7k; 4 groups instead of 2 lose at every size.
  Harness: `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/sparse-bench/bench_sp.py` + `run_bench.sh`, results there.
* **Turning it on** for a run: `--sparse 1 --conc 768` at a restart (a re-pin onto a build with zero-core
  141c2ba or later; ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1 as before). The desktop's self-play share then grows (the shared
  queue gives a batch-bound consumer its slots), so its dense local shards grow too (~4.2 GB per ~620
  games, kept `keep_data` iterations). Training (~100 s a generation, 40-50 s of it loading the 34 GB
  window) becomes the larger part of a generation.
* **Checks** (tier "opt-in core feature with byte-identical defaults"): zero-core pytest 329 passed - two
  CUDA tests of test_token_graphs.py (`test_graphs_match_eager_and_follow_new_weights` 3.7e-5 against
  its 2e-5, `test_absent_slots_are_never_read` one ulp) fail about 2 runs in 3 on the shared GPU, on main
  c6b959b too (hub todo); the new loop test; the Delver equivalence above; mtg-zero pytest.


## 83. A sparse training window (zero-core `feat/window-sparse`, run setting `window_sparse`, opt-in)

Branch `window-sparse` (from main 783aa5f), zero-core `feat/window-sparse` 13a4bd2 (its docs/az.md 10.8 has
the design, the equivalence and the measurements), 2026-11-01. Nothing live changed.

* **Why**: the Delver line's window (iteration 489: 73 shards, 864k rows, 7 local shards of 29.8 GB plain
  + 66 remote ones, 36 GB inflated) is over its 34 GB budget, so it is subsampled to 438k rows and the
  WindowCache (`window_cache` 1 since 10-31) reused nothing: 40-54 s of every ~100 s training reloaded
  every shard. A row is 252 non-zeros of 37,620 floats on average.
* **What**: zero-core run setting `window_sparse` (default 0): the window keeps rows as their non-zeros
  (float16 bits, -0.0 kept); with `window_cache` every shard is cached whole also over budget and the
  window subsampled from the cache, so an iteration loads only its new shards. Local shards (stored
  plain) are read in place (np.memmap) and converted on 8 threads. The budget still counts dense rows:
  the same 438k rows, the same batches.
* **Equivalence**: the dense and sparse windows of iteration 489 (40k-row budget) and the cached and
  uncached sparse ones (full budget): every array equal, 20 batches of 512 bit for bit. End to end:
  `delver-smoke` 2 iterations, dense against `--window-sparse 1 --window-cache 1 --sparse 1` (seed 1,
  CPU): iteration 1 and 2 networks identical tensor for tensor, iteration 2 reusing 836 rows.
* **Measured** (iteration 488 then 489, budget 438,636 rows, the desktop shared with r3-2b-exploit475):
  cold 29.8 s, warm **6.6 s** (8 new shards, 2 local) against 54.1 s dense; the process 4.3 GB in all
  against a 34 GB window; batches of 512 in 19-21 ms.
* **Turning it on**: `--window-sparse 1` (with `--window-cache 1`, which the main line has) at a restart on
  a build with zero-core 13a4bd2 or later; together with 82's `--sparse 1 --conc 768`. A larger
  `ram_budget_gb` would now cost little RAM but changes the window (more rows kept): a training change.
* **Checks** (tier "opt-in core feature with byte-identical defaults"): zero-core pytest 325 passed (the
  two flaky CUDA tests of 82 deselected), mtg-zero pytest 69 passed, the equivalences above.

## 85. The static training step and local linger (zero-core `feat/train-speed`, run settings `train_static` and `selfplay_local_linger`, opt-in)

Branch `train-speed` (from main 3abb2e3), zero-core `feat/train-speed` (its docs/az.md 10.9 and 10.10 have
the design, the equivalence and the measurements), 2026-11-01, the user's go-ahead ("yes to 1 and 2" after a
throughput review of r3-2b-late550). Nothing live changed.

* **Why**: with 82 and 83 a Delver generation (r3-2b-late550, warm gens 567-580) was ~183 s = self-play
  ~133 s + training ~49 s (542 steps at ~91 ms; the window 3 s). The training step was the eager token
  forward (per-segment packing, chunks of 64 rows, ~20 host syncs) with a foreach AdamW, and the desktop -
  ~75% of the games - idled through it while the Mac lingered.
* **What**: `train_static` 1 = training through `TokenNet.forward_static` (the inference graphs' forward:
  each batch one chunk, no host sync) with a fused AdamW on CUDA; a sparse window's batches travel as their
  non-zeros (~2.5 MB instead of 77 MB a batch of 512) and are made dense on the device. `selfplay_local_linger`
  1 = the desktop's self-play plays on with the previous checkpoint while the run trains (a thread, its
  CUDA batches on a stream of their own), its games held for the next iteration's quota (lag 1, as the
  Mac's linger). CUDA graph captures are thread-local now (a capture beside the training thread failed
  both under torch's default mode).
* **Equivalence**: a training step's loss and gradients equal the eager step's to float32 rounding; one
  generation of the line's training (iteration 585 from 584 and its optimizer state, same window, same
  process): the logged losses equal to 5 decimals (policy 0.22216, value 0.37837, margin 0.17771 / 0.17770,
  entropy 0.22322, belief 2.50654), the networks 1.6% of the update's norm apart (AdamW amplifying rounding).
* **Measured** (the GPU shared with the live run): a training step 113.9 ms eager -> 40.4 ms (32.8 ms in a
  quieter minute); ~23 ms of it float32 kernels, half of that padding rows to the batch's longest. A 3-generation GPU smoke forked from
  late550@589 (400 games, 384 in flight, both settings, the desktop alone): the linger played 80 and 57 games
  during trainings of 31.3 s (cold window) and 12.9 s, none after the last generation, quotas exact; the
  training beside it 68-78 ms a step against 50 ms alone. The desktop's samples one checkpoint behind rise
  (67% / 54% at that small quota; the live line's ~35% today, from the games in flight carried over).
* **Turning them on**: `--train-static 1 --selfplay-local-linger 1` at a restart on a build with zero-core
  feat/train-speed, on top of 82/83's flags (`--sparse 1 --conc 768 --window-sparse 1`, ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1).
  Expected: training ~49 -> ~20 s; with the linger the desktop keeps playing through it (~9 games a second
  minus the training's share of the GPU), a generation ~183 -> ~140-150 s. Measure on the first real
  generations (the Mac's linger and the shared queue's rates are not in the smoke).
* **Checks** (tier "opt-in core feature with byte-identical defaults"): zero-core pytest 327 passed + the two known flaky CUDA graph
  tests (hub todo; one of them failed on main 13a4bd2 in the same session, both pass on a rerun); toy runs
  from main 13a4bd2 and this core with default settings (MLP and tokens, 3 iterations, seed 3, CPU) byte
  identical - every shard, checkpoint, optimizer state and the metrics without timings; mtg-zero pytest 69
  passed; the equivalences above. A full-suite run caught `data.batches` passing the new arguments to
  window-likes without them (distill's `Taught`, a test stand-in): fixed - the default path calls
  `W.batch(idx, device)` as before.

## 86. Floating mana from a source about to be lost (Wasteland, Daze)

Branch `float-mana` (from `view-known` 7a53953 = main 8e67300 plus the spectator view's known block),
2026-11-02. The user's report from the Delver Lab's Play tab: "I had my untapped Volcanic Island
Wastelanded and I was not able to float mana in response." docs/shortcuts.md 13.12 kept mana abilities
out of priority (floating there is activating the ability while paying later in the step) and named
this exception without handling it. The user approved a narrow fix plus one extension (Daze: "should
give you the option to float when you are returning an untapped land with Daze"). **Layout v5, its
width, every offset and every action id are unchanged**; the gen-424 checkpoint of
`runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch` loads (`mtgz.az.replays.check_encoding`).

### 86.1 In response: a targeted untapped source (CR 605.3a, 117.1d)

With priority, a player may activate the mana abilities of an untapped permanent they control while an
object on the stack targets it (`Game::floats_in_response`; `mana_at_priority` = `mana_with_priority`
or it, read by `activation_options` and `can_activate`). Wasteland's ability at a Volcanic Island:
tap the Island for {U} or {R} in response; Wasteland resolves; cast Lightning Bolt with the {R} later
in the same step. Also a Thundering Falls, a Wasteland, a Bolt at a Birds of Paradise, a Shatter at a
Sol Ring. The activation is the Lion's Eye Diamond path (`begin_activate` -> `ManaNow`: its costs,
then `ChooseMana` when it has several productions, mana to the pool, priority stays: 605.3a; `passes`
resets as for any activation, so both players pass again before the stack resolves). Tapped, the
source offers nothing more; a mana ability that doesn't tap (none in the Delver deck) can be offered
again while its cost can be paid. Every other priority is as before: an untargeted source, an empty
stack, a source already tapped.

### 86.2 Before a cost sacrifices or returns it (CR 601.2g before 601.2h)

A cost's choice of a permanent to sacrifice (`Sacrifice`) or to return (`BounceCost`) in `PayCosts`
offers, beside each candidate's `MY_PERM` id, `ACTIVATE` + its slot x 4 + i for each mana ability i
that `float_before_cost` allows: "activate its mana ability i, then it is the one sacrificed or
returned" (`cost_pick_options`). Chosen, the pick is recorded, `PayCosts` is pushed again and the
ability activates (`begin_activate`, the 86.1 path): the mana goes to the pool and stays there; the
rest of the cost follows as chosen. Daze: return the untapped Island, or tap it for {U} and return it,
then Brainstorm with the {U}. `float_before_cost` allows only an untapped source's abilities whose cost
is {T} (and life: the cost's own life is paid after it, CR 119.4, with a painland's damage first), so
the activation leaves the permanent where the cost needs it and changes nothing else the cost chooses
from: no mana cost, X, self-sacrifice, other sacrifice, counters, "sacrifice it if no counters" (a
Lotus Petal, a Treasure, Gemstone Mine are left out). A cost that taps its source (a fetch land,
Wasteland, Mishra's Bauble) never picks it, so nothing changes there.

Where it reaches (`CardDb::constructed`, scanned on this branch): Daze (return an Island), Tinker,
Goblin Engineer, Legion Extruder, Thopter Foundry (an artifact: a Sol Ring or a Mox first), Natural
Order, Bone Shards, Goblin Bombardment (a creature: a Birds of Paradise), Crop Rotation, Zuran Orb,
Sylvan Safekeeper, Baloth Prime, Mine Collapse (a land), Fallen Shinobi's and Kaito's ninjutsu (an
attacker, usually tapped), Retrofitter Foundry, Bolas's Citadel, Magda (Treasures: excluded, their
mana ability sacrifices them). Not included: emerge's sacrifice (Crabomination), chosen before the
total cost: the payment that follows may already tap that creature for the spell's mana, and a float
there would be spent by it (13.13); and no mana source of the pool has an ability that sacrifices or
exiles itself without {T}.

### 86.3 The pool

Floated mana is in `Player.pool` until the step ends (`flow.rs`, CR 500.4, 106.4) and pays through the
payment's virtual pool like a Dark Ritual's (section 34: the payment spends as much of it as it can;
`PayPool` when the pools it can leave differ). It is public state the network reads: the per-player
globals `g[24 + 40 side + 6 + k]` (viewer first) and `g5::POOL_ART` / `POOL_HASTE`; the public-state
gate's "mana in a pool" perturbation reaches both viewers' encodings (58.6). Those inputs were
untrained for this: in 400 recorded main-line games (r3-2b-beliefsearch, gens ~510-550, 97,809
decisions) no decision had mana in either pool. The network sees floated mana (that the opponent can
pay Daze's {1}, that a Bolt is live) but learns what it means only once a run trains on this engine.

### 86.4 Ids, decisions, bots, the spectator view

* **Ids**: the priority case uses the priority's `ACTIVATE` + slot x 4 + i (a land's mana ability is
  ability 0, the intrinsic one first: section 19); the cost case the same ids inside the existing
  `Sacrifice` / `BounceCost` decisions. No new decision kind, task or id range; the context block is
  unchanged (kind, the `PayCosts` task, the spell or ability being paid). A source's `ACTIVATE` ids are
  pointer logits from its token (22.2), as its `MY_PERM` id.
* **Bots**: the heuristic never takes them (its priority scores only non-mana abilities; its
  `Sacrifice` / `BounceCost` answer picks a `Card` option). Random play takes them uniformly (the fuzzer,
  the digests).
* **Spectator view** (`az/view.rs` `option_text`, what the Play tab shows): at priority "Tap Volcanic
  Island for mana" (`Choice::Ability`, kind `Priority`, the option's `c` = the permanent); in a cost
  "Tap Island for mana, then return it to hand" / "Tap Sol Ring for mana, then sacrifice it" beside
  "Return Island to hand". A source with several productions asks `ChooseMana` next, now worded by the
  mana outside a payment ("Add {U}" / "Add {R}" for a Volcanic Island; `NUMBER` + the production index;
  inside a payment still "Mana option k"). The pool is each player's `"pool"` string ("R", "UU": W U B R
  G C letters, present only when non-empty). The Play tab's default stops already include an
  opponent's object on the stack (the Wasteland float); the Daze float makes a one-Island `BounceCost`
  a real decision (two options) where it used to be answered alone.

### 86.5 Tests and gates

`tests/rules_float.rs` (11, CR-named): float in response to Wasteland, then Bolt after it resolves in the
same step (605.3a); the pool empties at the end of the step and the Bolt is no longer castable (500.4);
no option for a tapped source or an untargeted one, none at an empty stack; Daze: tap the Island, return
it, Brainstorm with the {U} (601.2g-h), a Volcanic Island floats either colour, a tapped Island offers
only the return, two untapped Islands offer four options; Tinker taps the Sol Ring it sacrifices; fetch
land and Wasteland activations unchanged (and the opponent of a Wasteland target gets the float); the
spectator view's labels.

The gate positions (az.rs) are played partly at random, so the new options moved them, and three
checks met positions they had not met before - none a fault of this change:
* the public-state gate's "a spell can't be countered" perturbation hit Abrupt Decay, already
  uncounterable (the perturbation's own fault, like 58.8's 7/7 on a 7/7): it skips such spells now;
* "colorless mana for artifacts only" needs {C} in a pool at a sampled decision and found none: marked
  rare, as "red mana that gives haste" (`AZ_SCALE=3`: applied twice, encoded for both viewers);
* `a_sharp_belief_concentrates_the_deal` met a Delver position with a cloud over the opponent's hand
  (P0 knows one of P1's hand cards is a Thundering Falls). A hand cloud's domain is the whole hand and
  `resample_weighted` fills its free places from the shuffled rest of the pool before the weights
  choose among them, so a sharp belief cannot concentrate there (0.09 of 1 dealt, uniform 0.07): a
  limitation of 69.2's weighted deal, not of this change (the test now skips such positions; a fix -
  weighted draws for a hand cloud's free places - changes belief search's behaviour and is left to the
  user). At `AZ_SCALE=3` the public-state gate also meets two more perturbation artefacts of the same
  kind (a base 7/7 set on Torsten, a 7/7; "can't block" on Headliner Scarlett): not part of the gate's
  default scale, left as they are.

Checks (tier "engine rules/cards"): the full suite (`cargo test --release -p engine -p card_ir
--no-fail-fast`) 1,507 passed and the 2 position-set failures above, fixed and rerun (`az` 40 passed,
`rules_float` 11); `FUZZ_GAMES=20000`: 20,000 games and 1,000 matches, no failure (519 s, 5,712,518
options completed); `FUZZ_POOL=delver FUZZ_GAMES=20000`: no failure (330 s, 4,459,370 options
completed); pytest 69 passed; digests re-recorded (`DIGEST_WRITE=1`, 70b545f): full **f6543eb2b1b8752f**
(was 132437374243f7b2), encoding-free **1c61c689e1829386** (was a0d54562c8330271), id-agnostic
(`DIGEST_IDS=choices`) dd91f84dfe3a262b; 1,083 of the 2,000 random games and 193 of the 500 heuristic
games changed (the random side takes the new options; the heuristic's own option lists grew).
`python tools/gate.py engine --no-mac --expect-digest f6543eb2b1b8752f --expect-digest0 1c61c689e1829386`: **GATE
PASSED** on 70b545f in 584 s (build, both digests as expected, `az` 40, `limits` 9, `hidden` 16, pytest 69, the
1-config search smoke: random seed 0, 0 of 1 failed).

### 86.6 The network on the new engine (gen 424)

264 games of `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch/models/iter_0424.pt` against itself on this branch's engine
(`python -m mtgz.az.replays ... --games 200 --conc 32 --device cuda --seed 424`, 3,809 s on a GPU shared
with another session's job, and `--games 64 --device cpu --seed 425`, 1,036 s; the run's settings: 64
simulations, `sims_minor` 4, evaluation rules, root-view leaves; replays in
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/float-mana/replays{,_cpu}`, scanned with `float_scan.py` / `float_q.py` there
(`pool_scan.py`: 86.3's count): the frames' options by their spectator-view words, `acts`, `n`, `q`, `p0`):

| | Offered | A game | Taken | Prior on it (median) | Visit share | Q(float) - Q(best other) | Mana spent in the same step |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| With priority (all 150: an opponent's Wasteland; half in the floater's own turn) | 150 | 0.57 | 127 (85%) | 0.98 | 0.84 | median -0.0001, mean -0.005 (80 with both visited) | 13 of 127 (10%) |
| Daze's `BounceCost` | 139 | 0.53 | 121 (87%) | 0.995 | 0.88 | median -0.003, mean -0.016 (72) | 42 of 121 (35%) |

* **Why it takes them**: the prior. A land's `ACTIVATE` + 4 s + 0 is the pointer logit the network learned
  in `PayMana` ("tap this land"), and nothing taught it otherwise here; the search agrees (Q equal to the
  alternatives within noise), as it should: in both spots the source is lost anyway (destroyed; back in
  hand), so a float costs nothing but the information that mana floats. No harmful tap-out is possible
  by construction (86.1-86.2 offer only sources about to be lost) and none was seen.
* **What it does next** with priority after floating (127): passes 45, plays a land 27 (a Wasteland in
  its own upkeep or main phase), Brainstorm 11, another activation 7, Mishra's Bauble 5, Lightning Bolt
  4, Dragon's Rage Channeler / Murktide Regent / Cori-Steel Cutter 3 each, Force of Will 2, Ponder,
  Unholy Heat, Prismari Charm, Urza's Bauble 1 each: most floated mana empties unused (the opponent's
  turn, nothing instant to cast), which is free.
* **The pool as an input**: 913 of these games' 63,080 decisions (1.4%) had mana in a pool, against 0 of
  97,809 in 400 recorded main-line games before (86.3). The small negative Q gaps are the value head's
  untrained reaction to pool mana (the two options' positions differ only by the pool and a land that
  leaves either way): noise of ~0.01-0.02 in value until a run trains on this engine.
* Not measured: strength (the mirror plays itself; there is no old-engine opponent in one process), and
  the human Play tab, where the AI's float decisions are these.

### 86.7 Not done: removal that doesn't target

The rule follows targets only. A source lost to an effect that doesn't target it is not covered: a
Wrath of God or Toxic Deluge at a Birds of Paradise, Armageddon, Balance, an edict ("each player
sacrifices a creature", chosen on resolution), Council's Judgment (votes, no target), Upheaval.
Proposed, not built: a per-ability fact computed once at lowering, the filter of permanents its program
moves off the battlefield without targeting them (`DestroyAll`, `ExileAll`, `BounceAll`, `Sacrifice`
by a player, lethal `DamageAll`; each `Ext` op that does so annotated once), and with priority the
mana abilities of the player's untapped sources matching a filter of an object on the stack offered as
in 86.1 - as cheap as the target test (a scan of the stack's items' facts), exact for those ops,
conservative for the rest (an `Ext` op not annotated offers nothing). The Delver mirror has none of
these cards, so it would change cube play only.

## 87. Forked self-play games and start-position archives (zero-core `feat/forked-games`, run settings `selfplay_branch*` and `selfplay_archive*`, opt-in)

Branch `forked-games` (from main 37d6574, which carries the float-mana rules the main line trains with, plus
a merge of `position-lab` a335129 for its `start` block, section 76), zero-core `feat/forked-games` (its
docs/az.md 24 and docs/search.md 2.11 have the design and the driver's protocol), 2026-11-03, the user's
"go" on review 5's step 2 (hub `delver_review_5_2026-11-03.md` section 5). Nothing live changed; nothing is
merged or pushed.

### 87.1 Why

Review 5: the line's value head rates the lines it never plays like the lines it plays (62 of 71
human-flagged mistakes at a 0.000 gap for three generations), the habits humans beat it with are ones
self-play never punishes, and every search- or representation-side lever since review 4 was null. The
cheap untried levers change **which positions the value head sees**: KataGo's side games (branch a share
of the games at a random move into games of their own) and Go-Exploit's start-state archive.

### 87.2 What (zero-core docs/az.md 24)

* **Branched games** (`--selfplay-branch 0.2 --selfplay-branch-moves 3 --selfplay-branch-temp 2.0
  [--selfplay-branch-differ 1]`): 20% of the games each draw a branch point uniformly among their decisions
  (a recording seat's searched decision, not a mana payment); when the game ends, its slot plays the
  branch: 1-3 deviation moves sampled from the network's priors at temperature 2 (one network row each; no
  search, **recorded nowhere** - neither a policy nor a value target), then normal self-play; the branch's
  rows get **its own z**. The game is untouched (its moves, rows and streams) and nothing before the branch
  point is recorded twice. `differ` 1: the first deviation is never the game's own move (87.4: without it
  gen 808 re-plays its own move first in 79% of the branches).
* **Archive starts** (`--selfplay-archive F --selfplay-archive-p 0.1`): 10% of the games start from a
  position of the archive instead of a new deal: the mtg spec's `start` block (section 76) with the
  source game's seed and root actions and `deal` "actual" - every card stays where it is, both hands and
  every card a player knows, and only the library orders nobody knows are dealt again, from the game's own
  seed (a fresh future each time the same spot is played).
* **No masked value targets.** The exploration feature (section 75) masks z := q before its forced
  deviation because there the deviation is inside the game whose outcome those rows get; here no row
  precedes a deviation of its own game (the deviations are recorded nowhere, a branch's rows come after
  them, an archive game's after its start), so every row keeps its real outcome and the shards have no new
  column.
* **Quota.** A branch is one of the generation's 1,600 games (the arms play the same number of games); a
  branch starts mid-game and an archive game at turn 3-15, so the forked arm records ~9% fewer rows and
  searches ~10% fewer decisions a generation (87.4) - fewer training steps (steps = new rows x reuse /
  batch). Raising its `--games` to ~1,760 would match the rows instead (the user's call: 87.7).

### 87.3 The archive: `tools/delver_archive.py`

Every position is replayed on this checkout's engine and checked, or skipped with its reason in the build
report (never dropped silently): **canary** spots (both canary libraries: main's 60, branch `blunders`'s 76,
by id once) - their raw steps replayed and checked by the library's own fingerprint (`spot_sig`), the
single-option steps dropped for the `start` block; **human** Play-tab games (`delver-lab/data/play`) - the
whole game replayed and its end compared with its recorded view (`view.json`: turn, step, active,
priority, life, library and hand counts, the human's hand, every public object with ids, tapped and
counters, the stack), then the first decision of each turn 3-8; **report** positions (`data/reports`),
checked against the report's own view. Every entry is then rebuilt through its `start` block and must equal
the source replay's whole exported state (deal "none"), and start with deal "actual" for the same decider
and fingerprint. `--canary none | half-a | half-b` keeps the canary spots out (or half of them, the other
listed as held out): a run that trains from those spots can no longer be scored on them.

Built for the line's spec (its config.json) at 13:35 on 2026-11-03: **331 entries - 76 canary, 252 human
(turns 3-8 of 52 Play games), 3 report** (entries' sha ac52a7bbf257ce81, 3 s); the smoke used the 13:05
build (321 entries: 76 / 242 / 3, sha a3cd874b0bacada5). **Skipped, listed in the report: 10 of the 62 Play
games** - 4 that do not replay on this engine (20261102-081857-df381d, -083313-639f05, -085829-5c5023,

## 88. The game's evaluation cache (zero-core `feat/eval-cache`, run setting `eval_cache`, opt-in)

**Why** (2026-11-03, the user's question whether "functionally the same" states could share a value): the
main search has no transposition table and no evaluation cache. Measured on r3-2b-float550's self-play
(gen 960, its exact seat, 48 games on the CPU, every row hashed: E:/mtg-zero-scratch/state-dedup/RESULTS.md):
33.8% of the network rows repeat a row the same game sent earlier - root-view value rows 62.6%, leaf rows
19.0%, belief rows 100% - none across games. The source is hidden information (each simulation deals the
opponent a new hand: its option lists differ, so its nodes, while the root decider sees one position: the root
decider's own decisions repeat 34%, the opponent's 3.8%), not permanent order: the permanents put in a
canonical order (cross-references relabelled) add 0.6 points. Equal features always had equal options.

**What** (zero-core docs/search.md 3.12, docs/az.md 25): `--eval-cache N` keeps each game's network answers,
at most N per game in flight, by (evaluator key, network id, 128-bit hash of the row's features and options);
a leaf whose rows are all cached is expanded at once, a root-view leaf sends only the row it misses. Off (0,
the default) the run of before; on, the answers are the network's to the same rows in another batch (float
rounding), games finish in another order (the shared queue's desktop / Mac split and the linger share move
with the throughput). The engine is untouched (digest f6543eb2b1b8752f).

**Measured** (the desktop's RTX 5090 alone after float550's gen 1000, MTG Zero main 37d6574 on the core,
E:/mtg-zero-scratch/state-dedup/gpu_timing.py): the line's self-play seat with gen 1000, 768 games in flight,
sparse batches, token CUDA graphs, two off / on pairs: **10.55 -> 14.15 games/s (+34%)**, 73k -> 99k
simulations/s, 34% of the rows cached; at N 8192 a game's cache filled ~0.3 times.

**Adopting it**: a run picks it up at a re-pin onto a checkout with this core (the Mac's remote checkout
too: a worker of an older core refuses the seat key) and `--eval-cache 8192` (or 16384). Not in the forked-
games A/B (both arms stay as pinned: the throughput moves the data mix); for runs launched after it.

## 89. Where a self-play simulation's thread time goes, and sparse rows without the full-row scans (zero-core `feat/sparse-encode`, no setting)

**Why** (2026-11-04, report 2.3 of the idea review E:/mtg-zero-scratch/fable-ideas/report.md): with the eval
cache (88) the line's self-play evaluator is busy only 62-70 s of a 92-102 s phase, and the arithmetic over
`metrics.jsonl` put a simulation at ~140 us of search-thread time against 21.2's 41 us. The suspects: the
thread count, and the per-row work - each row zeroed, encoded, scanned float by float for its non-zeros
(`LeafBuf::seal`) and scanned again for the cache key (`obs_hash`).

**The profile** (`rowcost`, a Rust micro-benchmark with no network: E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-3/rowcost,
mimalloc as `mtgz._engine`; 15 Delver mirror games searched with the line's seat shape - 64 / 16 simulations,
p_full 0.25, minor 4, a belief deal with mix 0.25 for full searches, a fresh world per simulation - and a
stand-in evaluator, priors 0.85 on the heuristic bot's move (the network's top prior is ~0.87, 68.5), value
0.5; every 16th leaf kept: 10,001 rows, both rows of a root-view leaf; five runs beside the live run, the
spread is the machine's load). Per row: `encode` 13-22 us (p50 of a row's best 8-13 us, p90 21-31 us: a
long tail), `seal` 11-14 us, `obs_hash` 3.0-4.6 us, a cached row's zeroing 1.9-2.3 us; ~252 non-zeros of
37,620 in ~82 of the 587 blocks of 64. The rest of a simulation (the deal, the walk, the engine's steps,
expansion and backup) 14-22 us. At the run's mix (gpu_timing.json, cache 8192: 1.48 rows encoded per
simulation, 0.98 sent and 0.50 answered from the cache) one simulation's measured work was ~50 us: the
walk 28%, `encode` 39%, the scan 22%, the key 9%, the zeroing 2%. So `encode` + scan + key + zeroing was
~72% of it - far above the 15% that would make a sparse path worth building. Not in it: the driver's own
bookkeeping (the cache's map and answer copies, the leaf buffers, the batch assembly, `decide`'s records)
and the group barrier. The 140 us is cycle time x threads / simulations, an upper bound: the isolated GPU
benchmark of 88 (8 threads, cache 8192) ran 99.5k simulations/s with the evaluator 93% busy - at most
80 us a simulation on a quiet machine, the threads not the bottleneck there. The allocator: the run's
build (619f1f2) is mimalloc (`py/src/lib.rs`, `#[global_allocator]`, unconditional; its strings are in the
`.pyd`), so 17's Windows-heap contention does not apply. The chunk locks: a chunk is one job (its mutex
taken once per group dispatch by one thread), the job queue's mutex ~34 times per group cycle at 8 threads
(32 chunks of 12 games a group): nothing to contend; the parallel loss is the group barrier (a group's walk
ends with its slowest chunk), which the thread sweep's `threads_busy` shows.

**What** (zero-core docs/search.md 2.12, docs/az.md 28): `SearchGame::encode_sparse` (default: `encode` into
the zeroed scratch + `game::sparse_scan`, which skips 32-float zero blocks by an OR and takes a block's
non-zero lanes from a bit mask), `lookahead::obs_hash_sparse` (== `obs_hash` of the dense row: the same
cache key), the driver's sparse leaf / root-view / belief rows through them, a cached row's pairs truncated
instead of the scratch zeroed. The same batches byte for byte, so no setting. MTG keeps the default: its
own pair-emitting encoder would save only what is left of the scan (~3 us a row, ~4-5 us a simulation)
at the price of rewriting `encode.rs`'s ~2,000 lines of index arithmetic (overwrites and `max` updates
inside slots), every float of which the digest guards - not worth it now; `encode` itself (the long tail
above) is the larger remaining cost.

**Measured** (2026-11-04, beside the live run: CPU timings inflated by it, compared within one process or
under the same load). Per row, old -> new, interleaved row by row on the 10,001 rows (`rowcost` phase D):
**a sent row 21.0 -> 11.8 us, a cached row 12.4 -> 11.4 us** (the scan 10.7-12.3 -> 3.0-3.9 us, the key
3.0-3.5 -> 0.65-0.88 us); at the run's mix -9.5 us a simulation, -23% of the ~41 us measured in the same
process. The driver (this line's self-play seat with gen 1000 on the CPU, eval_cache 8192, root-view rows,
the belief, sparse batches; 24 games in flight, 2 threads x 2 groups, one seed; the old build, eval-cache
619f1f2, and this one at the same time: E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-3/ab_conc.sh): the search threads' time per
simulation (`busy_s` / sims) **103.4 -> 87.0 us and 93.8 -> 80.8 us (-16%, -14%)**, the same 62,578 rows
sent in the timed window. Byte identity end to end (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-3/digest_ab.py: the same seat,
6 games, answered by a function of each row's non-zeros - torch's CPU floats are not reproducible run to
run): the old and the new build give the same 29,114 batches, samples and results digest for digest, the
same 25,428 cache hits, 14,533 value-only and 536 belief rows. What it buys a run depends on whether its
self-play is thread-bound: the GPU sweep at the gen-1200 stop answers that
(E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-3/bench_threads.sh: threads 8 / 12 / 16 x groups 2 / 3 on the run's build, and
8 x 2 with the run's per-batch sample handling and dense float16 shard writes on the caller thread, ~9 GB a
generation, which gpu_timing.py left out - the other candidate for the GPU's idle third).

**Checks.** `engine/tests/az.rs::encode_sparse_is_the_rows_non_zeros_with_the_same_key` (1,642 rows of cube
and Delver mirror states, both viewers: the pairs are `encode`'s non-zero bits in index order, the scratch
zeroed again, `obs_hash_sparse` == `obs_hash`; the guard any MTG override must pass); `rowcost` phase D (the
same on 10,001 search-leaf rows); zero-core's cargo test 114 and pytest -k "sparse or cache"; the re-pin
gate on this commit (`python tools/gate.py repin --expect-digest f6543eb2b1b8752f --spec delver --preset
delver-mirror --no-mac`) on 79a3e27: PASSED in 207 s - the build, the digest f6543eb2b1b8752f (= main's), the
1-config search smoke on the Delver spec (0/1 failed); the Mac step skipped.

## 90. The optin-core gate's build-only step built no game: smoke_all.sh from the gated worktree's submodule (2026-11-04)

Branch `fix/gate-smoke-games` (from main e098aff); zero-core branch `fix/smoke-all-games` (7d3dbd8, docs
045ee8d, on aa10733; zero-core docs/az.md 29) - **not pinned here**: the gate fix works with the pinned
aa10733's smoke_all.sh too.

**The bug.** `gate.py optin-core`'s last step, "build-only: the other games" (70.3), ran `bash
third_party/zero-core/tools/smoke_all.sh --with-this-core --build-only` from the checkout under gate and
passed on exit 0. Without `--other-games` it gave no game, and smoke_all's discovery looked only beside its
own checkout: from `<checkout>/third_party/zero-core` that is `<checkout>/third_party/`, where no game lives
(worktree or main checkout alike). It found none, ran the core's cargo test, build and ~12-16 min pytest,
and printed GREEN. (The `--other-games` help even said the default "finds none from a pinning checkout's
third_party/zero-core".) Before 40f5655 (2026-10-30) a given `--other-games` was also split on spaces, so
`C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/...` became path fragments smoke_all skipped silently (one `skip` line each) -
GREEN again.

**Consequence** (every `gates/logs/*optin-core-build-only*` log on the desktop: 18, the last run per commit,
2026-10-29 to 11-04): 12 built all three games (the paths passed with `--other-games`); **6 built none** -
three printed GREEN, so the step passed: the Gumbel gate on bb56855 and b212420 (68: "Glass Road Zero, Caverna Zero and
Kingdom Builder Zero build against the core (GREEN ...)" was not true of that gate - its logs hold six empty
`skip`s and no game build), and 619f1f2 (2026-11-03, `mtg-zero-wt/eval-cache`); the other three (explore
db3bb5a, heavy-decisions 091a62e, e098aff) failed on the core pytest's load flake
`test_cotrain_the_local_driver_is_never_starved` instead (explore's and heavy-decisions' later gates passed
`--other-games`). Main's core today is fine: aa10733 builds Glass Road, Caverna and Kingdom Builder (the
explicit run below, and E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ab-ideas/smoke_build_only.log).

**The fix** (`tools/gate.py`):

* The step names the games itself: `glassroad-zero`, `caverna-zero` and `kingdombuilder-zero` beside this
  repo's MAIN checkout (from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, so it works from any worktree), else beside
  this checkout - all three required, or the gate stops before running anything (exit 2, naming the missing
  repo). `--other-games` paths must exist (exit 2 otherwise).
* Positive evidence: an `ok <game>: build ...` summary line for EVERY game the step names, a `=== <game>:
  worktree ... with zero-core <sha>` line matching this checkout's core pin, and exit 0. GREEN alone is no
  longer a pass.
* `SKIP_CORE=1`: the core's cargo tests are the tier's own "core tests" step, and its pytest is not in the
  tier's recipe - it rode along inside this step, took most of its time and failed it on load flakes (76,
  78 and three of the six runs above). This is a deliberate narrowing: the step now checks only what its
  name says. (91 makes the core pytest a step of the tier itself, "core pytest", with a retry policy for
  `tests/test_remoteplay.py`.)
* Its own `SMOKE_TARGET` (`mtgz-gate-<checkout dir>`, the games' target dirs
  `E:/cargo-target/<game>/mtgz-gate-<checkout dir>`) and `SMOKE_DIR` (`E:/zero-smoke/mtgz-gate-<checkout
  dir>`), and the gate's own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` unset for the step (a `None` step env value now unsets a
  variable), so no game builds into this repo's target dir and two checkouts never share one.
* `--dry-run` prints each step's env overrides too (70.1 said it did; it did not).

zero-core's side (az.md 29): with no game arguments smoke_all now also looks beside the main checkout of a
worktree and, for a submodule, beside the superproject's checkout and its main checkout; finding no game
fails (exit 1, never GREEN) unless `--core-only`; the summary counts the games checked; a missing explicit
path, an unknown option, a non-game directory or a `--with-this-core` submodule that could not be moved to
the core's HEAD fail instead of being skipped.

**Checks** (2026-11-04, IDLE priority, 2 build jobs, CPU only, beside the r3-2b A/B). `tests/test_gate.py`
(4 passed): the checker fails the e098aff output (core steps only), a missing game, a failed build, exit 1
and a build against another core, and passes three ok lines; the default games found beside a fake main
checkout and a missing one refused; the step's argv / env; a `None` env value unsets. zero-core's
`tests/test_smoke_all.py` 5 passed. The old smoke_all (aa10733) from this worktree's submodule,
`SKIP_CORE=1 ... --with-this-core --build-only`: an empty summary and GREEN, exit 0; the new one (7d3dbd8)
finds `C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/{glassroad,caverna,kingdombuilder}-zero` from there (`--dry-run`), and
exits 1 without GREEN when they are hidden (`SMOKE_GAMES_ROOT` pointing nowhere). The step itself through
gate.py's own `build_only_step` / `run_step` / checker (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/gate-fix/gate_step_driver.py,
the submodule at 7d3dbd8): **PASS in 159 s** - Glass Road 41 s, Caverna 43 s, Kingdom Builder 66 s against
7d3dbd8, `games: 3 of 3 checked`, the scratch worktrees removed by smoke_all; with `--other-games` a
