## 91. The gate never passes a check it did not perform: required inputs, named skips, a positive marker for every step, the core's pytest as its own step (2026-11-04)

Branch `fix/gate-no-silent-pass` (from main 38fc995): `tools/gate.py`, `tests/test_gate.py`; zero-core pinned
at 045ee8d (91.7).

**Why.** gate.py promised "positive evidence, not absence of FAILED" (70.1), and 90 fixed one place that
broke the promise (the build-only step that built no game). The review after 90 found more ways a tier
could print GATE PASSED for a check it never made:

1. A skipped step still ended "GATE PASSED": optin-core and search-core without `--baseline-root` skipped
   `check_checkpoint_compat` (the point of those tiers), encoding without `--checkpoint` skipped the
   checkpoint load, engine without `--tested-sha` skipped the Mac recheck. Only the step's own line said so.
2. A digest step without `--expect-digest` / `--expect-digest0` recorded the digest and passed.
3. The build steps, `check_checkpoint_compat` and the Mac steps (the engine tier's Mac `cargo test
   --no-fail-fast` too, which never looked for a "test result:" line) passed on exit 0 alone.
4. The pytest check took the first "N passed" anywhere in the output, and the first "N failed|error".
5. The core's pytest was in no tier's recipe: 90 took it out of the build-only step (`SKIP_CORE=1`), where it
   had ridden along and failed it on load flakes. The user's decision: a labelled step of its own in
   search-core and optin-core.
6. The pinned zero-core (aa10733) smoke_all.sh could report a game built "with zero-core <sha>" when moving
   the game's core had failed (90's caveat).

Scanning gate.py for more found the ones in 91.6.

### 91.1 Required inputs and named opt-outs

| tier | required | opt-out (named in the final line) |
|---|---|---|
| docs | - | - |
| python | - | `--allow-skip build` (the build step is new, 91.6) |
| encoding | `--expect-digest`, `--expect-digest0`, `--checkpoint` | `--record-digest full` / `encoding-free` (91.2), `--allow-skip checkpoint-load` |
| engine | `--expect-digest`, `--expect-digest0`, `--tested-sha` | `--record-digest ...`; `--no-mac` or `--allow-skip mac-recheck` |
| search-core | `--baseline-root` | `--allow-skip checkpoint-compat` |
| optin-core | `--baseline-root` | `--allow-skip checkpoint-compat` |
| repin | `--expect-digest`, `--spec`, `--preset` | none (`--no-mac` skips `mac-eval-checkout`) |

Without a required input gate.py refuses before running anything (exit 2, at `--dry-run` too), naming the
input and its opt-out. An opted-out step is SKIPPED (a record-only digest RECORDED, 91.2) - never PASSED -
in its step line and the report, and the final line names each one:

```
GATE PASSED <tier> <sha> in Ns; report <path>                    (every step on its own positive evidence)
GATE PASSED WITH SKIPS <tier> <sha> in Ns - skipped: <step> (<why>), ...; recorded, not compared:
    digest-full = <digest> (--record-digest); report <path>
GATE PASSED WITH FLAKY RETRIES <tier> <sha> in Ns - flaky, passed on retry: core-pytest: <test>; report <path>
GATE PASSED WITH SKIPS AND FLAKY RETRIES ...
GATE FAILED <tier> <sha> in Ns - <step>: <reason>; not run: <steps>; report <path>
```

Exit status 0 for every GATE PASSED form: an opt-out is the caller's explicit choice (`--no-mac` on the
A/B's re-pins is the usual one), and the final line, the step and the report (`clean: false`, `skipped`,
`recorded`, `flaky`) say what was not checked; 1 for GATE FAILED; 2 for a refusal. `--dry-run` prints each
step's positive evidence ("passes on: ...") and ends with the line a pass would print ("on success: GATE
PASSED WITH SKIPS - skipped: ...").

Also refused: an option the tier does not use (it was ignored silently - `--expect-digest0` on repin,
`--checkpoint` on optin-core - and the check it names did not run); an `--allow-skip` whose input was given
too, or naming a step the tier cannot skip; `--record-digest X` together with X's expected value; a
`--checkpoint` that does not exist; a digest that is not 16 hex digits.

A conditional step whose condition is false is not a skip: the engine tier's Mac recheck when
`--tested-sha` is this commit, or differs from it only outside `engine/` and `card_ir/`, is "N/A (not
needed: <why>)" in its step line and the report, and the final line stays GATE PASSED. Without
`--tested-sha` (with `--no-mac` / `--allow-skip mac-recheck`) it is a skip: whether it was needed was never
decided.

### 91.2 Digests

The tiers whose digest step is a comparison require the expected value: encoding and engine both digests,
repin the full one (as before). `--record-digest full|encoding-free` (encoding, engine) records a digest
without comparing it; the step is RECORDED, never PASSED, and the final line says "recorded, not compared:
digest-full = <d> (--record-digest)". (The full digest test also compares with the checkout's own
`engine/tests/data/digests.txt` either way: it fails on a mismatch.)

The digest checker also wants exactly one "N random + M heuristic games in ... s; combined digest <16
hex>" line, over the full 2,000 + 500 games (`DIGEST_RANDOM` / `DIGEST_HEURISTIC` give the digest of fewer
games); no "wrote ...digests.txt" (`DIGEST_WRITE` re-records instead of comparing); and the digest test's
own "test result: ok. 1 passed" line. A caller's `DIGEST_*` no longer reaches any step (91.6): before,
`DIGEST_WRITE=1` in the environment made the full digest step rewrite digests.txt and pass - only
`DIGEST_ENCODING` and `DIGEST_IDS` were dropped.

### 91.3 A positive marker for every step

On top of exit 0:

| step | positive evidence |
|---|---|
| build (`tools/build_py.sh`) | build_engine.sh's last line, `mtgz._engine OK: <file> \| games: [...]`, printed only after it imported the module it installed: the file in THIS checkout's `mtgz/`, at least one game |
| core build (zero-core `tools/build_py.sh`) | `zero._engine OK: <core>/python/zero/_engine.* \| games: [...]` |
| `check_checkpoint_compat` | its result line `{"identical": true, "differences": []}`; an `old:` line for the baseline and a `new:` line for this checkout, each importing its own `mtgz/_engine`; every policy target with samples > 0 on both sides (identical digests of nothing prove nothing) |
| cargo test | "test result:" lines, all ok, 0 failed, more than 0 passed in total; a `--test <name>` step exactly one such line |
| digest | 91.2 |
| pytest (this repo's, the core's) | 91.4 |
| Mac steps | mac.sh's `[mac] <host> <branch> @ <sha9>:` line for THIS commit (it reached the Mac and ran the gated commit), then the step's own: the engine recheck's cargo lines; `--eval-checkout`'s Mac build line under `run-<sha12>/`, `mtgz remote: ... is <sha12>, unchanged, its engine built there` and `eval checkout ready: .../run-<sha12>` |
| build-only (90) | also smoke_all's `games: N of N checked` for exactly the N games named |
| docs | `py_compile: N file(s) compiled` for exactly the N files (the step is now `python -c` over `py_compile.compile(..., doraise=True)`: `-m py_compile` prints nothing) |
| search smoke | `search smoke: 0 failed of N configurations` with N the configurations asked for (any N passed, 0 too) |
| checkpoint-load (h2h) | h2h's final result line (a JSON object, not a `# batch` line - the old regex took the first `"unfinished"` anywhere): 8 games, 0 unfinished |
| run-loop smoke | metrics.jsonl's last row with self-play `games` and `unfinished` both present (a missing `unfinished` read as 0), 0 unfinished, games > 0 (exactly 16 for mtg-smoke / delver-smoke) |

### 91.4 pytest: the final summary line

`parse_pytest_summary` reads the LAST pytest summary line ("1 failed, 301 passed, 3 skipped, 1 warning in
881.28s (0:14:41)", with or without the "=" fill; "no tests ran in ..." too), never the first "N passed"
anywhere (a test's own output can print one). `check_pytest` passes only on 0 failed, 0 errors, N > 0
passed and exit 0; "no tests ran", only skips, no summary line at all (a crash, a timeout) and a non-zero
exit under a clean summary each fail with their own reason.

### 91.5 The core's pytest as its own step, and its flaky policy

search-core and optin-core end with two new steps:

* **core build**: `bash tools/build_py.sh` in `third_party/zero-core` - zero-core's own engine module,
  `python/zero/_engine` (the toy games), which its tests import. search-core's old "zero-core pytest" step
  ran the suite without it: a fresh worktree has no such module, a reused one an old one.
* **core pytest**: `python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider -rfE -W ignore::pytest.PytestWarning
  --basetemp=<dir>` in the core checkout - the way zero-core's AGENTS.md and `smoke_all.sh` run it (its
  conftest puts `python/` on `sys.path`, so `../tests` from `python/` is the same suite). The base temp dir
  is off C: on the desktop like smoke_all's (`E:/zero-smoke/mtgz-gate-<checkout>-pytest/core-<sha12>-<id>`)
  and removed after a pass. CPU only and below normal priority, like every step. Last in the tier: it is the
  longest (12-16 min in 90's gate logs), so the cheaper checks fail first. optin-core's budget goes from ~10
  to ~25 min, search-core's from ~20 to ~35.

**The flaky policy** (zero-core AGENTS.md: `tests/test_remoteplay.py` "times real threads and can fail on
a loaded machine: rerun it alone before you call it a regression"). When the core pytest fails and EVERY
failure is a test in that file - read from the last "short test summary info" block's FAILED / ERROR lines
(hence `-rfE`), whose number must equal the summary line's failed + errors - each failed test is rerun
alone once (`python -m pytest <node id> ...`, its own base temp dir), into the same log. The step passes
only if every one passes alone, and is then recorded as "flaky, passed on retry" in its reason, the report
(`flaky`, the step's `retries`) and the final line ("GATE PASSED WITH FLAKY RETRIES ... flaky, passed on
retry: core-pytest: tests/test_remoteplay.py::<test>"). A failure anywhere else, a collection error (a
path, not a test), a count that does not add up or a retry that fails again fails the step; nothing else is
ever retried.

### 91.6 Other ways a tier could pass without evidence (found scanning gate.py)

* **No build in search-core, optin-core or python.** pytest, the smokes and `check_checkpoint_compat`
  imported whatever `mtgz/_engine.pyd` the checkout had - possibly built from an earlier commit, so
  "identical" could compare the baseline with an old build of itself. Each now starts with the build step
  (91.3), which installs this commit's module (incremental in the gate's per-checkout target dir). The python
  tier may skip it by name (`--allow-skip build`: its changes are Python only), named in the final line.
* **An uncommitted tree was gated under the commit's name**, a zero-core submodule off the pin included
  (`build_py.sh` builds one under a caller's `ZERO_CORE_UNPINNED=1`). gate.py now refuses a checkout whose
  tracked files differ from HEAD (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`: the submodule counts,
  untracked files do not) unless `--allow-dirty` (named in the final line), and a step that changes a tracked
  file fails the gate (a last pseudo-step, "tracked files unchanged by the gate").
* **The caller's environment** could change what a step checks: `DIGEST_*` (91.2), `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` (`-k`
  deselects tests), `PYTHONPATH` (another checkout's modules), `ZERO_CORE_UNPINNED`. None of them reaches a
  step now.
* **The baseline** was passed through unchecked: it must exist, not be this checkout, not be at this commit
  with this core (a vacuous comparison), and have its `mtgz/_engine` built (refused before anything runs,
  instead of failing after the build); its HEAD, pin and engine module (sha256, mtime) go in the report.
  `--baseline-root` is resolved against the caller's directory.
* **repin's `--spec` / `--preset` had defaults** (delver / delver-mirror): a re-pin of another run
  smoke-tested the Delver mirror and passed. Both are required now.
* **The build-only step's core check was skipped** while the submodule was not initialised (the pin was read
  from the submodule's HEAD: None then). It now comes from HEAD's gitlink, always known.
* **`--sha`** accepted any prefix, one character too, and the report kept the prefix; it now needs 7+
  characters, and the report has the full sha.
* Smaller: a step's stdin is closed (a command reading it got gate.py's); a step timeout no longer crashes
  on `TimeoutExpired`'s bytes output; a step never runs above gate.py's own priority (it raised an
  idle-priority caller's children to below normal); `--jobs` defaults to the environment's
  `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` (it overrode it with 4); output is decoded as UTF-8 (was the locale's code page); after a
  failure the report and the final line list the steps not run.

### 91.8 What callers must change

| tier | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| docs | `gate.py docs` | unchanged |
| python | `gate.py python` | unchanged (builds first now; `--allow-skip build` keeps the existing module) |
| encoding | `gate.py encoding --expect-digest D --expect-digest0 D0` (`--checkpoint` optional) | `gate.py encoding --expect-digest D --expect-digest0 D0 --checkpoint <run>/models/iter_N.pt` (or `--allow-skip checkpoint-load`; `--record-digest ...` for a digest without an expected value) |
| engine | `gate.py engine --expect-digest D --expect-digest0 D0` | `gate.py engine --expect-digest D --expect-digest0 D0 --tested-sha <the agent's sha>` (the commit's own when gated directly; or `--no-mac`) |
| search-core | `gate.py search-core` (`--baseline-root` optional) | `gate.py search-core --baseline-root ../merge-main` (or `--allow-skip checkpoint-compat`) |
| optin-core | `gate.py optin-core --baseline-root ../merge-main` | unchanged; ~25 min (build, core build, core pytest added) |
| repin | `gate.py repin --expect-digest f6543eb2b1b8752f --spec delver --preset delver-mirror` | unchanged (`--spec` / `--preset` are required now); with `--no-mac` it ends "GATE PASSED WITH SKIPS ... skipped: mac-eval-checkout (--no-mac)" |

Every tier: a committed checkout (or `--allow-dirty`). A script that greps for "GATE PASSED" should read
the whole line (or the report's `clean`): "GATE PASSED WITH SKIPS" is a pass the caller opted into, not a
clean one.

## 92. Information-set merging in self-play: zero-core `feat/infoset-merge-selfplay` (`selfplay_infoset_merge`, off by default; 2026-11-04)

Branch `feat/infoset-selfplay` (from main a81b59b); zero-core pinned at 62881d7 = main's 045ee8d +
`feat/infoset-merge-build` (70e4c2e the read-only `Tree::shape` split, 5ee4bd3 the merged tree, ef4381a the driver,
bindings, `eval_infoset_merge` and h2h's flags, 176afdf docs: the evaluation build of
E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-4b/) + `feat/infoset-merge-selfplay` (6dbd7f4 merge of main, e815fc4 self-play, 62881d7
docs). Notes: E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-4c/NOTES.md.

**Why.** The evaluation-only paired h2h of the merged search (zero-core docs/az.md 30: one checkpoint of this line on
both sides, the run's evaluation seat, side A merged) came out **+9.3 +- 5.3 Elo over 2,400 paired games**, above
its stop rule's +7: self-play support, then a self-play A/B on the GPU (the main session's).

**What changes here.** Nothing by default. The core adds `selfplay_infoset_merge` (default 0) beside
`eval_infoset_merge` (default 0); off, both give the seats of before key for key and the core's golden records and
matches are unchanged. No crate of this repo changed: the engine digest stays **f6543eb2b1b8752f**. To turn it on for
self-play: `selfplay_infoset_merge 1` with `selfplay_leaf_value_view root` (this line has it); every search of the
self-play seat merges (full 64, fast 16, minor 4); the records ('cq', `cq_prior_w`), the root value q, the value-only
samples' `next_q`, resignation and the moves read the root as before (zero-core docs/search.md 3.16, Self-play).
Remote self-play: the Mac's checkout must have this core - a worker whose hello does not report merging is REFUSED,
killed and retried in 10 minutes, never used. New metrics `selfplay.merge` (links, merged, aliases, growths, shared,
merged_per_leaf; this machine's driver). The leaf's row of the root decider comes from the merged tree's own
encoding of it (`Tree::leaf_obs`: one encode fewer per leaf, the same batches byte for byte).

**Measured on this line** (CPU, the run's self-play seat and driver from gen 1000's config with eval_cache 8192;
E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-4c/throughput.py, throughput.log): per simulation, off -> on (8 configurations of 12 games alternating, 24
games in flight, 2 threads x 2 groups, the gen-1000 network on the CPU, idle priority beside the live run): rows sent
to the network **0.988 -> 1.200 (+21.5%)** - the same 1.49 rows are needed, but the eval cache answers 0.29 instead
of 0.50 (the repeats it answered are merged away) -, value-only rows 0.188 -> 0.317, encodes 1.49 -> 1.77 (+19%; +83%
without the leaf-row reuse), the search threads' time 99.0 -> 140.1 us median (84.9 -> 113.0 min; loaded, noisy),
simulations per wall second 1,008 -> 723 (CPU network). Merged trees: 1.23 links, 0.40 merges, 0.125 growth leaves
and 0.96 shared rows per simulation. Every game finished and every record checked valid (pi a distribution, q in
range, z the result; 607 + 301 value-only records per 12 games merged, 634 + 318 not), the same in every repeat. So
expect a merged generation to take ~20% more evaluator time (GPU-bound) and up to ~+40% search-thread time.

**The self-play A/B** (proposed for the GPU, the main session's): zero-core docs/az.md 30.1 has it in full. As the three-arm A/B
(E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ab-ideas/RESULTS.md): one fork point K, arms in turn on this checkout (off = the line bit for
bit), 40 generations each at 1,600 games, `eval_infoset_merge` 0 in both. Arms: control vs ism (`--selfplay-infoset-
merge 1`). Primary: paired h2h ism@K+40 vs control@K+40, 1,200 paired games, 32 sims, both sides unmerged (what the
network learned), readout at K+20. Secondary: ism merged vs control unmerged (deployable), both merged, the fresh-row
value CE on the control's rows, target h_norm / max_share, `selfplay.merge`, min/gen and the evaluator's busy share,
the blunder suite / fingerprints / canary. Stop rule: K+20 primary < -14 -> stop ism; K+40 primary > +7 -> extend to

< -7 -> drop. Remote self-play only with this core on the Mac (else its workers are refused): the same remote setting
in both arms.

## 93. Self-play's shards on a writer thread: zero-core `feat/shard-writer-thread` (`shard_writer_thread`, off by default; 2026-11-04)

Branch `feat/shard-writer-thread` (from main 9397d67); zero-core pinned at d494da4 = main's 62881d7 +
`feat/shard-writer-thread` (57fd981 the binding, the writer thread, the loop and its tests; d1930c8 a writer that keeps
its rows' non-zeros gets float32 rows; d494da4 docs: zero-core docs/az.md 31, docs/search.md 2.4). Notes and the
bench: E:/mtg-zero-scratch/shard-thread/.

**Why.** The thread benchmark of the Delver line's self-play (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-3/bench_threads_ab.json, the
GPU, gen 1000's seat and driver, 8 threads x 2 groups, 768 games in flight): **13.7 games/s without the run's sample
handling, 10.7 with it** (-22%; the evaluator's busy share 0.92 -> 0.71, the live run's phases ~66-71%). The thread
that feeds the GPU also took every batch's samples (`take_samples`: a dense float32 copy, 37,620 floats a row),
split, tallied and wrote them - 117k rows, ~9 GB of float16 shards a generation, each 65,536-row shard concatenated,
cast, checked and written between two batches. Of the pump's 15.4 s of caller time there, 11.6 s were shard writes
and ~3 s the take's copy.

**What changes here.** Nothing by default: the core adds `shard_writer_thread` (default 0) and `shard_writer_queue_mb`
(default 4096). Off, the loop is the one of before (take_samples, the synchronous ShardWriter, no new metrics key);
no crate of this repo changed - the engine digest stays **f6543eb2b1b8752f**. On (`--shard-writer-thread 1` at a
restart; config.json keeps it): the caller only takes `take_results` and the records (`SearchDriver.take_records`,
moved, not copied), splits them per game and queues them; a writer thread converts them (take_samples' arrays, built
off the GIL; float16 features), tallies them and writes the same shards byte for byte (zero-core docs/az.md 31). The
caller blocks only when 4 GB of records wait (counted). Every shard is on disk before the training reads the window;
PAUSE mid-phase completes the shard being written and leaves no temporary file. This machine's self-play, the shared
queue's accounting, the local linger (its held games keep their records) and the remote's workers (their config's: the
Mac's checkout ignores the setting until it has this core - its shards are the same, written by its old background
writer). New metrics, only when on: `selfplay.shard_writer` (`samples_s` = the caller's seconds in its sample handling,
`waits` / `wait_s` for room, `close_s`, `writer_s`, `queue_peak_mb`), `linger.samples_s`,
`selfplay.remote.shard_writer`; a log line per generation. It changes timing only, but timing decides which games a
rolling / shared quota takes, so it is opt-in.

**With sparse shards** (the parallel `feat/sparse-shards`, its section 32 in zero-core's az.md): the two compose. The
writer thread wraps whichever ShardWriter the phase makes; a writer that keeps its rows' non-zeros (`sparse`) gets the
float32 rows and casts them itself. The branches touch run.py / remoteplay.py in different lines (the shards' meta
there, the writer and the take here); docs/az.md's ends both append a section (31 here, 32 there): a trivial
conflict at the end of the file when both merge.

**Measured here** (CPU only, IDLE priority beside the live run and other jobs; relative numbers): the thread bench with
the 't' configurations (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/shard-thread/bench_threads.py, bench_cpu.log / .json; gen 1000's seat
and driver, the network on the CPU, 48 games in flight, 4 threads x 2 groups, the same 32 games / 2,849 rows / 3
shards of 1,024 rows per configuration, p and t interleaved twice): the caller's sample handling inside the phase
**529 / 442 ms per 1,000 rows synchronously ('p') -> 13 / 8 ms with the writer thread ('t')** - take_samples' copy
alone was 120-160 us a row (take_results + take_records 7-12 us), the shard writes ~0.3-0.4 ms a row; the writer
thread was busy 1.5 / 0.9 s; the queue never filled (peak 20 MB of 4,096). The phase end waits for the last shard
either way (0.1-0.2 s here). Games per second on the CPU are the network's and the load's (0.14-0.21, noise), not this.

**The GPU bench for the main session** (the live run stopped, as for ideas-3's; ~15 min; the plain and 'p'
configurations run this build's unchanged take_samples path, 't' the setting's):

    CONFIGS=8x2,8x2p,8x2t,16x3,16x3p,16x3t bash E:/mtg-zero-scratch/shard-thread/bench_threads.sh

Expected from the per-row costs: 't' at about the plain configuration's games/s (8x2: 13.7, 16x3: 19.6 on gen 1000),
or above it (the plain one still pays take_samples' copy every 64 batches, ~6% of its caller's time); the evaluator's
busy share back to ~0.9. If it is, turn it on at a restart of the line: `--shard-writer-thread 1`.

## 94. Sparse sample shards: zero-core `feat/sparse-shards` (`shard_sparse`, off by default; 2026-11-04)

Branch `feat/sparse-shards` (from main 9397d67); zero-core pinned at 3f830c5 = main 62881d7 + the sparse shards

the shard copies deleted).

**Why.** zero-core's ShardWriter stored each row's features dense as float16: 37,620 floats (75 KB) a row, ~9.6 GB
per generation of the Delver line (iteration 1289: 124,581 local rows in two shards, 9,632 MB) for ~242 non-zeros a
row. The window keeps only the non-zeros (`window_sparse`, zero-core docs/az.md 10.8), so the dense files cost disk
(E: has run short; a forked A/B arm needs ~50 GB of shards of its own), write time on the run's caller thread (part
of the 22% of self-play throughput lost to sample handling, E:/mtg-zero-scratch/ideas-3/bench_threads_ab.json), RAM
(the writer buffers the driver's float32 rows until a shard is full: ~9.5 GB, ~20 GB at the flush) and the Mac's

ones - the samples, window, batches and training are the same, so no fork is needed). Remote self-play: a Mac worker

## 97. Rented GPU boxes (Vast.ai): `tools/vast.py` and the remote `'vast'` (branch `vast`, 2026-11-05)

**Why.** The user asked what it takes to distribute work to a rented Vast.ai GPU, then wanted "the flexibility of
both" ways: (1) a box playing self-play for a run on the desktop, (2) a whole run on a box while the desktop does
other work (the Delver main line stopped at 1610 while the land-hold work had the desktop). Dominion Zero has
complete Vast tooling (`domz/az/vast.py`, `fleet.py`, `gpuhost.py`, `box_guard.py`), but it never moved into
zero-core; mtg-zero had one remote, the hard-wired `'mac'`.

**What.** No crate changed (engine digest stays **f6543eb2b1b8752f**); no zero-core change (pin d499716).

* `tools/vast_provider.py` (domz's Vast client copied at 6048187, without its mock) and `tools/vast_guard.py`
  (domz's deadline guard): the instance's start script writes the guard and runs it before anything else, so a box
  destroys itself at its deadline + 10 min even if the desktop never reaches it (per-instance `CONTAINER_API_KEY`).
* `tools/vast_bootstrap.sh`: apt, rustup 1.95.0 (= the desktop's), pip numpy / psutil / pytest / flask, a CUDA
  matmul check. The image `pytorch/pytorch:2.11.0-cuda12.8-cudnn9-runtime` (= the desktop's torch 2.11.0+cu128)
  has /usr/bin/python 3.12 under PEP 668: pip takes `--break-system-packages --ignore-installed blinker`.
* `tools/vast.py`: `offers`, `rent NAME --hours H` (RTX 5090, >= 16 threads, >= 60 GB RAM, reliability >= 0.98,
  verified, **US/Canada by default** (`--region any`), fast desktop CPUs first, then price; waits for the instance,
  writes a managed `Host mtgz-NAME` block into ~/.ssh/config, confirms the guard), `prep NAME [--checkout DIR]
  [--gate DIGEST]` (push the checkout's commit and zero-core pin to bare repos on the box, worktree
  `~/mtg-zero-wt/run-<sha12>`, build, stamp, `mtgz.az.remote check`; `--gate` runs `gate.py repin` there),
  `status`, `extend`, `ssh`, `destroy NAME | --all`; ledger ~/.config/vastai/mtgz_boxes.json.
* **(1) remote `'vast'`** (`mtgz/az/__init__.py`): a `RunCommitRemote` on host `mtgz-vast` (or `$MTGZ_VAST_HOST`),
  /root, /usr/bin/python, `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1`; self-play: one worker, CUDA, conc 1536, 16 threads x 3 groups,
  sparse. `eval_remote` and `selfplay_remote` resolve separately, so a run can self-play on the box and evaluate on
  the Mac: `--selfplay-remote vast --selfplay-remote-procs 1 --eval-remote mac`. `RunCommitRemote` takes `prepare`
  (the preflight's hint: mac.sh for the Mac, `vast.py prep vast` here). zero-core still takes one self-play remote
  per run.
* **(2) a whole run on a box**: `run-push NAME RUN` (the run stopped; uploads config.json with the box's paths and
  remote settings off, run_state, metrics / evals / logs, elo/, data/ (the window), the last 33 checkpoints + the
  best + opt_latest + index.json, the anchors and held-out shards to /root/runs/_ext; clears an older copy on the box
  first; the desktop copy gets `ON_VAST.json` and a PAUSE file by 'tools/vast.py', so a desktop supervisor started by
  mistake waits instead of forking the run), `run-start NAME RUN [-- args]` (the desktop supervisor's arguments minus
  eval_remote / selfplay_remote / their procs and lingers, paths remapped, + extra args; `supervise.py` detached on the
  box with `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1 MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200`), `run-sync NAME RUN [--loop SEC] [--no-data]` (new and
  changed files by tar over ssh, written to a temporary name and renamed; append-only logs by their new bytes; the
  window's pruning mirrored; never config.json, supervisor_state.json or the control files), `run-ctl
  stop|pause|resume|tail`, `run-home NAME RUN` (marks the run homing so a sync loop ends and waits for it, STOP on the
  box, waits for the run's iteration to end, full pull, restores the desktop's paths and remote settings, removes its
  PAUSE, leaves STOP: relaunch as usual).

**Measured** (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/vast-test/NOTES.md):

* Delver self-play bench (`bench_threads.py`, gen 1000, conc 768, cache 8192) on a 5090 + Ryzen 7950X3D: **~25.4
  games/s**, GPU-bound from 16x3 (evaluator busy 0.93) vs the quiet desktop's 19.6 (~1.3x); 8x2 19.0 vs 13.7.
* A Linux box builds bit-identically: `gate.py repin` passed on three boxes (digest = f6543eb2b1b8752f, the 1-config
  Delver smoke 0/1 failed). Rent to a verified box: ~4-5 min in Texas (build 38-43 s), 11 min in Taiwan (the first
  push of the repo's history alone took 5 min).
* **Distance decides**: Texas ~8-11 MB/s each way (scp; run-push 1.74 GB in 160 s, run-sync 508 MB in 60 s); Taiwan
  (160 ms) ~0.1 MB/s - a 7 MB checkpoint took 73 s, the remote's shards missed their phase (iteration "SHORT 96").
  Hence `--region na` by default.
* (1) on a fork of the main line at 1610 (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/vast-test/vt1610), 400 games per generation, the
  desktop at 8 threads beside the land-hold lab: Texas box **326 of 400 games** (8.3 games/s vs the desktop's 4.7),
  2 shards (2.1 MB compressed) back in 2 s, staleness 100% <= 1. Shards are small: ~20 MB for a 2,000-game
  generation.
* (2) the fork pushed to the box, 1613 -> 1627 there in five starts (16x3, 400 games: 12-37 s of self-play a
  generation at ~135k leaves/s; the 1616 / 1624 evaluations ran on the box: anchored Elo 1706 +- 48 at 1616),
  synced live, brought home mid-run (STOP at 1627, the run ended 17 s later), and **resumed on the desktop** at 1628
  with self-play on the box.

**Bugs found by the tests and fixed:** a text-mode pipe on Windows sent the bootstrap with CRLF (bash: "pipefail\r");
`a && b && cmd &` backgrounded the whole list and held the ssh channel until the run ended; `pgrep -f` matched the
`bash -c` running it (now anchored to `python tools/supervise.py`); deleting the PAUSE file while open failed silently
on Windows; a sync pass after run-home overwrote supervisor.log (now the homing marker + waiting for the loop).

**Tests:** `tests/test_vast_tool.py` (6: run arguments for the box, path remapping, ssh-config blocks, the homing
marker, the guard's start script, the remote spec) + `tests/test_mac_remote.py` (11, `RunCommitRemote` changed): 17
passed. Spend: ~$1.00 for the session's boxes (balance $26.30 -> $25.31).

**Using it on the main line.** (1): re-pin the line onto a commit with this branch, `rent vast --hours H`, `prep vast
--checkout <the run's worktree>`, relaunch with `--selfplay-remote vast --selfplay-remote-procs 1` (the Mac then only
evaluates). (2): stop the line (STOP, clean exit), `rent`, `prep --gate f6543eb2b1b8752f`, `run-push`, `run-start`,
`run-sync --loop 120` in the background (the publisher and the blunder sidecar read the desktop mirror), later
`run-home` and `destroy`. Pick boxes with >= 64 GB for the line (desktop peaks ~49 GB) and set `--hours` to the span
plus margin (`extend` moves the deadline; at the deadline the guard stops the run and destroys the box: the desktop
keeps what the last sync pulled).

### 97.1 The Delver main line on a box: 1610 -> 1810 (2026-11-05)

The user had the line (r3-2b-float550) moved onto a box for one span: `rent line --hours 12 --min-ram 88` (7950X3D +
5090, Texas, $0.907/h), `prep line --checkout mtg-zero-wt/run-a99fa6c --gate f6543eb2b1b8752f` (passed on the box),
`run-push` (2.42 GB in 245 s), `run-start ... -- --iters 1810` (the line's own arguments minus the Mac's remotes),
`run-sync --loop 120` on the desktop, and a finish watcher (E:/mtg-zero-scratch/vast-test/line_finish_watch.py: on the
box run's clean exit, `run-home` then `destroy`). Before the push a hard-linked fork of the line at 1610 was frozen
(runs/r3-2b-float550-k1610) for the land-hold A/B, whose control arm was the line itself.

* **Speed**: ~78 s a generation (self-play 2,000 games ~65-85 s, training 11-13 s at 25-27k samples/s - the same
  ~600 steps the desktop trained at 5-7k samples/s while its GPU also played), the Elo evaluation every 8th generation
  ~135-141 s on the box itself: ~93-96 s on average (the desktop with the Mac: ~95-100 s). 200 generations in 5.3 h,
  **~$4.92**. Home at 19:10 (the data window 2.79 GB in 355 s); box destroyed by the watcher.
* **Strength**: anchored Elo block means 1400s 1705, 1500-1609 1697, 1610-1709 1713, 1710-1810 1710 (+-13 each): no
  change from training on the box.
* **Fixed on the way** (main 4bf2db3, 6bea9b4): `tar_fetch` deadlocked (tarfile stops at the end-of-archive marker;
  the record padding after it stayed unread and ssh blocked on the full pipe forever - the mirror stopped at 1640 for
  ~45 min): the stream is read to its end, a transfer is killed after 30 min, a pass never ends the loop. run-home's
  final pull also brought the box's supervisor_state.json (box args, /root/runs/_ext paths) over the desktop's: it is
  never pulled now; the line's desktop args were rebuilt and checked against its logged 04:46 start. The box's
  `log.txt`, written every few seconds, was never pulled under the 20-s settle rule: append-only logs are exempt.
  The loop now runs with `--no-data` for a live run (the window grows ~460 MB a generation against ~7 MB/s; it
  comes home with `run-home`).
* **The Delver AI site** read the desktop copy's guard PAUSE as "paused": the publisher (branch delverai-float,
  8987fc7 + 002a410) reports a run with ON_VAST.json from its mirror - running while the mirror is fresh, "N min
  behind" when the sync is late, stopped only when the fresh mirror's log stops for 30 min.

### 97.2 Any number of self-play workers: zero-core's multi-host self-play (pin 37a0cd0, 2026-11-05)

**Why.** The user asked for "a setup to have any number of workers able to run and contribute simultaneously" (and
how best to use two GPUs, and whether training can be distributed). zero-core took one self-play remote per run.

**Core** (zero-core `feat/multi-remote` 37a0cd0 = d499716 + docs/az.md 34; Python only): `selfplay_remote` is a
comma-separated list - each host its own workers, mirror, checkpoint shipping and fetches on a manager thread of its
own, one shared quota; consumers `<name>/w<k>`, `selfplay.remotes` per host in the metrics. A name `prefix:arg` calls
the package's callable remote `prefix:` with `arg`. The run dir's `selfplay_remotes` file (one name per line) replaces
the setting's list and is re-read at every iteration's start: a listed host joins (resolved on a thread, retried if it
fails, never stopping the run), an unlisted one leaves at a phase start (its unaccepted games are dropped, nothing
double-counted); the file alone turns remote self-play on if present at the run's start. `selfplay_local` 0: this
machine plays no games while a worker takes work (trains only - an asynchronous actor / learner split) and plays the
quota itself when none does. One name, no file and selfplay_local 1 behave exactly as before (the agent's comparison
against d499716: metrics key paths, log lines, shards and checkpoints identical).

**mtg-zero** (d662940): remotes `vast:<box>` (any rented box: alias mtgz-<box>, its prepared checkout of the run's
commit; `vast_remote`) and `gpu:<N>` (`LocalGpuRemote`: GPU N of this machine, a worker process in the run's own
stamped checkout, workdir ~/mtgz-gpu<N>, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=N` - a box with two GPUs: the run trains on GPU 0).
`tools/vast.py`: `rent a b c`, `prep a b c` (in parallel, logs ~/.config/vastai/prep-<box>.log), `link TRAINER
WORKERS` (the trainer box's own key into the workers' authorized_keys, their aliases into its ssh config; the desktop's
key never goes to a box), `workers RUN show|set|add|remove|clear` (the run's selfplay_remotes file, on its box while
the run lives there), `--gpus N`; run-sync never pulls the workers file.

**Using it.** Trainer on a box with N workers: `rent t w1 w2`, `prep t w1 w2 --checkout <run worktree>`, `link t w1
w2`, `run-push t RUN`, `workers RUN set vast:w1 vast:w2`, `run-start t RUN -- --selfplay-local 0 ...`; add a box later
with `rent w3`, `prep w3`, `link t w3`, `workers RUN add vast:w3` (from the next generation); drop one with `workers RUN
remove vast:w3`, wait for its `removed` log line, `destroy w3`. A 2-GPU box: `rent t --gpus 2 --min-cores 32`,
`workers RUN set gpu:1`.

**Expected** (not measured yet): self-play ~25 games/s a 5090 box, training ~12 s a generation; with the trainer only
training, a generation takes about max(2,000 games / the workers' rate, training) + overhead: ~40-45 s with 2 workers,
~20-25 s with 4 (vs ~95 s on one box), at about the same cost per generation. Data-parallel training across boxes is
not worth it (a step's gradients ~7 MB x ~600 steps = ~4 GB a generation at ~8 MB/s); inside one 2-GPU box it would
save ~5 s of ~12.

## 99. Edge of Eternities sealed: the set's cards in the engine (branch `eoe-base`, 2026-11-07)

**Why.** The user's next project (DESIGN.md 9): a network that builds the best 40-card deck from a
sealed pool, practised on Edge of Eternities (EoE), whose 17lands sealed data (9,765 best-of-one
pools, 56,256 games; 903 best-of-three pools) is the yardstick, never a training signal. The first
step is every card an EoE play booster can hold, in the Rust engine.

### 99.1 The import

* **The IR.** mtg-bot main 2cb79f77, `cards export-ir --pool cube legacy eoe --out data/cards`:
  one schema over the three pools (`70c85fff4b77...`, was `181ba4b8a1e7...`: 188 more classes,
  most used by EoE cards only). `powerlsv.ir.json` and `legacy.ir.json` are the previous files
  card for card (identical apart from `schema_sha256`). mtg-bot's `eoe` pool is four Scryfall dumps
  (Edge of Eternities, Stellar Sights, the EoE Special Guests, Duskmourn);
  `tools/codegen/filter_eoe_ir.py` keeps the first three and the basic lands: `data/cards/eoe.ir.json`
  holds 320 cards, the set's 316 nonbasic cards (the 17lands sealed card list, the same 316) but
  Paradox Haze (no IR: mtg-bot's parser leaves it out), and the five basics.
  `card_ir/src/generated.rs` regenerated.
* **One match was exhaustive** over an IR enum (`lower/statics.rs::lower_pt_formula`, `PTFormula`):
  it gained the catch-all every other lowering has (`unsupported("PTFormula:<class>")`).
* **`CardDb::eoe()`**: the set's own card table (the set's cards, then their tokens and faces), as
  `constructed()` is the Delver mirror's. Nothing of the cube sees it, and it holds no cube
  definition: the 20 cards the set shares with the cube are lowered from the set's export (the same
  parser, the same IR). Unlike `constructed()`, unsupported cards are allowed while the port is
  under way.
* **The support report** (`engine/tests/support.rs::eoe_support_report`;
  `cargo test --release -p engine --test support eoe -- --nocapture`; `SUPPORT_DUMP` /
  `SUPPORT_LIST` as for the cube): **93 of 320 supported** (88 nonbasic cards and the basics); 227
  blocked, 141 of them by one feature alone; 232 distinct blocking features.
  `SUPPORTED_EOE_BASE` holds the 93; one list per lane (99.2-99.5) keeps the four branches off each
  other's lines.
* **IR defect 20** (docs/ir_defects.md): the parser drops Station from the five planets and The
  Eternity Elevator. The planets then lowered as plain taplands, "supported": they are blocked
  through `lower::IR_DEFECTS` (98 -> 93). Lane B audits the other base cards.
* **`FUZZ_POOL=eoe`** (`engine/tests/fuzz.rs`): random 40-card decks (17 lands, 23 spells) of the
  EoE table's supported cards; games only (sealed matches come with milestone S2). 2,000 games
  passed on the 93 base cards. Each lane runs it over its own cards.
* **Unchanged:** the cube's IR, support (546 / 546) and behaviour digests; no layout, encoding,
  zero-core or Python change.

### 99.2-99.5 The four lanes (parallel branches from `eoe-base`)

Every blocking feature belongs to exactly one lane (the feature -> lane table is
`docs/eoe_lanes.md`). A lane implements only its own features, ports the cards whose blockers are
all its own, and tests a feature whose cards also need another lane's feature with custom IR test
cards (`tests/common`). The 53 cards that need features of two or more lanes are finished after the
merge (99.6).

| Lane | Branch | Features | Cards within the lane | Theme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (99.2) | `eoe-a-station` | 66 | 47 | Station, Spacecraft, counters, artifacts, Equipment, Auras |
| B (99.3) | `eoe-b-lands` | 33 | 38 | lands, mana abilities, Lander tokens; audit of the 93 base cards |
| C (99.4) | `eoe-c-void` | 57 | 40 | void, warp, spells cast this turn, cost reductions, graveyard / exile / library / hand |
| D (99.5) | `eoe-d-combat` | 76 | 44 | creatures, combat, removal, damage, life, tokens, pumps |

Each lane appends its own subsection here (99.2 lane A, 99.3 lane B, 99.4 lane C, 99.5 lane D).

### 99.6 After the lanes (maintainer)

Merge order B, A, C, D (B's base audit first; C finished before A and merged second). Then the cross-lane cards, the IR defects the lanes
list (one mtg-bot batch and one re-export, so the schema changes once), and the 20k fuzz over the
EoE table.

### 99.2 Lane A: Station, Spacecraft, counters, artifacts, Equipment, Auras (branch `eoe-a-station`)

**Why.** Lane A of the port (99.2-99.5): the set's headline mechanic, station (CR 702.184, 722:
21 Spacecraft and the five planets), and the counter, artifact, Equipment and Aura cards. Lane A
owned 66 blocking features and 47 cards whose blockers were all its own (docs/eoe_lanes.md).

**Station** (`lower/eoe_a.rs::station`, from `station_threshold` / `stationed_keywords`):

* The station ability (702.184a): an activated ability, "tap another untapped creature you
  control" (`Cost::tap_untapped`, so summoning sickness doesn't matter, 302.6), sorcery speed,
  putting charge counters equal to the tapped creature's power on the source
  (`Ext::PutCounters { on: Source, n: Amount::TappedPower }`). The cost notes the tapped creature
  on the stack item (`StackItem::noted`); `Amount::TappedPower` reads its power as the ability
  resolves, or as it last existed (608.2h), both per the set's rulings; negative power puts
  nothing (107.1b). A station card has it at all times (722.4), appended after its printed
  activated abilities.
* The striation of `station_threshold` (722.2a-b): a static ability of the permanent itself,
  "as long as it has N or more charge counters", with the stationed keywords and, when the card
  has a power/toughness box, "is a creature with base power and toughness P/T in addition to its
  other types" (`Mod::Types` + `Mod::SetPt`, Kaito's machinery: layer 4 through `own_type_mods`,
  layer 7b with the permanent's timestamp). The card's definition has no power or toughness
  (722.2c: none in any other zone, nor below the threshold); a later "becomes a 2/2" effect wins
  layer 7b by timestamp (the ruling on station and Synthesizer Labship).
* The "N+ |" abilities (`tier_threshold`; `lower_trigger_tiered`, `lower_static_tiered`,
  `lower_activated_tiered`): the permanent has them while it has N charge counters. A triggered
  one triggers only then (`TrigPred::State(Cond::SourceCountersIn)`, checked as the event happens,
  not on resolution, 113.7a); a static one carries the condition (`Cond::All` with its own); an
  activated one (a mana ability too) is an "activate only if" that reads the source
  (`Cond::SourceCountersIn` now evaluates from an ability's source in `cond_holds_from`; it was a
  static's own condition only).
* A land with station (the planets: no power/toughness box, CR 722.1) works the same; tested with
  a custom IR planet (a 3+ activated ability and a 5+ mana ability that pays a spell). The planets
  stay blocked by docs/ir_defects.md 20 until the IR carries their station.
* Engine fixes found on the way: a non-mana ability's "tap an untapped <permanent>" cost with no
  mana may tap a creature with a mana ability (`cost_payable_with`; the mana-ability path keeps the
  old count, so Urza's activation offers don't change: applied there too, it changed 12 of the
  2,500 digest games, Urza's "tap an untapped artifact you control: add {U}" offered at priority
  with only mana artifacts untapped, which the rules allow; left for the maintainer, since this
  lane must not change the cube); and layers' own-type pass read the
  condition of every self-static, so a "this gets +1/+1 as long as you control an artifact" static
  (its condition counts permanents by type, asking for its own types again) recursed forever once a
  Spacecraft on the battlefield made the pass run (the EoE fuzz's stack overflow): only the
  conditions of statics that change types are read now.

**Auras that enchant a permanent** (`aura_enchant_type` creature / artifact, `aura_yours_only`;
`lower/eoe_a.rs::aura_enchant`, `resolve_eoe_a.rs::{aura_enchants, bad_aura}`): the Aura spell
targets what it may enchant (303.4a) and enters attached (608.3c, the existing `aura_spell` path);
704.5m puts it into its owner's graveyard when it is attached to nothing, to an object it can't
enchant (its enchant filter with its controller as "you", protection, 702.16c), or is a creature
(303.4d); put onto the battlefield without being cast (Rescue Skiff), its controller chooses a
permanent to enchant as it enters (a `ChoosePermanent`), or it stays where it is (303.4f-g;
Animate Dead's graveyard choice unchanged). "Enchanted creature gets ..." is the IR's
`equipment_bonuses` on an Aura (Scope::Equipped: the attached host); `TriggerPredicate:IsHost`;
"enchanted permanent has ward {n}" (a granted ward trigger, only for an Aura enchanting a permanent
you control, whose controller then controls the ability, 303.4e).

**Effects and predicates** (`lower/eoe_a.rs::lower_effect_eoe_a`; new instructions in
`program::EoeA`, run by `resolve_eoe_a.rs`): exile all creatures and Spacecraft / all artifacts with
mana value n or less (`ExileAll`); search for an Equipment to the battlefield (may fail, 701.19b);
3 damage or 5 with a Spacecraft (checked as it resolves); damage equal to your artifacts; n charge
counters on a Spacecraft or Planet you control; the owner's choice of top or bottom of the library
(`EoeA::OwnerPutsTopOrBottom`, the owner decides); destroy an artifact or tapped creature / an
artifact, enchantment or flyer; return an artifact card; poison counters for the event's player;
an artifact becoming a 2/2 artifact creature with flying until end of turn (205.1b keeps its
types); an Equipment attaching to target creature you control as it enters, the creature gaining a
keyword until end of turn; surveil X by artifacts (`LookTopN`); "if it has a +1/+1 counter, draw";
`ObjectPredicate:HasCounter`; the "creatures you control with a +1/+1 counter" static scope
(`Filter::HasCounter` in static scopes: counters are no characteristic, nothing recurses);
"gets +X/+0, X the greatest mana value among other artifacts you control" (`Mod::PowerPlusGreatestMv`,
a layer 7c static, not a CDA); "you may sacrifice an artifact. When you do" (603.12,
`SacrificeThenReflexive`); look at five, may reveal a Spacecraft, else a +1/+1 counter
(`EoeA::MarkPile` / `CounterOnSourceUnlessPileShrank`); "destroy it" of an enchanted creature's
trigger (`EoeA::DestroyEventObj`).

**For the cross-lane cards** (99.6), lane A's features they use, each tested on a custom IR card
(`tests/eoe_a_kit`): tap target artifact or creature; pump target artifact or creature; +1/+1
counters and a keyword on target creature you control; "sacrifice an artifact or creature" as an
additional cost; "put its counters on target creature you control" (`EoeA::PutSourceCountersOnTarget`,
last-known counters); the tier abilities and station of the cross-lane Spacecraft (Dawnsire,
Entropic Battlecruiser, Fell Gravship, Infinite Guideline Station, Larval Scoutlander, Pinnacle
Kill-Ship, Sledge-Class Seedship, Specimen Freighter, The Seriema); Auras and `IsHost` (Chorale of the
Void, Pain for All, Hardlight Containment, Atomic Microsizer). After lane A each of those needs only
other lanes' features.

**IR defects** (docs/ir_defects.md 21-30, `lower::IR_DEFECTS` under "Lane A"): 21 "enters with"
counters as an enters trigger (Dockworker Drone, Luxknight Breacher, Blast Zone); 22 Haliya's "one
or more" as once per turn; 23 the white Human Soldier token printed colourless (Honored
Knight-Captain, Rayblade Trooper; Cosmogrand Zenith and Knight Luminary in `SUPPORTED_EOE_BASE` have
it too; lane B's entry 51 is the same defect, found independently: keep one at the merge); 24 Mechan Shieldmate's attack permission as losing defender; 25 Loading
Zone's recipients dropped; 26 The Eternity Elevator's 0/0 (behind entry 20); 27 Nesting Grounds'
"move a counter" narrowed; 28 Meltstrider's Resolve's menace for "can't be blocked by more than one";
29 Tractor Beam's "enchant creature or Spacecraft" and 30 Moonlit Meditation's "enchant artifact or
creature" narrowed to creature.

**Tests.** `tests/cards_eoe_a.rs` (station and the station symbols: CR 702.184a, 722.2a-c, 722.4,
302.6, 608.2h; a land with station), `cards_eoe_a_ships.rs` (the Spacecraft against their Oracle
text), `cards_eoe_a_cards.rs` (the counter, artifact and Equipment cards), `cards_eoe_a_more.rs`
(more cards and the cross-lane effects), `cards_eoe_a_auras.rs` (Auras, Cryoshatter, granted ward),
and their card table `tests/eoe_a_kit` (the EoE table plus lane A's custom cards: never in the fuzz
or digest pools, which `tests/common` feeds).

**Measurements.** EoE support 93 -> 125 of 320 (32 lane A cards; 11 more of lane A's are blocked by
IR defects 20-31). Cube unchanged: 546 / 546, behaviour digests f6543eb2b1b8752f unchanged. Lane A's
56 tests pass; the full engine suite 1,577 passed, 15 ignored, 0 failed. `FUZZ_POOL=eoe
FUZZ_GAMES=20000`: 20,000 games (wins 9,443 / 9,441, 1,116 draws, mean 34.7 turns, 224.0
decisions), and the default `FUZZ_GAMES=20000`: 20,000 games (9,967 / 9,994, 39 draws) and 1,000
matches, all four fuzz tests passed. (The EoE fuzz found the own-type recursion above.)

**Left in lane A, and why.** Of the 47 cards whose blockers were all lane A's, 32 are supported (Atmospheric Greenhouse, Beyond the
Quiet, Cerebral Download, Cryoshatter, Debris Field Crusher, Drill Too Deep, Drix Fatemaker, Dual-Sun
Technique, Emissary Escort, Extinguisher Battleship, Galvanizing Sawship, Illvoi Light Jammer, Invasive
Maneuvers, Lost in Space, Lumen-Class Frigate, Meltstrider Eulogist, Meltstrider's Gear, Pulsar
Squadron Ace, Radiant Strike, Rescue Skiff, Ruinous Rampage, Scour for Scrap, Selfcraft Mechan,

* Robe of Stars (`PhaseOutEquippedCreature`): phasing (CR 702.26), a subsystem of its own (phased-out
  permanents treated as though they don't exist, phasing in during the untap step).
* Mm'menon, the Right Hand: casting artifact spells from the top of the library (a `CastFrom` beside
  Bolas's Citadel's, paying mana), a granted mana ability, and a new spending restriction ("only to
  cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand").
* Steelswarm Operator (`spend_restriction(ArtifactActivation)`): mana spendable only on activated
  abilities of artifact sources: the pool's restricted mana covers spells only (`pay.rs`); lane B
  has the same kind of restriction for lands, best built once after the merge.
* Scout for Survivors (`ReturnUpToNSmallCreaturesFromGraveyardWithCounters`): "up to three target
  creature cards with total mana value 3 or less" is a constraint on the set of targets, which
  `TargetReq` can't say (a new field on every requirement).

Lane A features left on cross-lane cards (99.6): Bioengineered Future's
`grants_etb_counter_per_land_entered_this_turn`, `CloseEncounterEffect`, Dyadrine's
`enters_with_counters_from_x(ManaSpent)` (the mana spent to cast it), Frenzied Baloth's
`grants_creature_spells_uncounterable`, Ragost's Food grants and `sacrifice_food`, the costs
`exile_artifact_from_graveyard` (Rust Harvester), `tap_x_untapped_artifacts_you_control` (Secluded
Starforge) and `remove_plus_one_counter_from_your_creature` (Sunstar Chaplain), Sothera's
`ReanimateOneExiledWithSourceWithCounters`, Tapestry Warden's "stations using its toughness" (702.184c:
needs the tapped creature's last-known toughness, which the engine doesn't keep), The Eternity
Elevator's `AddChargeCounterManaOfChosenColor` (a mana production by the source's counters, behind
IR defect 20), and Blast Zone's two (behind defect 21).
### 99.3 Lane B: lands, mana abilities, Lander tokens; the audit of the base cards (branch `eoe-b-lands`)

**Why.** Lane B's 33 features (docs/eoe_lanes.md) and the audit of `SUPPORTED_EOE_BASE`: the 93
cards the import supported had never been read against their Oracle text, and the import had
already found one silent drop (docs/ir_defects.md 20).

**The audit of the base cards.** A script compared each card's IR (`data/cards/eoe.ir.json`) with
its Scryfall object field by field: mana cost, card types, subtypes, supertypes, power and
toughness, loyalty, the evergreen keywords, and for lands the colours of every "Add" against
`produces` and the mana abilities. Every type, cost and body matched; the keyword differences were
all mechanics the IR states elsewhere (warp as `warp_cost`, surveil and mill as effects, ward as
`ward_*`, affinity as a cost reduction, landfall as an enters trigger). Then each card's IR was read
next to its Oracle text, ability by ability, and the 59 cards new to mtg-zero got card tests
(`tests/cards_eoe_b_base.rs`, `cards_eoe_b_base2.rs`: bodies and keywords, warp costs, every
trigger, activated ability, static ability and spell), which found one more defect. Removed from
`SUPPORTED_EOE_BASE` (93 -> 84) and blocked through `lower::IR_DEFECTS`, each an entry of
docs/ir_defects.md:

| Card | What the IR drops or reshapes | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| Blinkmoth Nexus | its animation isn't an artifact ("a 1/1 Blinkmoth artifact creature"): the schema can't say it | 41 |
| Divert Disaster | a hard counter: "unless its controller pays {2}. If they do, you create a Lander token" dropped | 43 |
| Unravel | "If the amount of mana spent ... was less than its mana value, you draw a card" dropped | 44 |
| Xu-Ifit, Osteoharmonist | "It's a Skeleton in addition to its other types and has no abilities" dropped | 45 |
| High Market | "Sacrifice a creature" widened to "another creature or artifact" | 46 |
| Power Depot | "{T}: Add {C}" and Modular 1 dropped; the spend restriction loses "activate abilities of artifacts" | 40, 47 |
| Starfield Shepherd | one search for "a basic Plains card or a creature card with mana value 1 or less" made modal | 48 |
| Knight Luminary, Cosmogrand Zenith | the white Human Soldier token left colourless (found by the card test) | 51 |

Read and kept, with notes: Mm'menon's and Weapons Manufacturing's "an artifact you control enters"
carry an extra `Not(IsSelf)`, and Munitions an invented "Munitions" subtype; neither can be
observed in this table (neither card can be an artifact entering; nothing reads an artifact
subtype). Lightless Evangel's "whenever you sacrifice" is the `is_sacrificed` event of your
permanents, the same thing (CR 701.21a). The cube's own tests cover the 20 nonbasic cards the set
shares with it: `cards_eoe_b_base.rs::the_cards_the_set_shares_with_the_cube_lower_the_same`
confirms the 25 shared cards (basics included) have the same IR printing in both exports, lower to
the same `CardDef` (lowering reads only the printing), and are supported in both tables with the
same characteristics and ability counts.

**`mana_only_from_produces(land without a mana ability)` (18 cards) is an IR defect.** Every one of
them has "{T}: Add {C}." in its Oracle text; 16 have no mana ability in the IR at all and rely on
the Python engine's "any land pays one generic" fallback (mtg-bot's own comment: "pre-existing
printings rely on it for their dropped `{T}: Add {C}.` lines"). Reading the absence as "{T}: Add
{C}" would invent data, and the fallback isn't that ability anyway (no {C} pip, not a mana
ability): docs/ir_defects.md 40 (19 lands, the three with another mana ability included). The other
two (Meteor Crater, Reflecting Pool) had a mana ability the engine didn't lower: done below.

**The Lander.** CR 111.10's predefined token, "{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: Search your library
for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." The 13 `CreateToken`
printings of it in the IR drop the {T} (docs/ir_defects.md 42: observable when a Lander is tapped
by another cost or effect, or made a creature); those cards are blocked. The engine has the rules'
Lander (`lower/eoe_b.rs::LANDER_TOKEN`, lowered like any printing) for the effect classes that make
one without a printing; a custom card with the IR's printing plus {T} lowers to the same token
definition (`the_fixed_ir_lander_printing_is_the_rules_lander`), so the 8 lane-B-only cards among
the 13 are supported once the IR is fixed.

**Features** (`lower/eoe_b.rs`, `resolve_eoe_b.rs`, `Ext::EoeB`; hooks in the catch-alls of the
shared lowerings):

* `SearchLibraryForBasicLandTapped` -> `Op::Search` (basic land, battlefield tapped, may fail: CR
  701.23).
* `CreateLanderAndScheduleSacrifice` (Kav Landseeker: "At the beginning of the end step on your next
  turn, sacrifice that token"): a delayed ability about the token with a new
  `DelayedWhen::YourNextTurnEndStep`; `Delayed` gains `turn` (the turn it was created in; the end
  step of the controller's turn whose number differs). Hashed in the state vector only for this
  timing, so digests are unchanged.
* `DestroyTargetNonlandPermanentWithLanderForController` (Emergency Eject): `Remember`, `Destroy`,
  the Lander for the remembered controller (CR 608.2h), whether or not it was destroyed.
* `DealDamageToTargetCreatureWithExcessLanderRider` (Orbital Plunge): `EoeB::DamageJumpUnlessExcess`,
  excess damage = dealt beyond lethal damage (CR 120.10; 120.6 toughness less damage marked, 702.2c
  deathtouch).
* `SacrificeNLandsYouControl` (Lotus Field) -> `Ext::SacrificeN` (itself allowed, CR 701.21a).
* `TannukEnsignLandfallEffect`: 1 damage to each opponent, then `EoeB::JumpUnlessSecondResolution`
  (the `Game::resolved` count per source object, as `Ext::CounterOrDoubleOnSecond`): the
  draw on the second resolution only.
* `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect`: `EoeB::ExileUntilNonlandMayCastThisTurn` (CR 701.20a, each
  card revealed, a cast permission for this turn).
* `ReturnTargetLandFromGraveyardToHand` (Petrified Field): the `ReturnFromGraveyard` node's lowering.
* Mana: `AddOneManaOfChosenPermanentColor` (Meteor Crater) -> `ManaProd::ColorAmong(permanent)`;
  `AddOneManaFromControlledLandsProductions` (Reflecting Pool) -> new
  `ManaProd::LandsCouldProduce` (CR 106.7: the types the lands' mana abilities would make, costs
  ignored, abilities of the same kind adding none: two Pools alone make nothing);
  `GrantLifeToEachOpponent` inside a mana ability (Grove of the Burnwillows) -> `ManaAbility.opp_life`,
  applied in `activate_mana_costs`.
* `LandsYouControlPT` -> `PtCda::LandsYouControl` (CR 604.3); `PerDifferentlyNamedLand` ->
  `Discount::PerDifferentlyNamedLand` (`Game::differently_named_lands`, nameless permanents not
  counted); `OpponentControlsMoreLandsThanYou` -> `Cond::OpponentControlsMoreLands` (an
  intervening "if").
* `BecomeLandCreatureUEOT.granted_activated_abilities` (Lavaclaw Reaches, Wandering Fumarole):
  latent activated abilities the land has until end of turn (`Mod::GainLatent`, as Urza's Saga);
  `PumpSelfXPowerUEOT` -> `Ext::ApplyPtX` on the source with the ability's X (the "{X} not used"
  guard accepts an effect that reads X); `SwitchSourcePowerToughnessUEOT` -> new `Mod::SwitchPt`,
  layer 7d after counters (CR 613.4d; two switches cancel).
* For IR-blocked or cross-lane cards, on custom IR cards (`tests/eoe_b/mod.rs`): `UntapTargetLand`
  (Deserted Temple), `PutBasicLandFromHandOntoBattlefieldTapped` (Terrain Generator),
  `DestroyTargetNonlandPermanent` (Thaumaton Torpedo), and the Lander printing with {T}.
* `testkit::Game::set_tapped` (test setup only).

**Cards** (`SUPPORTED_EOE_B`, 14): Emergency Eject, Fungal Colossus, Grove of the Burnwillows,
Harmonious Grovestrider, Kav Landseeker, Lavaclaw Reaches, Lotus Field, Meteor Crater, Orbital
Plunge, Petrified Field, Reflecting Pool, Tannuk, Memorial Ensign, Territorial Bruntar, Wandering
Fumarole; each read against its Oracle text and tested (`tests/cards_eoe_b.rs`). EoE support 93 ->
98 (84 base + 14).

**Supported once the IR is fixed** (their only blockers are entries 40 and 42; the features are in):
Beamsaw Prospector, Biomechan Engineer, Dauntless Scrapbot, Galactic Wayfarer, Glacier Godmaw,
Sami's Curiosity, Seedship Agrarian, Sunstar Expansionist (Landers); Bonders' Enclave, Cathedral of
War, Deserted Temple, Terrain Generator ({C} lands).

**Not done, and why:**

* Raging Ravine (`granted_triggered_abilities`): the engine has latent activated abilities but no
  latent triggered ones; a delayed trigger "whenever it attacks this turn" (`TriggerThisTurnFor`)
  is not the creature's own ability (its controller, losing abilities), so it would approximate.
* Eldrazi Temple, Sunken Citadel, Plaza of Heroes (`spend_restriction` ColorlessEldrazi,
  LandActivation, LegendaryPermanentAbility): the pool's restricted mana is built around
  artifact-only {C} (`pay.rs`); new kinds belong with lane A's `ArtifactActivation` after the merge.
* Gene Pollinator (a mana ability costing {T} and tapping another permanent): payment treats a
  card's mana abilities as tapping or sacrificing their source, and "tap an untapped permanent" is
  only a whole cost (`pay::TAP_FOR`); combining both is new payment work.
* Magus of the Moon (`nonbasic_lands_are_mountains`, CR 305.7: layer 4 land types replacing the
  lands' abilities with "{T}: Add {R}"): not started.
* `ManaAbility.cost.mana(more than one mana)`, `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand`,
  `optional_copy_land_from_graveyard`: only IR-blocked cards use them (Cascading Cataracts, Crystal
  Quarry, Thespian's Stage, Echoing Deeps).
* Cross-lane features of lane B not done: `CardPrinting.devour_land_multiplier` (Famished
  Worldsire), `CardPrinting.has_convoke` (Vote Out), `OptionalSacLandOrLanderForBasicLandRamp`
  (Larval Scoutlander), `ReturnTargetCreatureToOwnersHand.allow_nonland_permanent` (Desculpting
  Blast: the node lane D also extends).

**Cross-lane cards** (99.6) needing lane B's part, now in: Thaumaton Torpedo (lane C's
`AttackedWithThisTurn` reduction left), Survey Mechan (lane D's effect left; the discount is in),
the Lander cards Bioengineered Future, Biotech Specialist, Edge Rover, Lithobraking, Scrounge for

their other lane's effect).

**Shared files touched** (additive): `db.rs` (variants `ManaProd::LandsCouldProduce`,
`PtCda::LandsYouControl`, `Discount::PerDifferentlyNamedLand`, `Cond::OpponentControlsMoreLands`,
