##### 13.3: a cost's source, per ability

A cost that tapped, sacrificed, exiled or discarded its source excluded every mana ability of the
source from paying its mana (`activate::mana_exclude`). CR 601.2g-h: the mana abilities come
first, the cost after, so only those that conflict are out. `pay::SelfUse` (from `keep_for`,
`Keep::self_use`) is what the cost takes of its source: it taps it, moves it (sacrifice, exile,
discard), removes counters. `Game::classes_for_self_use` (applied by `can_pay_with`,
`can_pay_without` and the payment's `payment_classes`) leaves out the source's sources that tap
or move it when the cost taps it, that move it when the cost moves it (tapping a land for mana and
then sacrificing it is one payment), and, for a source that removes the same counters, the uses
past what the cost leaves (and, when the cost needs the source, the use whose last counter
sacrifices it); a Pollinator or Lumberjack the cost taps no longer activates. `mana_exclude` now
excludes no ability's source (its callers are unchanged).

Test: `cr_601_2g_a_source_taps_for_mana_then_is_sacrificed_for_its_cost` (B3's Test Cycle Land,
"{T}: Add {G}. {1}, Sacrifice this land: Draw a card", alone; Test Tap Draw Land's "{1}, {T}"
needs another land).

##### 13.16: Black Lotus delved in the payment it helps

A source that sacrifices itself is in the graveyard before delve's cards are exiled (CR 601.2g
before 601.2h); only one-mana ones (Lotus Petal) were delve or graveyard-exile sources.
`pay::delve_source`: any that sacrifices itself with no mana cost of its own (one mana, several,
Wizard's Rockets). `delve_sources` (delve's options, an escape's or "exile n cards from your
graveyard" forced sources) takes them all; `delve_classes` (castability) gives a several-mana one
delve's typeless unit with each production (`Class::delve`; a converter's way carries it, used when
it converts); the payment activates a forced several-mana source first with each production that
leaves the rest payable (asked when several do), and a forced Rockets as a pick of it.

Test: `cr_702_66a_black_lotus_is_delved_in_the_payment_it_helps` (Treasure Cruise with the Lotus,
an Island and three graveyard cards; with two it isn't castable).

`token_count` multiplied a creation and cut it at 64; `CreateTokensN` clamped its number to 64.
Both now make any number, as many as the player's 96 permanents leave room for (the engine limit of

`perm_action` would have to be paged first, A's note in 100.2). `CreateTokensN` with attacking
tokens passes a u8 to `CreateTokensAttacking`: 255 or more make as many as any larger number, the
room being at most 96 (a compile-time assert).

##### The payment's numbers (F7's list, part)

* **Life** (`Keep::life`, `PayMana::life_after`, `PayMana::phyrexian_life`, `db::Cost::life`): u32,
  their sums in u64 (`PayMana::later_life`; `keep.life + phyrexian_life` and `phyrexian_life += 2k`
  could wrap a u8), `budget` and the Phyrexian split compare in i64, and the life paid goes to
  `lose_life` through `i32::try_from` (at most the life total: CR 119.4 was checked). "Pay X life"
  (`x_range`) offers every X up to the life total (255 at most before); `life_later` adds X life
  and Bolas's Citadel's mana value exactly (one of them is 0, CR 107.3b); `with_life` adds with a
  checked add.
* **`ManaCost::total`** is a u32: the u8 sum wrapped, so {250}{R}{R}{R}{R}{R}{R} read as a cost of
  nothing. `mana_value` (of a printed cost) is a u8 by the lowering's bounds (`try_from`).
* **The virtual pool's counts** (`vgroups`, `most_spent`, `singles_vm`, `PayMana::vm`,
  `each_subset`, `masks_of`, `pool_rems`' groups): u32. The pool's and the picks' mana of a type
  together passed a u8 (clamped at 255), and `most_spent`'s spend was cut to a u8 (`k as u8`).
* **Not done** (open, with the design): the u8 parts of a `ManaCost`. X and taxes are added into
  its u8 generic part (`act_mana_x`, `total_mana`, `ManaCost::plus` saturating), and `x_range`,
  `mana_now`'s X and `choose_times` offer no value whose generic part would pass 255. Exact needs
  the generic part (and the pips `plus` adds, multikicker's) widened to u64, `less_generic` and the
  discounts in it, `need_of`'s count from the lowering's bounds, `PermKind::Airbent`'s copy, and
  the encoding's `ctx::COST` read as before. The pool's u8 amounts and a production's (`ManaPool`,
  `[u8; 6]`, `PerPermanent`'s and `SameTypeCounters`' `.min(255)`) are F7's (aborted past them).

#### 100.4.7 B4: the last of mana and payment (branch `eoe-b3-pay`, from 7ae9032)

**Why.** 100.4.6's open list, in the brief's order. Tests: `engine/tests/rules_payment_b.rs`
(section "100.4.7", with a table of its own, `b4_db`: the cube, the shared test cards, Gene
Pollinator and B4's Pollinators of other kinds: a noncreature artifact, a Forest, a Rebel); each
failed before its fix.

##### N23: the actors of shared activations

Gene Pollinator's "{T}, Tap an untapped permanent you control: Add one mana of any color" and Orcish
Lumberjack's "{T}, Sacrifice a Forest: Add three mana" are sources on the permanent tapped or
sacrificed, and the permanent whose ability it is (the actor) is tapped too. One count of
Pollinators (`Class::share`, with `Class::taps`) stood for every actor, and the Lumberjacks shared
the same `Budget::tap`: a "whenever you tap a creature for mana" bonus was a loud failure with
Pollinators of which only some are creatures (`pol_classes`' assertion), no Pollinator got a
land-subtype bonus when it was a land, an actor tapped for its own other mana ability (a Pollinator
given Mm'menon's "{T}: Add {U}", one that is a Forest) or for convoke (a Lumberjack) still
activated, one Lumberjack and two Pollinators allowed one activation in all, a later "tap X
artifacts" with Pollinators of which only some are artifacts was a loud failure (`reserved_n`), and
the Pollinator, Lumberjack or Squandered Resources that activated was the first ready one
(`finish_payment`, `activate_sac_for`), which could be the one a later tap cost needed.

* **Pools** (`Class::pool`, `Class::actors`). The actors are grouped by what their activation is:
  for Pollinators the mana and filter and the bonus their own tap adds (CR 106.12: the permanent
  whose mana ability has {T} is the one tapped for mana, so Badgermole Cub's {G} and Nissa's "Forest"
  {G} follow the actor; `Game::tap_bonus`), for Lumberjacks the productions with that bonus and the
  permanents they may sacrifice (`Game::sac_groups`; a Lumberjack that is a Forest may sacrifice
  itself). Each group of actors that tap is a pool, numbered per `mana_classes` call; its sources
  carry the pool in their id (`Src::g`), so one permanent is a source of each pool that may tap or
  sacrifice it (asked which by its own id, `PayMana::which`, when it stands for several; an
  `LJ_FOR` source with another of its slot on the permanent goes by the permanent's own id too).
  Squandered Resources' kind taps nothing: one source per land, its `actors` the permanents whose
  ability may sacrifice it, no pool.
* **The feasibility** (`pay::PoolCtx`). Each activation of a pool needs one of its actors that
  nothing else taps. Actors alike in their pools and in whether a later "tap X untapped
  <permanents>" needs them (a signature) do the same, so the search counts activations per pool and
  the actors tapped otherwise per signature: a way that taps its card, when the card is an actor
  (its own mana abilities, tapped for a Pollinator's ability, improvise, convoke, Urza's tap, a later
  tap cost's `Way::crew`), takes one from its signature (`Way::sig`); a sacrifice doesn't (the actor
  activates, then is sacrificed: CR 601.2g). A branch with more activations of a pool than actors
  left is cut; a leaf holds when the activations get distinct actors (`PoolCtx::fit`: per pool when
  no actor is in two pools, else a matching, `mana::max_flow`), the fewest reserved ones among them
  coming out of the sacrifice budget (the largest matching into actors not reserved is the most any
  matching of every activation uses: an augmenting path keeps every actor it had). That replaces
  `pol_split`, `reserved_n`'s assertion, `tap_limit` and `Budget::tap`.
* **Its reductions, kept exact.** A Pollinator source on a permanent with another way, or on an
  actor, is left out when each pool's free targets (whose only ways are Pollinator activations, not
  actors, not reserved, not a later tap cost's candidates) number at least the activations still
  possible, the actors left (any such activation moves to an unused free target: the same mana).
  Free targets of one pool only are committed as fixed units up to the pool's idle actors (not
  reserved, no other way that taps them) less the activations counted already: those activations
  take actors nothing else could use (`free_shared` committed up to one count of taps, whatever the
  actors' other ways).
* **The actor, a choice** (CR 602.2b). Right after a shared source is picked (`PayMana::actor_for`),
  the payment asks which of its class's actors activates (`ChoosePermanent`, the actors' own ids):
  those no pick taps whose choice leaves the payment payable with the picks so far and the sources
  still to pick (`actor_options`; one is recorded without a question). The choice is recorded
  (`PayMana::actors`): picks then count the actor as tapped (`used_res`), a reserved one leaves the
  sacrifice budget one fewer (`after_picks`), and `finish_payment` taps it (`activate_sac_for` with
  the actor, its own or granted ability that may sacrifice the land).

Tests: `cr_106_12_the_creature_mana_bonus_follows_the_pollinator_that_taps` (Badgermole Cub, Gene

##### 24.7.5k, 40.1: costs with several parts that take cards

`merge_costs` refused two parts that take permanents or cards in hand (retrace's land discard with
Force of Will's or an evoke Incarnation's "exile a <color> card from your hand", Daze's "return an
Island", Mine Collapse's "sacrifice a Mountain", Bitter Triumph's or Bone Shards' "discard a card"),
because `Game::keep_for` kept one reservation (`Keep::sac`, `discard`, `exile`) and the budget one
count; so retrace wasn't offered with them.

* **`Keep::reserves`** (`pay::Reserve`): every such part, with its card: `Perm` (sacrifice, return,
  remove a counter from; with `true`, "tap X untapped <permanents>", which taps), `Discard(n,
  filter)`, `Exile(filter)`. A filtered discard is one now too (retrace's "a land card"; it wasn't
  kept, by a pool argument: no mana source in hand is a land). One reservation is counted as before
  (`Budget::sac`, `reserved`); several by `pay::ResCtx`: their candidates grouped by the reservations
  each is a candidate of, and a payment holds when, for every set of reservations, the candidates
  of any of them left are at least what they need together (Hall's condition: distinct candidates
  for each; a card discarded is not exiled, a permanent sacrificed not returned). A mana source
  that sacrifices a permanent or exiles a card from hand uses one up (`Game::consumes`, `Way::rsig`):
  the search cuts a branch that breaks the condition and checks it at each leaf; such a source is
  never a fixed unit then. ("Tap X" is paid alone, the lowering's `check_cost_w3`, which `merge_costs`
  keeps: a `ResCtx` never holds one.)
* **Two discards** (`Cost::discard_also`): `merge_costs` adds discards of one filter and keeps two
  filters apart (the unfiltered one is `discard`); `pay_costs` asks the filtered one first.
* **The cost's checks** (`cost_payable_with`) see the parts together (`reserves_ok`: with Grief's
  evoke and one Swamp in hand, retrace isn't offered), and **`pay_costs`** offers only picks that
  leave the later parts their candidates (`cost_picks_ok`: the parts left, the picks so far and this
  one out). A permanent picked to be returned isn't one picked to be sacrificed.
* **A permanent tapped and sacrificed for one cost** (CR 601.2h: the parts in any order): the tap
  choice of "tap n untapped <permanents>" left out the permanents picked to be sacrificed or
  returned, which the feasibility counted (`Keep::taps`); the taps come before the sacrifices and
  returns, so they are offered now. (Not yet when the cost also exiles graveyard cards: its
  sacrifices are made before those are chosen, so that sacrificed cards may be exiled, ruling
  bea302d9, and so before the taps: left open, below.)

##### 13.15: chains of mana abilities with mana costs

`MADE` and `NOT_MADE` were one bit each: the mana of a mana ability with a mana cost paid no such
ability's cost in the same payment (Loot, the Pathfinder's three {R} for Arena of Glory's {R};
one Sunken Ruins' mana for another's {U/B}). CR 605.3a, 602.2b: while paying a cost, mana abilities
may be activated, each one's mana existing once it resolves; so one's mana pays the cost of one
activated after it, never its own or an earlier one's: the "pays the cost of" relation is acyclic.

* **Chain ids** (`mana::chain`, `Tag` bits 16-63; `Tag` is a u64): a `MADE` unit carries the
  activation that made it, a `NOT_MADE` need the one whose cost it is (`pay::chain_id`: the
  source's place among the classes' sources with a mana cost, and its use, for one used several
  times); `fits` lets a `MADE` unit pay a `NOT_MADE` need when its id ranks lower. The picks keep
  them (`PayMana::marked`, `PayMana::made_by`, the virtual pool's kinds, `vgroups`, `pool_rems`),
  the candidates too (`cands`).
* **The order** (`payable_iter`): with such needs and such mana that could pay another's, every
  order of the activations is tried, their ids relabelled by rank; activations alike (the same
  needs and the same mana) keep a fixed order among themselves. Two bounds come first, one
  matching each (`Chains`): with no such mana paying such a cost (the old rule) a payment every
  order allows holds; with every such mana free to pay every such cost (its own too) one that fails
  fails every order. A payment with such costs among its needs is decided by the matching
  (`payable_restricted`: their chain ids part the needs and units into many groups, which
  `best_chosen`'s split of each need over the groups made exponential), and cards alike but for
  their activations' chain ids are one group of `ways_payable`'s search (each copy takes the next
  card's way). (Without these the EoE fuzz ran seven times slower, some games a hundred times:
  seed 1005, 0.4 s before 13.15, over 120 s; now 1.3 s.) A search past `SEARCH_NODES` is a loud
  failure (ENGINE.md 51). `payable_iter`'s counts are u32 and its groups unbounded (a u8
  count saturated, 128 tags and 24 needs were fixed arrays).
* **`UseCap`** (N10) relied on the old rule ("an ability with a mana cost pays only the cost, so it
  is used at most the cost's size times"): such an ability is never cut now.
* **Converge** (`record_converge`): the mana made by such abilities spent is as little as the rest
  of the pool allows (it pays more), whose (`made_by`) every choice, the most colours any shows;
  `most_colors_matching` checks each colour set with `payable_n` (the orders tried). (Its hybrid
  and Phyrexian fallback is 28.8.2k's, workstream D's.)

#### 100.9 C2: permanents entering simultaneously (branch `eoe-c2-together`, from `eoe-base` 2f065ff)

**Why.** W6 found it (99.16, docs/shortcuts.md 99.16.1): the engine put the permanents of one event
onto the battlefield one by one and matched each one's `Enters` event as it arrived, so a newcomer
never saw the newcomers before it enter. CR 603.6a: "Each time an event puts one or more permanents
onto the battlefield, all permanents on the battlefield (including the newcomers) are checked for any
enters-the-battlefield triggers that match the event." Two creatures with "whenever another creature
enters" returned together triggered once instead of twice, and which one triggered depended on the
order the engine moved them. The same order leaked into what applies as a permanent enters (CR
614.12a: only effects that already exist): an earlier newcomer's "enter tapped", Blood Moon or "other
lands" counted for a later one.

**Entries** (`triggers::Entry`, `Game::begin_entering` / `end_entering`, `Task::EntersTogether`).
Every `put_onto_battlefield` is an entry of its own unless it runs inside one; an effect that puts
several permanents onto the battlefield with one instruction opens one entry around them. Each
newcomer's `Enters` event (with its note) is held in the entry (`entered_event`). When the entry ends:

* nothing was queued as its permanents entered: the events are matched at once (`enters_together`),
  in entry order, each against every permanent on the battlefield, the newcomers included; then
  day and night look at the newcomers (702.145c-g come after the event);
* its permanents queued choices as they entered ("as this enters", "enter as a copy", devour,
  Mox Diamond's discard, an Aura's object, the 613.7m timestamp order: CR 614.12, 603.6d, all part
  of the entering event): `Task::EntersTogether` goes under those tasks and matches the events once
  they are done. A copy's event already waited for its copy choice (26.3); now the other newcomers'
  wait with it, so a Clone entering beside Guide of Souls copies first and then sees it enter. A task
  that puts its permanent onto the battlefield later (EnterAura, EnterByDiscardAny) joins the waiting
  entry (`put_onto_battlefield_joining`). Any other entry while one waits is an event of its own.

The events are matched in the entry's event group (603.2c: a "whenever one or more" ability
triggers once for it); `batch_once` keeps later groups' records when an earlier group is matched
afterwards (an entry's task, a 616.1 choice's `release_held`).

**What applies as a permanent enters** (`Game::entry_since`: the entry's first timestamp; permanents
with it or a later one are the entry's, not yet on the battlefield for 614.12a): Containment Priest
(already so, by event group: now by entry), "enter as a copy" choices (26.3, likewise),
`enters_counters_per` (likewise), an opponent's "enter tapped" (Spider-Woman, Stunning Savior;
Archon of Emeria) and the permanent's own "enters tapped unless" condition (the fast lands' rulings:
"it doesn't take those lands into consideration"; read on a copy of the game without the entry's
permanents, `cond_before_entry`), "nonbasic lands are Mountains" as a land enters (`moon_entering`;
`moon_on` for permanents already there is unchanged), Bioengineered Future (neither one entering at
the same time nor the lands of the entry), devour's lands (not one entering at the same time), and
Loading Zone and the counters' putter (W6, `W6State::entering`). `Game::group_ts` is gone.

**The instructions that put several permanents onto the battlefield** (each one entry): token
creation (`create_tokens`, `create_token_copies`, W6's Moonlit Meditation copies; the tokens of one
instruction, doublers included), `FromGraveyard` and `FromGraveyardAs` (several targets), Exhume's
`EachPutFromGraveyard`, Scout for Survivors and Chorale of the Void (`GraveyardTargetsOntoBattlefield`:
attacking ones attacking as they enter, 508.4; the +1/+1 counters after, the next sentence), Parallax
Wave's `LinkedToBattlefieldOwners`, Endless Sands' `LinkedToBattlefieldOwnersMatching`, Ghost
Vacuum's `LinkedCreaturesToBattlefield` (with its counter and as a Spirit), Skyclave Apparition's
`LinkedOwnersCreateMvToken` (each token X/X as it is made), Ocelot Pride's copies
(`CopyTokensEnteredThisTurn`), Nissa's `finish_search_any`, the cards exiled until a permanent leaves
(`release_links`) and until a player becomes the monarch (`set_monarch`). Famished Worldsire's pile
(`PileTo` to the battlefield): the lands are chosen first (`Frame::picked`; they stay in the library,
known to their owner, like the rest of the pile) and put onto the battlefield together when the
choice ends (`pile_to_battlefield`); before, each entered as it was picked.

Found with a temporary counter of entries per instruction over 3,000 default and 2,000 EoE fuzz
games (not committed): every instruction left with two or more entries does them in sequence by the
rules (a draw replaced by a Treasure each time, CR 121.2; an exile whose "until" cards return before
the "return it" that follows, 610.3).

**Leaving together.** The cards exiled until a permanent leaves return immediately after the event it
left in (CR 610.3): in a simultaneous move (`begin_batch`) they now wait for its end
(`Game::releasing`, `end_batch`), then return together, one entry; before, each returned as its
source moved, while the others were still leaving (a returned creature saw them leave). The
instructions that destroy, exile or return to hand several targets (`Op::Destroy`, `Op::Exile`,
`Op::ReturnToHand`) and "exile all ... until this leaves" (`ExileEachUntilSourceLeaves`) are one
simultaneous move (603.10a: each one's leave abilities see the others leave).

**W6's Vocalist.** `W6State::entry_triggers` (a Vocalist entering later in an entry added instances
for its controller's triggers that earlier newcomers caused) is gone: the Vocalist is on the
battlefield as its entry's events are matched, so `w6_entry_triggered` counts it for all of them.

**Left as it was.** A permanent is still moved onto the battlefield before the choices made as it
enters are asked (26.3's model); its entry's events, and the other newcomers', now wait for them, so
no trigger sees the permanent before its choices. An entry that begins while another waits for its
choices is matched first: the one way is a land sacrificed to devour that had exiled cards "until
this leaves the battlefield" (610.3), and no land of the cube or EoE tables does.

#### 100.7 F7: exact numbers, ranges and loops (branch `eoe-f7-numbers`, from `eoe-base` 5f0b07e; `eoe-base` 2f065ff and `eoe-c2-together` merged)

The audit's F7 (docs/faithfulness_audit.md 5.7) and E2 (100.6). Every number the game keeps is
exact or the game ends **aborted**, and no optional loop is cut by a count.

**The aborted terminal** (2cab11d, 6af45fe). `EndReason::Aborted` via `Game::abort(why)`: the
game has no result (`Game::aborted`), its running task finishes and `advance` stops. Every outcome
is set through `Game::end_game`: an aborted game stays aborted, and a game that ended before an
overflow keeps its exact result. An aborted game aborts a best-of-three match
(`MtgAz::match_aborted`). zero-core `feat/aborted-games` e4779b2 (opt-in `SearchGame::aborted`):
the driver ends such a game as not over with no samples, and the search values an aborted terminal
by the network, like a deferred one. Every other zero-core game is unchanged.

**Numbers** (d94e9ed, e658d58; `engine/src/num.rs`). `num::Count` = u64 within `COUNT_MAX` =
i64::MAX; stored amounts i64 (life totals, life gained, marked damage, `Mod::Pt` / `SetPt`, LKI
power and toughness, `Frame::x`, starting life); derived values `num::Wide` = i128 (power and
toughness in layers.rs, `Game::amount`, every sum). Narrowing goes through `Game::exact` /
`exact_count` / `exact_u32` / `exact_u8` (abort out of range), and bookkeeping counts through
`Game::exact_inc` (abort at u32::MAX: timestamps, stack ids, event groups, tokens, spells cast,
cards drawn). Objects: `CardIdx` and `ObjRef::inc` are u32 (`add_card` aborts at `OBJECT_LIMIT`);
`CardIdx` is a `NonZeroU32` holding index + 1, so `Option<CardIdx>` / `Option<ObjRef>` carry no
tag. LKI power and loyalty bookkeeping moved to side lists (`Game::lki_power`, `Game::loyalty`),
which keeps `Obj` at 64 bytes. Mana keeps B's u8 model: `ManaPool::add` reports overflow and
`Game::add_mana` / `finish_payment` / `check_counter_mana` abort past 255 of a type (B4 widens the
cost side, 100.4.7). Fixes found on the way: devour's 65,535 cap, `ExileAll`'s 8-bit per-player
count, "enters not from a graveyard or exile" reading bit 15 wrong with `ENTER_BIG`, the cascade
mana value as u8, the encoding's total power, `KEY_GAME`'s 255 clamp (a loud assert now). Perf on
e658d58 against 5f0b07e: clone 1,279 vs 1,220 ns, determinize 948 vs 830 ns, 7.61 us/decision.

**Ranges** (d301776). `Ext::LookTopN` looks at exactly n cards (it clamped n to 60); the pick
among the pile pages through `Game::ask_paged` over the LIBRARY range, with the decider's list
block showing the page (az/encode.rs `decision_list`; unpaged piles encode as before).
`Pos::FromTop` is u32: "beneath the top X" goes exactly X deep (CR 401.4).

**E2** (2cab11d). A copy effect put on a permanent makes its copiable values single-faced
(`CopyVals::dfc`, CR 707.8a), so a token copy of Shifting Woodland as Outland Liberator can't
transform (701.28c).

##### Loops (CR 732.2a, MTR 4.4): no progress is a stop (0a58c14)

`ACTIVATION_CAP` (31 activations a turn of one permanent's non-mana ability) and `MAY_COPY_CAP`
(31 "may copy this spell" copies a turn) are gone, with `Game::activations` / `may_copies`
(docs/shortcuts.md 29.6.6, 26.11.7). `engine/src/loops.rs` replaces them:

* **Loop actions**: activating a non-mana activated ability of a permanent on the battlefield
  (own or granted; what the activation cap counted), and YES to "may copy this spell". These are
  the engine's only sources of unbounded optional repetition.
* **The rule**: when player p takes a loop action, `Game::loop_taken` records (until the turn
  ends) the loop hash of the state as p's decider sees it, with the action (`LoopAct::Activate
  { place, slot }` / `LoopAct::MayCopy`). The action is not offered to p at a decision whose hash
  equals a recorded one for the same action. The state is then identical to one where p took it,
  so everything reachable by taking it now was reachable then; taking it again can only repeat an
  iteration that made no progress (MTR 4.4). Manual repetition that changes anything is unlimited:
  Grim Monolith untaps as long as lands pay for it, Chain of Smog copies until both hands are
  empty, and Time Vault + Voltaic Key take turns until the turn limit.
* **The loop hash** (`Game::loop_hash`): a fixed hash of the state part of `Game::view_of`
  (factored out as `view_state`; `view_of` = state part + pending decision, unchanged). Its
  properties: it is the same in every world `determinize` deals for that viewer (options stay
  determinize-invariant and reveal nothing hidden), and the public-state gate proves that every
  public field changes it. Canonicalised so a repeated state hashes equal:
  - consecutive passes left out (a loop action sets them to 0, CR 117.3c);
  - every timestamp named by its rank;
  - continuous effects that change nothing left out (+0/+0, CR 613.4c: Lavaclaw Reaches' "{X}:
    +X/+0" with X = 0, the EoE fuzz's seed 1004 that never ended);
  - an object's power and toughness switches read by parity (layer 7d holds only switches and
    each toggles, CR 613.4d: Wandering Fumarole's free "{0}: Switch" is back at its state after
    two).

  It adds what the view leaves out but the rules read: the order of timestamps across kinds, group
  effects' filters, deathtouch damage, waiting/delayed triggers' full events, the LKI of gone
  objects that stack items and frames name, an open simultaneous entry's held Enters events (C2,
  100.9), and for a may-copy the suspended frame (destructured exhaustively, so a new field is a
  compile error) and the rest of the agenda. Nothing else is dropped: a wrong "equal" would prune
  a legal option, while a missed one only lets a loop run longer. A 64-bit collision within one
  turn has probability ~n^2 / 2^65.
* **The board** (the user's decision, 2026-11-09). The EoE fuzz's seeds 1016 and 1024 never ended:
  a player holding priority stacked Wandering Fumarole's "{0}: Switch" and Lavaclaw Reaches' X = 0
  pump in endless new orders, and each longer stack was a new state. The user: tournament rules
  require a player who loops without progressing the board state to choose a different action
  (MTR 4.4), so the loop detection enforces it. The hash reads the state without the stack
  objects loop actions put there (`loops::loop_product`: activated abilities of permanents). So
  holding priority and activating again while the first activation waits is no progress, unless
  the activation changed the board itself (a cost paid: mana, a land tapped, life, a card) or
  something else did (another player's response, a triggered ability, a resolution). Free
  activations stop after one of each a board; paid ones go on while resources are spent (Lavaclaw
  Reaches with X = 1 stacks while lands pay). Digests 3d59118e6fb9e706 (from af00cc85e05ea0c1;
  DIGEST_ENCODING=0 660b3c387f18be70 -> 9bf41c0836e39125): 21 of the 2,000 random games change and
  none of the 500 heuristic games, which matches a rule that only removes a repeated activation of
  the same ability while the board is unchanged.
* **Cost**: computed only when a loop action is taken and at a decision where the decider has a
  record of that action (once per decision). `determinize` keeps the viewer's own records and
  drops another decider's (hashes of views that hold what the viewer doesn't know).
* **Not built: "repeat it N more times"** (the audit's cycle detection + `ask_number`). Exact
  repetition needs a replay of every iteration, CR 732.2b lets each other player shorten a
  proposed shortcut, and the legal range depends on hidden information. The rule above already
  ends every no-progress loop, and manual repetition is exactly what the CR allows.

Tests: engine/tests/rules_loops.rs (10: Basalt Monolith paid by itself loops once, also with an
unused land; Lavaclaw Reaches X = 0, not offered again holding priority (the board is unchanged);
Lavaclaw Reaches X = 1 stacks while lands pay; Fumarole and Lavaclaw stacked for free stop after
one of each, and random play from there ends the turn; Wandering Fumarole, offered after one switch and not after two; Grim Monolith untaps past
31; Time Vault + Voltaic Key to the turn limit; Chain of Smog past 31; the options are the same in
every determinized world). Also: Chain of Smog forever stops after 2 questions, and Zirda +
Basalt Monolith goes past 31.

Digests: 02d4bccc94314d6d -> ab7e8aea0f65b8df (DIGEST_ENCODING=0 856218d6b081056c ->
660b3c387f18be70): 73 of 2,500 games, all random play re-taking a no-progress loop action at a

also inside the heuristic decider's determinized playouts). With C2 merged: full af00cc85e05ea0c1;

#### 100.5 D: the encoding and layout v6 (branch `eoe-d-encoding`, from `eoe-base` 9c67a75)

**Why.** The audit's N2, N3 and F8 (`docs/faithfulness_audit.md` 3, 5.8): the network must see
every public fact the rules use, with no hidden one, and The Dominion Bracelet (CR 722,
controlling another player's turn) was blocked because a controlled decision's action ids are
the controlled player's while its decider was encoded in its own seat (ENGINE.md 99.14, EoE fuzz
seed 12441). Three commits: layout v6 with the gaps and the frame (6049e27), the card
unblocked (787f5be), the graveyard's order by decomposition (593e271).

**Layout v6** (43,956 floats; `mtgz/az/layout_v6.json`, version 6; v5's and v4's files stay). It
is layout v5 with additions only, as v5 was v4's (60.1), so a v5 network widens onto it exactly
and a v4 network too (through v5):

| Block | v5 offset | v5 floats | v6 offset | v6 floats | Added |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| globals, context | 0 | 128 + 256 | 0 | 128 + 256 | (context 248: the frame flag) |
| bags | 384 | 19 x 1024 | 384 | 23 x 1024 | rows 19-22 |
| tops | 19,840 | 6 x 54 | 23,936 | 6 x 54 | |
| my / opponent permanents | 20,164 / 25,668 | 32 x 172 each | 24,260 / 30,532 | 32 x 196 each | status 120-143 (9 used, 15 spare) |
| hand | 31,172 | 16 x 60 | 36,804 | 16 x 60 | |
| stack | 32,132 | 8 x 124 | 37,764 | 8 x 204 | status 72-151 (76 used, 4 spare) |
| triggers, list, graveyard abilities, companions, match | 33,124.. | as v5 | 39,396.. | as v5 | |
| globals v5 | 37,556 | 64 | 43,828 | 64 | |
| globals v6 | | | 43,892 | 64 | per player 24 (6 used), the game's 16 (5 used) |
| **total** | | **37,620** | | **43,956** | +6,336 (bags 4,096, permanents 1,536, stack 640, globals 64) |

The same 11 segments, slot counts, present flags, identities and action ids (the token network's
170 positions); the bags grow at the end; v5's three global blocks are v6's, the fourth is new.
`encode::v5_projection()` is the v6 index of every v5 feature, `v4_to_v5()` the old v4 map and
`v4_projection()` their composition. v5's spare floats (permanent 112-119, stack 64-71, the
globals' 22 + 14) stay unset: everything new is at a v6 position, so the v6 encoding at the
projection IS the v5 encoding, which `DIGEST_ENCODING=v5` proves on every hashed state (below).
A sample is ~88 KB in a shard (float16) instead of ~75 KB (+16.8%).

**What v6 encodes** (the gate's gaps, `public_state::V6_FIXED`, 18 perturbations):

| Fact (perturbation) | Where |
|---|---|
| a creature was cast for its warp cost; regeneration shields; the mana spent to cast it | `perm::WARP_CAST`, `REGEN` / 2, `MANA_SPENT` / 8 |
| a copy is legendary by its exception | `perm::LEGENDARY`: legendary as it is (`supertypes_of`); the code's float 47 stays the copiable definition's |
| granted triggered abilities (no perturbation before: "a permanent gained a triggered ability" added), granted activated abilities | `perm::GRANTED_TRIGGERS` (those a later "loses all abilities" didn't remove, 613.7), `GRANTED_ACTIVATED` (`granted_activated`) |
| a spell's granted alternative cost came from another permanent | the spell's `stack::ALT_GRANTED`, `ALT_GRANTER_SLOT`, `ALT_GRANTER_OPP`; the granter's `perm::GRANTS_ALT` |
| a stack item noted another object | its first noted object (`stack::NOTED_PERM` side and `NOTED_SLOT`, or `NOTED_CARD` / `NOTED_THEIRS` / its identity's 32 digits); the permanent's `perm::NOTED` (items noting it) |
| a stack item targets another exiled card | its first exiled target (`stack::EXILE_TARGET`: present, owner, identity digits), the counts `TARGETS_EXILED`, `NOTED_EXILED`; every exiled target and noted card in bag 19 (`bag::EXILE_REFS`) |
| a permanent is phased out; phased out indirectly | bags 20-21 (`MY_PHASED`, `OPP_PHASED`, by what they are); `g6::PHASED`, `PHASED_INDIRECT` per controller |
| the other player learns a hand card past the 16th | bag 22 (`MY_HAND_KNOWN`: the viewer's hand cards the opponent knows, every one) |
| a player will control the other's next turn; the active player is controlled this turn | `g6::NEXT_TURN_CONTROLLED`, `CONTROLLED` per player, and the frame (below) |
| an artifact entered under a player's control this turn | `g6::ARTIFACT_ENTERED` |
| more life gained this turn (was a Design limit: Haliya reads the amount) | `g6::LIFE_GAINED` / 4 |
| a permanent entered this turn (was a Design limit: two cards read it) | `perm::ENTERED` |
| void holds | `g6::VOID` (`void_active`) |
| the turn goes on with another phase after its combat phases | `g6::AFTER_COMBAT` (one-hot: untap, precombat main, end, another step; none for the postcombat main phase) |

The stack item's exiled references follow the target block's own design (its first two
targets in detail, 22.1): the first exiled target and the first noted object by identity or
slot, all of them in the bag and the counts.

**The frame (N3).** `Game::encoding_seat(viewer)`: the decision's player when `viewer` makes that
player's decision (`decider_of`: it controls them this turn), else `viewer`. `encode_features`
frames everything in that seat ("me": its hand in the hand slots with the legal flags, its
permanents as `MY_PERM` with their `ACTIVATE` flags, its list block, its triggers, its graveyard
abilities, its companion; the globals and match block viewer-first from it) and reads every
piece of knowledge as the viewer's (`knower`: tops, face-down identities, the library bags, the
opponent's hand and clouds, the exile-play bags). The viewer's own hand is then the frame
opponent's hand, known exactly (`OPP_HAND_KNOWN`), its library the frame opponent's unknown pool
(`OPP_HIDDEN`, a multiset it knows); the controlled player's library is `MY_LIBRARY` (open
decklists: its contents follow from the decklist and the controlled hand the controller sees; with
hidden decks, the cards it knows exactly, its clouds and the candidates of what it knows of their
pool: `encode_match`). `ctx::FRAME` (context 248, reserved for this by A0, 100.1) is 1 and
`DECIDER_IS_VIEWER` is "the viewer makes this decision" (`decider_of(player) == viewer`): the
value the network estimates is the viewer's (zero-core's `to_move`, the row's player), the frame's
opposite seat; the network learns that from the flag. The controlled player's own encoding is its
seat, with no options or list (it decides nothing, 722.4). The belief target is the frame
opponent's hand (`aux_target`). In every game without a controlled turn the frame is the viewer's
and nothing changes (the digests).

**What the controller sees (99.14.2 fixed).** `Game::controller_sees(p, c)`: during a turn another
player controls `p`, each hidden card `p` sees is its controller's at once, keyed (`KEY_LOOK`,
private): from `learn` (a look, even at a card `p` knew already), a draw, a card of a looked-at
pile put back where `p` knows it, a found card put into the hand or on top. A later private
rearrangement makes it a cloud for the controller as for any other player. The end-of-transition
sync stays and also shares a looked-at pile named by definition and, while `p` searches their
library (701.19), that library. What `p` merely remembers from before the turn is not shared.
`docs/shortcuts.md` 99.14.2: fixed.

**The Dominion Bracelet** is supported (`SUPPORTED_EOE_EXILE`; the lowering's block removed). Its
W4 tests (4) and W3's (1) run again;
`cr_722_3_a_controlled_decision_is_encoded_in_the_controlled_seat` reads a controlled main phase
back: both viewers framed in P1's seat, the controller's frame flag and decider flag, every legal
`HAND` id a present slot of its card with its legal flag, P1's Bear in `MY_PERM`, the non-decider
without options, and 8 determinized worlds of each viewer encoding identically. The fuzz checks
every `HAND` option against the decider's hand slot (`check_hand_options`, as `LIBRARY` options
against the list since 65.10) and counts the controlled decisions.

**Gap #1, the graveyard's order (593e271).** Priority's casts and plays from the graveyard were
`GRAVEYARD` + the card's position, so an id depended on the order, which the bags don't show. Now
they are one option, `GRAVEYARD` + 0 (`Choice::FromGraveyard`, "cast or play from the
graveyard"), and `Task::GraveyardCast` asks a `ChooseGraveyardCard` over the graveyard list
(65.10's mechanism: `LIBRARY` + the card's slot, the list block holding the graveyard in order
with each card's token and legal flag) whose options are exactly the casts and plays Priority had
(`graveyard_cast_options`); the answer is Priority's (`priority_ask`). A choice in two steps with
nothing between them: rules-equivalent (class 1). The bots judge the expanded options as before
(`priority_expanded`, `graveyard_cast_priority`). While that choice is pending, another player's worlds keep the caster's hand cards its casts count on (its hand mana sources; an alternative cost's or retrace's hand card), as for a face choice (ENGINE.md 71.4: `payment_in_progress`, `exile_filters_in_progress`): `the_bags_show_what_the_viewer_knows_of_the_pool` (best-of-three) found a world of the other player where no cast was left (`ChooseGraveyardCard with no options`). Tests that read Priority's options for a graveyard card use the testkit's `offered()` (the choices with "cast or play from the graveyard" expanded) and `choose`/`has_option` take the two steps; `cr_702_34a_a_cast_from_the_graveyard_is_one_priority_option_then_the_cards_list_token` checks both graveyard orders. The limit is back to `Design` ("graveyards are
bags of identities, 22.2"; the order is in the list block whenever a decision is about graveyard
cards). `public_state_reaches_the_encoding` asserts only `Design` limits: three about what the
opponent knows of the viewer's cards (the information model) and the graveyard's order.

**Adding a gap later** (W2's restricted pool mana and `lands_entered`, A's and W6's new state):

1. The new field is classified `Public` in `public_state::fields` and gets a perturbation
   (made by hand; no draw from the gate's random stream when it applies to one fixed object).
2. If the encoding can't show it yet, a `Limit` with kind `NextLayout` and its reason; the gate
   test's allowlist (`public_state_reaches_the_encoding`) names it.
3. To encode it: a v6 spare float (permanent status 129-143, stack 148-151, `g6` per player
   6-23, the game's 53-63) or, for card identities, the next layout's bag row; never a v5 spare
   (v5's floats must stay what v5 encoded: `DIGEST_ENCODING=v5`) and never a token or action id.
   Name the float in `encode.rs` (`perm::*`, `stack::*`, `g6::*`) citing the CR, write it in
   `encode_features` from the frame's seat and the knower's knowledge, move the perturbation's
   name from `limits()` to `V6_FIXED`, read it back for both viewers (a rare one by hand, as
   `v6_rare_facts_are_encoded`), and re-run the gate and `the_v5_facts_encode_no_hidden_information`
   (which covers `V6_FIXED`).
4. Digests: the full digest changes where the float is set; `DIGEST_ENCODING=0` and
   `DIGEST_ENCODING=v5` must not (a v6 spare float is a layout v6 addition, so the layout and
   `layout_v6.json` are unchanged and every v6 checkpoint loads).

#### 100.5.1 D2: the encoding's final round (branch `eoe-d-encoding`, `eoe-f7-numbers` 33931fc merged)

**Why.** Workstream D's layout v6 (100.5) was held until the other workstreams landed. This round
merges them, encodes the next-layout gaps they added, makes paged decisions show their page, fixes
EoE fuzz seed 10071, and makes the public-state gate independent of the order of its perturbations.

**The merge (34ad053).** `eoe-f7-numbers` 33931fc (`eoe-base` 2f065ff = the EoE port and
faithfulness A0/A/B/B2/C/T/W6/loose ends, with C2 and F7): v6 wins on layout, the base on rules.
Priority's options are A/F7's paged ranges (`EXILE`, `GY_ABILITY`) with gap #1's one "cast or play
from the graveyard" option folded in (`priority_options` = `priority_options_split` with the
graveyard casts as `GRAVEYARD` + 0); the bots judge the first page of the decision as it was
(`priority_decision_split`, through `decision::paged_options`, factored out of `ask_paged_ranges`
unchanged). Two base bugs fixed on the way: `tests/rules_faithful_c2.rs` built a `CardIdx` from a
`u16` (F7 made it a `NonZeroU32`), so the suite didn't compile on 33931fc; and F7's counter-mana
check in `finish_payment` read a picked source's ability from its own definition, which panics for a
granted mana ability (Mm'menon, the Right Hand's "{T}: Add {U}" on a Nutrient Block): it reads it
through `src_ability` as the payment does (fa6c97c; `cards_eoe_w6_granted::cr_613_1f_your_artifacts_
tap_for_blue_to_cast_from_outside_your_hand` failed on 33931fc). `tests/digest.rs` gained
`DIGEST_LINES=<file>` (every game's digest in any mode, to count the games a change alters in the
encoding-free mode).

**The six gaps W2 and W6 added, encoded (f38d6d9).** `public_state_reaches_the_encoding` asserts
only `Design` limits again (the four of 100.5); `V6_FIXED` 18 -> 24.

| Fact (perturbation) | Where |
|---|---|
| mana in a pool restricted beyond the Workshop's (CR 106.6, `Game::pool_restr`) | `g6::POOL_KINDS`: per player, type (W U B R G C) and kind, the amount / 4: 6 x 16 floats. The kind is the restriction as one of the seven a mana ability can have (`lower/activated.rs`: artifact spells, legendary spells, artifact abilities, both, colorless Eldrazi, land abilities, spells cast from outside the hand; any other is refused there, and `encode::pool_kind` panics on one), + 8 with the rider "that spell can't be countered" (8 alone: the rider on unrestricted mana) |
| lands entered this turn (`Game::lands_entered`, Bioengineered Future) | `g6::LANDS_ENTERED` / 4 per player |
| a player created tokens this turn (`W6State::tokens_turn`, Moonlit Meditation) | `g6::TOKENS_CREATED` per player (the rules' own test: the turn number) |
| the mana spent to cast a spell on the stack (Unravel) | `stack::MANA_SPENT` / 8 (148) |
| a copy has an ability by its exception (CR 707.9b, Thespian's Stage) | `perm::KEPT_ABILITY` = (its place + 1) / 8 (its `ACTIVATE` slot), and `g6::KEPT_FROM`, the 32 digits of the card whose ability it is while a permanent has one (a table has one such ability: `add_kept_ability_defs` refuses two) |
| a control effect ends at the end of the turn (CR 613.1b, 613.7, 514.2; `W6State::control`) | `perm::CONTROL_EOT`, the player (1 the frame's, -1 the other) of an "until end of turn" effect that decides the controller until the turn ends; `CONTROL_LASTING`, the player that decides it once those end; on an Aura that says "you control enchanted permanent" `AURA_CONTROL`, its place among them (0.5 later than the lasting one, 1 later than an "until end of turn" one too, 0 overridden for good) |

The control floats are exact for the recorded effects (`Game::w6_control_layers`,
`w6_aura_control_place`): a lasting effect ends only as its permanent leaves, so only the latest
lasting one can decide again; the "until end of turn" ones end together, so only the latest of them
can; an Aura's effect can end at any time, so each Aura carries its place. Without recorded effects
(no card with such an effect in the game), the `Mod::ControlFrom` "until end of turn" effects: the
latest's player and the player before the earliest (each one's end returns the permanent to the
player before it while its player controls it, so with two players the earliest decides). The gate's
control perturbation sets `SEEN_W6_CONTROL`, as a game with such a card has it.

is the item at position w (n - 1) + j, while the stack, waiting-trigger and graveyard-ability blocks

**EoE fuzz seed 10071 (cd412c5).** Anticausal Vestige puts an Aura from the hand onto the
battlefield; `put_onto_battlefield` leaves it in the hand while `Task::EnterAura` asks what it
enchants (chosen as it enters, CR 303.4f), and `determinize` for the other player dealt that hand
slot another card: the refreshed question named a card with nothing to enchant ("ChoosePermanent with
no options"). The card is being put onto the battlefield, a public zone: it is revealed as the
question is queued, so no world deals it away. The other entry tasks (`AsEnters`, `EnterAsCopy`, C2's
`EntersTogether`) run after the card has moved, and `EnterByDiscardAny` moves it out of the hand
first. Test `cards_eoe_d::cr_303_4f_an_aura_put_onto_the_battlefield_from_hand_is_revealed_as_it_enters`
(Tractor Beam; failed first with the seed's panic). Seed 10071 itself passes in release on this branch
and on 33931fc (the games differ by gap #1's decisions); the test pins the mechanism.

##### 28.8.2k: the payer chooses the colours spent

**Why.** docs/shortcuts.md 28.8.2's kept part (the audit's F4): converge and sunburst counted the
most colours the payment's sources could show, so a player couldn't spend fewer, which matters when
more colours hurt (Prismatic Ending on a permanent of its caster's, fewer charge counters), and
hybrid pips with many sources were an upper bound. CR 106.1b: each mana's type is chosen as the mana
ability resolves; 601.2h: the player chooses which mana pays what. The colours spent are those
choices.

**What.** `pay.rs::colour_sets` computes, exactly, every set of colours an exact payment of the
spell's cost by the payment's units can spend (with the colours `fixed` already): for each WUBRG set
m, every unit makes a type of m or colourless, and each colour of m not shown yet is made by some
unit, so the slot it pays (a generic pip or a hybrid pip with that colour; a coloured pip of it
needs it anyway) becomes a pip of that colour, each in turn, and the rest must be an exact payment
(`shows_exactly`, `mana::payable_n`); a payment showing exactly m gives such a choice of slots and
back. The mana costs of mana abilities activated in the payment (`PayMana::marked`) are paid by some
of the units, a multiset of them at a time, and that mana isn't spent on the spell. B4's activations
of abilities with a mana cost (`made_by`) are each of their splits. `record_converge` takes the union:
one set is recorded; several push `Task::ColorsSpent`, which asks the payer right after the payment
(part of casting the spell, nothing between): `DecisionKind::ChooseColorsSpent` (the 48th kind), its
options `NUMBER` + the WUBRG mask of each set (32 ids, every subset: no paging). `Mark::Converge`
holds the set; `converge_of` counts it, so a reader of a colour ("if {R} was spent") finds it. The
heuristic bot spends the most colours (what was counted before). `most_colors_matching`,
`converge_colors` and the hybrid upper bound are gone.

**The encoding.** No layout change: the context block shows the kind (one-hot 47), the asking task
(code 28) and the spell (its card code, `AbilitySlot::Spell`); the options are their sets' ids, legal
by the action mask. The sets depend on public permanents and the pool only, so every world of either
player asks the same (tested).

**Tests** (each failing before): `cards_m7c_tail::cr_106_1b_cr_601_2h_the_caster_chooses_the_colours_spent`
(Prismatic Ending, X = 2, paid by Plains, Tundra and Underground Sea: exactly W U, W B and W U B
offered; W U leaves Coalition Relic, W U B exiles it; determinized worlds ask the same),
`cr_601_2h_one_possible_set_of_colours_asks_nothing` (Plains, Island, Swamp),
`prismatic_ending_counts_the_colours_spent_converge_cr106_1b` (rewritten: the most, chosen),
`cards_m7c_tail3::cr_702_44a_sunburst_counts_the_colours_chosen` (Pentad Prism by Tundra and
Underground Sea: U, W U, W B, U B; blue only, one charge counter), and the unit test
`pay::tests::cr_106_1b_the_colour_sets_a_payment_can_spend` (hybrid pips, colours spent already, a
mana ability's own cost paid by one of the units). docs/shortcuts.md 28.8.2: the kept part **fixed**.
